Assuming an Earth-mantle-like bulk Moon, we demonstrate that additional differentiation processes beyond just core formation are required to further deplete Ni in the LMO, such as the fractional crystallisation of olivine. Even then, it is difficult to deplete Ni to the extent required by the olivine compositions, suggesting perhaps that a further process occurred such as the segregation of iron sulfide in the LMO. Alternatively, the bulk Moon is depleted in Ni relative to bulk silicate Earth, but not other refractory elements, which is difficult to reconcile with our current understanding of the Earth-Moon system.

title: First-principles study of hydrated and hydrolyzed Nd(III) adsorption on kaolinite (001) and 00 1 ¯ surfaces
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Yingzi Xia, Shanqi Liu, Huiquan Tian, Yongbing Li, Shuping Yin, Jianming Liu
abstract: Ion-adsorption deposits (IADs) are important sources of heavy and selected light rare earth elements (REEs), yet the adsorption mechanisms of hydrated and hydrolyzed Nd(III) on clay-mineral surfaces remain incompletely resolved. Structural refinement of adsorbed Nd by extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) is challenging because the Nd L3-edge region is susceptible to interference from nearby Ce and Pr absorption edges. In this study, first-principles calculations were performed to investigate the adsorption of [Nd(H2O)9]3+ and [Nd(OH)(H2O)8]2+ on the (001) and ( 00 1 ¯ ) basal surfaces of kaolinite. Optimized isolated complexes show that nine-coordination represents the saturated first hydration shell of Nd3+. Upon adsorption, [Nd(H2O)9]3+ remains outer-sphere on both basal surfaces. Partial dehydration occurs on the (001) surface, whereas the dehydration behavior on the 00 1 ¯ surface depends on the adsorption geometry. For [Nd(OH)(H2O)8]2+, adsorption remains outer-sphere on the (001) surface without dehydration. On the 00 1 ¯ surface, the adsorption mode of [Nd(OH)(H2O)8]2+ is influenced by the Nd–OOH bond orientation, with a toward-surface orientation leading to partial dehydration and inner-sphere complexation. Electronic-structure analyses reveal localized interfacial charge redistribution on the (001) surface, pronounced Si-O framework polarization on the 00 1 ¯ surface, and more pronounced overlap between Nd-d and surface O-p states in the inner-sphere complex. DFT + U tests for [Nd(H2O)9]3+ indicate no substantial changes in adsorption geometries or net interfacial charge redistribution. These results indicate that Nd hydrolysis, Nd–OOH bond orientation, and basal-surface chemistry jointly influence the adsorption mode of Nd on kaolinite, providing molecular-level constraints on pH-dependent light REE retention in IADs.

title: Turbidite-associated pyritization in deep-sea sediments: Geochemical insights from the Bengal Fan
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Xiangyu Chen, Jingrui Li, Yu Gu, Xin Chang, Xuefa Shi, Shengfa Liu, Xiting Liu
abstract: Marine microbial sulfate reduction (MSR) is the principal process driving authigenic pyrite formation in marine sediments, yet the influence of episodic turbidite deposition on pyritization and early diagenetic sulfur cycling remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated a turbidite-bearing core (BOB-91) and a hemipelagic reference core (BOB-4) from the western Bengal Fan by integrating sedimentological observations, bulk-sediment geochemistry, reactive iron speciation, pyrite sulfur isotopes, and in situ pyrite trace-element analyses. Two turbidite intervals in BOB-91 are distinguished from adjacent hemipelagic sediments by abrupt grain-size coarsening followed by fining-upward trends, prominent XRD peaks of quartz and albite, and higher Fe/Al, Ti/Al, and K/Al ratios. Compared with adjacent hemipelagic sediments, the turbidites contain more nitric-acid-extractable iron (FeHNO3), lower contents of dithionite- and oxalate-extractable iron (FeD and FeO), a modestly higher mean degree of pyritization (DOP = 0.034 versus 0.023), and lower δ34Spy values. These changes are consistent with more efficient conversion of reactive iron into pyrite and larger apparent sulfur-isotope offsets between seawater sulfate and sedimentary pyrite within the turbidites. Turbidite-hosted pyrite is generally enriched in Mg and Mo and depleted in Cr relative to pyrite in adjacent hemipelagic sediments. This trace-element pattern records distinct pyrite-forming conditions within the turbidite intervals, but does not independently resolve the relative contributions of organoclastic sulfate reduction (OSR) and sulfate-driven anaerobic oxidation of methane (SD-AOM). In addition, FeHR/FeT and MoEF/UEF relationships do not indicate a persistent shift toward strongly reducing bottom-water conditions. Taken together, these observations suggest that turbidite deposition reorganized local early diagenetic reaction–transport conditions, rather than causing a sustained change in bottom-water redox state, and was associated with more efficient pyritization. These findings highlight the importance of depositional processes and sedimentary facies in regulating pyrite formation and interpreting sulfur cycling in deep-sea sediments.

title: Determination of ferrous iron in biotite by EPMA using the flank method: development of a mineral-specific calibration
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Shahed Shahrestani, Ioan V. Sanislav, Yang Liu, Kevin Blake, Avish Kumar, Shane Askew
abstract: The oxidation state of iron in biotite provides key information on redox conditions, magma evolution, and fluid–rock interactions in igneous, metamorphic, and hydrothermal systems, yet routine determination of Fe2+ and Fe3+ by electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) remains difficult. This study presents a biotite-specific calibration of the flank method for estimating Fe2+ from Fe Lβ/Lα intensity ratios. Rather than defining flank positions from garnet end-members, as in the conventional approach, flank positions were established directly from biotite spectra, exploiting the comparatively narrow Fe3+/ΣFe range of biotite to achieve more consistent spectral behaviour. Twelve biotite samples spanning a wide range of total iron content (8.29–22.61 wt% ΣFeO) were analysed by EPMA and independently characterised by wet chemistry to calibrate and test the method. A simple linear regression of Fe2+ against Lβ/Lα produced a strong correlation with wet-chemistry values (R2 = 0.95, average error 0.47 wt%), and incorporating total iron (ΣFe) into a multiple regression model improved the prediction of Fe2+/ΣFe, accounting for matrix-dependent effects associated with total Fe concentration. Leave-one-out cross-validation was applied to evaluate the performance of both models, and independent validation against a well-characterised reference biotite (LP-6) yielded Fe2+ estimates within 0.4–0.6 wt% of the reported composition. These results demonstrate that mineral-specific calibration of the flank method, combined with controlled instrumental conditions, offers a practical, and in-situ alternative to Mössbauer spectroscopy or synchrotron XANES for constraining Fe2+/Fe3+ in biotite, with potential application to other Fe-bearing silicates and to broader petrogenetic, ore-deposit, and metamorphic studies in which iron oxidation state provides information on mineral-forming conditions.

title: The Sutrakar trachydacite: volcanology, 40 Ar/ 39 Ar systematics and petrogenesis of a crystal-rich silicic flood lava in the western Deccan Traps, India
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Arunodaya Shekhar, B. Astha, Hetu Sheth, Hijas Hameed, Anmol Naik, Waliur Rahaman, Ghulam Rabbani, Hugo K.H. Olierook, Fred Jourdan, Christopher L. Kirkland
abstract: The 16-km-long Sutrakar flow, in the western Deccan Traps, is a fissure-fed, crystal-rich, silicic flood lava with an original volume > 4.8 km3. It contains abundant phenocrysts and glomerocrysts of plagioclase (andesine), and minor augite and Fe–Ti oxides, in a glass-rich groundmass with oligoclase, anorthoclase and sanidine microlites. Its composition is mainly trachydacite, less commonly rhyolite or trachyte, due to slightly variable phenocryst contents; an altered vitrophyric variety is a dacite. Most samples are metaluminous. Phenocryst cores yield crystallisation temperatures of 1123–1089 °C (± 35 °C, 1σ, clinopyroxene) and 1071–1021 °C (± 12 °C, 1σ, plagioclase) at 1 kbar pressure. Fe-Ti oxides in the vitrophyre and a trachydacite yield T-fO2 conditions on or above the nickel‑nickel oxide buffer, indicating interaction with oxidising fluids. Plagioclase 40Ar/39Ar step-heating spectra for two trachydacites show low-temperature 40Ar* loss and high-temperature excess 40Ar and do not yield a geologically meaningful age; existing geochronological data for the underlying Jawhar Formation basalts indicate the Sutrakar flow to be younger than ∼66.0 Ma. The flow shows enrichments in the light rare earth elements (LaN/LuN = 9.41–14.9), negative Nb-Ta, Sr, Eu, P, Ti anomalies and Pb peaks in multielement patterns, and high (87Sr/86Sr)t ratios (0.71854–0.72814) and very low εNdt values (−21.7 to −23.2). The geochemical data, combined with Magma Chamber Simulator (MCS) and Energy-Constrained Assimilation and Fractional Crystallisation (EC-AFC) modelling, show that the Sutrakar silicic magma originated by advanced fractional crystallisation of Jawhar Formation basalts with ∼20–30% assimilation of ancient granitic basement crust.

title: Redistribution of iron isotopes during serpentinization: Insights from peridotites of Troodos Ophiolite, Cyprus
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Kun Xu, Yanhong Chen, Yaoling Niu, Meng Duan, Xiaohong Wang, Hongmei Gong, Yong Wu
abstract: Serpentinization redistributes iron (Fe) among secondary minerals and drives significant Fe isotope fractionation, yet the role of Fe3+-bearing serpentine in this process remains poorly constrained. We investigated serpentinized harzburgites and dunite from the Troodos Ophiolite, Cyprus, integrating petrography, mineral chemistry, Raman spectroscopy, Fe isotope analyses, and thermodynamic reaction-path modeling. Bulk-rock samples exhibit limited Fe isotope variation (δ56Fe = −0.06 ± 0.03‰ to 0.00 ± 0.03‰, 2SD), indicating that serpentinization has negligible effect on the bulk Fe isotope composition of peridotites. In contrast, serpentine separates display divergent Fe isotope trends relative to coexisting olivine between two protolith types. Serpentine from harzburgites yields δ56Fe values similar to or heavier than coexisting olivine (Δ56FeSrp-Ol = −0.01‰ to +0.10‰, differences exceeding the analytical uncertainty of 0.03‰ for all but one sample), whereas serpentine separated from dunite is slightly lighter than olivine (Δ56FeS rp-Ol = −0.04‰). This contrasting fractionation pattern indicates that Fe isotope redistribution during serpentinization is primarily governed by the assemblage of secondary Fe-bearing minerals and the initial protolith composition. Petrographic observations, mineral compositional data, and thermodynamic modeling collectively constrain the moderate to intense serpentinization of harzburgite to low-temperature (< 200 °C), high water/rock ratio conditions that favor crystallization of Fe3+-bearing lizardite but limited magnetite production. Under this condition, lizardite with preferential incorporation of heavy Fe isotopes results in higher δ56Fe values in serpentines than in olivine. In contrast, secondary sulfides may act as a potential reservoir for light Fe isotopes, consistent with the extremely low δ56Fe value of −1.08 ± 0.02‰ (2SD, measured in one sample). By comparison, magnetite-dominated serpentinization partitions heavy Fe into magnetite, leaving serpentine with comparatively light Fe isotopes. Our findings demonstrate that Fe isotope redistribution during serpentinization depends not only on magnetite formation, as previously recognized, but also on the occurrence of Fe3+-bearing serpentine under low-temperature, high-fluid-flux regimes. Given that serpentine is the primary mineral dominating the Fe budget in these rocks, while sulfides have a negligible effect, Fe3+-bearing serpentine thus constitutes a critical yet underappreciated endmember for global Fe cycling linked to seafloor alteration. Because of unavoidable impurities in mineral separates and the lack of comprehensive data on coexisting sulfide and magnetite, further in-situ Fe isotope and valence state analyses are warranted to provide microscale constraints.

title: Triple oxygen isotope insights into the HIMU source
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): J. Cameron Adams, James W. Dottin, Daniel E. Ibarra, Matthew G. Jackson, Jon Woodhead
abstract: Geochemical analyses of oceanic hotspot lavas exhibit chemical heterogeneity that is interpreted as the expression of a chemically heterogenous mantle that was established through partial melting and crustal recycling. The diversity of mantle sources is often observed among the concentrations and isotopic compositions of trace lithophile and siderophile elements. However, oxygen (O), among the most abundant elements on Earth, exhibits minimal isotopic variability across the full spectrum of geochemical heterogeneity expressed by oceanic hotspot lavas. The homogeneity of O isotopes among ocean island lavas is difficult to reconcile with the proposed proportions of recycled crustal materials and suggests that either not yet constrained magmatic processes or sampling biases are at play. Recent advances in mass spectrometry now allow for the high precision measurement of 17O/16O which, when combined with the traditional measurement of 18O/16O, may provide additional insight into the magmatic processing of O throughout Earth's tectonic history, beyond confirming depleted versus enriched recycled crustal components in plume lavas. This study reports δ18O and Δ′17O (Δ′17O = δ′17O − λ × δ′18O, where λ = 0.528) in olivine and clinopyroxene separated from nine Mangaia basalt samples. Mangaia is an oceanic island (Macdonald hotspot) and a type locality for the high-μ (μ = 238U/204Pb, HIMU) mantle component which offers the opportunity to evaluate the potential advantages of 17O/16O measurements in geochemically extreme plume lavas. The data reveal considerable isotopic variability. The δ18O values range from +2.38‰ to +6.31‰ (± 0.352, 2σ) and Δ′17O values range from −0.041‰ to −0.085‰ (± 0.008, 2σ). Some Δ′17O values are distinct from estimates of the bulk convecting upper mantle (−0.052‰). The δ18O values of likely co-genetic olivine and clinopyroxene pairs indicate that the olivine and clinopyroxene are not in isotopic equilibrium. There is also inverse co-variation in δ18O and Δ′17O observed. Together the data are reconciled as an interplay between two isotopically unusual O mantle reservoirs: one that fingerprints a composition established through early mixing of a recycled crust component (e.g., altered oceanic crust) in the deep mantle and another (e.g., a sub-continental lithospheric mantle component) subsequently introduced at shallower depths, possibly during crystallization. Ultimately, this work shows that mantle plume lavas are not homogenous with respect to oxygen isotopes when measured on individual mineral phases and that the additional measurement of 17O/16O is valuable for constraining the source of recycled materials within a single plume system and identifying processes involved in the plumes' chemical evolution.

title: Experimental investigation of the reaction between sediment-derived supercritical fluid and mantle peridotite
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Zhaohui Yu, Wan-Cai Li, Quanyou Liu, Huaiwei Ni
abstract: Slab-derived supercritical fluids serve as important agents for material transport in deep subduction zones. However, the mechanisms and products of the reaction between supercritical fluid and mantle peridotite remain poorly constrained. In this study, we experimentally investigated the reaction between a peridotite (PERD, specifically spinel lherzolite) and a supercritical fluid (SCF) containing 50 wt% solute (devolatilised global subducting sediment) under hot wedge condition. Using a double-capsule technique, an SCF was first synthesised in an inner Ag capsule at 3.0 GPa and 1000 °C; the temperature was then raised to 1200 °C to melt the Ag capsule and to allow SCF–PERD reaction. The quenched liquids and residual mineral assemblages were characterised by EPMA and LA-ICP-MS. With an increasing SCF:PERD mass ratio from 1:15 to 2:1, the liquid evolved from a hydrous basaltic melt to a hydrous boninitic (high-Mg andesitic) composition, and the residual mineral assemblage changed from Opx + Cpx + Ol + Grt + Amp to Ol + Opx, and ultimately to Ol. Comparison with the starting materials reveals that the hot SCF leached a range of components including MgO, FeO, and CaO from the peridotite, in contrast to melt–peridotite reactions, which instead introduce felsic components and produce pyroxenite. In addition, the basaltic melts formed through the interaction of SCF and peridotite contained lower levels of Na2O, K2O and Al2O3. More unique to SCF–peridotite reaction is that high-Mg andesitic magmas, such as those from the Mariana Arc or the Kamchatka Arc, could be generated by a substantial flux of SCF into the mantle wedge.

title: Sulfur isotope evidence for shale recycling in pyroxenites from the Beni Bousera orogenic massif (Morocco); insights on the HIMU mantle endmember
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Jabrane Labidi, Jean-Pierre Lorand, Pierre Cartigny, Fatima El Atrassi
abstract: The recycling of surface materials into the mantle shapes the chemical diversity of oceanic basalts. The Beni Bousera orogenic massif (Morocco) provides a unique window into these processes, exposing a great diversity of mantle pyroxenites, including samples formed from the recycling of lower oceanic crust. This massif hosts especially rare graphite-bearing pyroxenites, with evidence that graphite was once diamond. Here we present sulfur isotope compositions (δ34S, Δ33S, Δ36S) of graphite-free and graphite-bearing pyroxenites from Beni Bousera. Graphite-free pyroxenites preserve near-zero sulfur isotope signatures with low sulfur contents (∼300 ppm), similar to MORB. In contrast, graphite-bearing pyroxenites exhibit fractionated isotopic signatures, with δ34S ∼ −3.5‰, Δ33S ∼ +0.065‰ and Δ36S ∼ −0.45‰. Those are associated with extreme sulfur enrichment, up to 5600 ppm. Mass balance calculations indicate that these signatures reflect the addition of ∼5% black shale to an igneous oceanic crust protolith. The Δ36S/Δ33S systematics and the magnitude of Δ33S anomalies suggest the recycled shale is of post-Archean age. The sulfur isotope signatures documented in Beni Bousera are similar to those observed in basalts from the Mangaia HIMU plume. We propose that partial melting of shale-hybridized pyroxenites, analogous to those at Beni Bousera, generates metasomatic melts that transfer carbon and sulfur with fractionated isotope signatures to plume sources. The radiogenic lead isotope composition of Mangaia, however, remains consistent with the classical model of slab devolatilization and U/Pb fractionation during subduction. Our mechanism reconciles the classical HIMU model with the growing evidence for carbon and sulfur enrichment in the Mangaia HIMU mantle source.

title: Controls on Rb enrichment during granitic magma–hydrothermal evolution: Constraints from fluid–melt partitioning at 850 °C and 200 MPa
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Jianping Li, Jinsheng Han, Xia Hu, Xingcheng Liu, Huayong Chen
abstract: Rubidium (Rb) enrichment in granites and granitic pegmatites commonly reaches several thousand to tens of thousands of μg/g, far exceeding average crustal abundances, yet the relative roles of magmatic differentiation and fluid exsolution in generating such enrichment remain poorly constrained. Here, we experimentally determined Rb and Cl partitioning between hydrous granitic melts and supercritical Cl-bearing aqueous fluids over a range of melt and fluid compositions at 850 °C and 200 MPa, and integrated the partitioning results with Rayleigh-type modelling to track the coupled evolution of fluid chlorinity and Rb extraction efficiency during progressive magma crystallization. Rb fluid–melt partitioning is controlled primarily by fluid chlorinity rather than by melt composition, with fluid–melt partition coefficients for Rb increasing systematically from 0.3 to 1.2 as fluid chlorinity rises from ∼1 to 4 mol/kg H₂O, consistent with increasingly important RbCl complexing in saline fluids. However, comparison with previous in situ measurements indicates that the absolute magnitude of D Rb f / m at the highest chlorinity varies among experimental systems and should be interpreted cautiously. Combining Cl partitioning data, the modelling results indicate that the chlorinity of exsolved fluids rapidly decreases and stabilizes near ∼1 mol/kg H₂O (∼ 5 wt% NaCleq.) during crystallization, largely independent of initial melt H₂O content, melt composition, or initial fluid chlorinity. Under these conditions, fluid–melt partition coefficients for Rb converge rapidly to ∼0.3, causing magmatic fluids to extract only a minor fraction (<10% at 99% crystallization) of the total magmatic Rb budget even in initially saline systems. In contrast, residual melts continuously concentrate Rb to ore-forming levels during advanced crystallization. These results demonstrate that extreme Rb enrichment in granite systems is controlled primarily by prolonged magmatic differentiation, whereas magmatic fluid exsolution is generally inefficient for Rb concentration.

title: Hydrothermal alteration of volcaniclastic sediments: experimental insights into smectite authigenesis and its subsequent chloritization
description: Publication date: 5 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 725 Author(s): Anas Muhammad Salisu, Abdulwahab Muhammad Bello, Abduljamiu O. Amao, Ignatius Argadestya, Khalid Al-Ramadan
abstract: Volcaniclastic sediments are a significant component of the sedimentary record and are increasingly recognized as important targets for hydrocarbon exploration and energy transition. This study investigates the hydrothermal alteration of modern volcaniclastic deposits from the Opak Estuary (Java, Indonesia) under controlled laboratory conditions. Sediments were reacted with natural Red Sea water at 80, 150, 200 and 250 °C for 28 days, and the reaction products were characterized using petrography, SEM–EDS, X-ray diffraction (XRD), wavelength-dispersive X-ray fluorescence (WD-XRF), and total reflection X-ray fluorescence (TXRF). The starting material is dominated by plagioclase and pyroxene and contains no detectable clay minerals. At 80 °C, alteration is limited to incipient dissolution of primary minerals without detectable clay authigenesis. At 150 °C, smectite nucleates as grain coatings and pore-lining aggregates following dissolution of reactive volcaniclastic minerals. With increasing temperature, the clay assemblage evolves through mixed-layer chlorite–smectite (C/S) at 200 °C toward chlorite-dominated assemblages at 250 °C, reflecting progressive chloritization driven by the availability of Fe and Mg released from dissolving mafic minerals. Fluid chemistry evolves systematically, with progressive acidification, increasing total dissolved solids, enrichment in dissolved Ca and Fe, and non-linear Mg behavior that quantitatively reflects the incorporation of seawater-derived Mg into authigenic clay minerals. Mass-balance analysis demonstrates that approximately 20% of the original solid mass was lost during alteration and provides a quantitative link between mineral dissolution, fluid evolution, and secondary clay formation. The experiments define a systematic reaction pathway from dissolution-dominated alteration to progressive chloritization under the present experimental conditions. Because the experiments were conducted over 28 days in a closed system, the reported temperatures should be regarded as experiment-specific reaction milestones rather than universal diagenetic thresholds. The principal outcome of this study is an experimentally constrained framework describing the sequence and mechanisms of clay authigenesis during hydrothermal alteration of volcaniclastic sediments, providing a basis for interpreting similar mineral assemblages in volcanic sedimentary systems.

title: A comparative study on the occurrence and enrichment mechanisms of Co and Ni in different types of marine polymetallic nodules and cobalt-rich Fe–Mn crusts: Implications for seafloor Co and Ni mineralization
description: Publication date: 5 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 725 Author(s): Sucheng Huang, Yazhou Fu
abstract: Marine ferromanganese crusts and nodules are valuable deep-sea mineral resources that host critical metals such as cobalt and nickel, which are indispensable for advanced and environmentally sustainable technologies. This study systematically investigates the characteristics, occurrence and enrichment mechanisms of Co and Ni in hydrogenetic, hydrogenetic-diagenetic, and phosphatized Fe–Mn deposits from the Pacific, using a combination of sequential leaching and microscopic to nanoscale mineralogical analyses. Results show that Co and Ni are predominantly hosted in Mn-oxide minerals, particularly vernadite and todorokite. Cobalt is enriched in vernadite under hydrogenetic conditions, whereas Ni is incorporated into the tunnel structure of todorokite during suboxic diagenesis. Hydrogenetic deposits exhibit high Co and moderate Ni, with Co structurally bound to vernadite via oxidative substitution and Ni adsorbed and incorporated into the vernadite lattice. Hydrogenetic-diagenetic nodules exhibit alternating Co-rich vernadite and Ni-rich todorokite layers, reflecting pore water-mediated diagenesis where Mg2+ assists interlayer expansion of vernadite and todorokite crystallization. Phosphatization triggers substantial remobilization: the contents of Co decreases by 23.6% due to reductive dissolution, while Ni increases by 87.5% through recrystallization into diagenetic todorokite and associated transitional 10 Å Mn-oxides. The extent of phosphatization governs Ni redistribution, with low-intensity causing Ni loss and higher intensities promoting Ni enrichment. These findings support a coherent enrichment pathway from hydrogenetic vernadite to diagenetic todorokite, emphasizing control by redox conditions and mineralogical transformation. This study advances understanding of marine metal cycling and provides a predictive framework for exploration of critical metals in deep-sea Fe–Mn deposits.

title: Decoding the paleoenvironmental and diagenetic signatures of ancient phosphorites using an integrated multidisciplinary approach
description: Publication date: 5 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 725 Author(s): A. Schneider-Mor, P.C. Hackley, R.J. McAleer, A.M. Jubb, B.J. Valentine, J.J. Hatcherian, J.L. Nedzweckas
abstract: Phosphorites are significant geological deposits that serve as key archives of past marine productivity, biogeochemical cycling, and sedimentary processes, as well as critical reservoirs of phosphorus, an essential element for global agriculture. Phosphorite deposition occurs under specific environmental settings, which allows for investigation of the interactions between microbial activity, organic matter (OM) preservation, and phosphate mineralization. This work focused on organic petrography of the Mishash Formation in southern Israel and offers insights into the paleoenvironmental conditions and diagenetic processes that influenced Late Cretaceous phosphorite deposition in Israel, which occurred in an extensive phosphorite belt spanning from present-day Turkey to Morocco. Three distinct OM types were identified based on their petrographic characteristics: organo-facies 1 to 3, each reflecting different stages of diagenesis and environmental conditions. Organo-facies 1 likely formed under reducing conditions, followed by transition to early diagenesis in more oxic environments. Organo-facies 2 represents an extreme case of oxidative degradation. Organo-facies 3 features suggest preservation under reducing conditions with minimal alteration. Geochemical data reinforce these petrographic findings and emphasize the critical role of sulfur in “locking” biological and chemical signatures. Our study highlights the role of varying redox conditions and microbial activity in shaping the diagenetic history of organic matter in phosphorites, providing insights into the mechanisms of phosphorite formation and preservation of OM. These findings contribute to a broader understanding of phosphorite genesis on ancient continental margins and offer a reference framework for interpreting global phosphogenesis events and assessment of the economic potential of phosphorite deposits worldwide.

title: Gibbs energy modeling of low-temperature bornite phases: Calculation of phase equilibria in the vicinity of Cu 5 FeS 4
description: Publication date: 5 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 725 Author(s): Peter Waldner
abstract: Thermodynamic modeling of two low-temperature bornite phases with the stoichiometry Cu5FeS4 is performed at a total pressure of 1 bar. Two Gibbs energy expressions as a function of temperature are modeled, taking into account experimental data from the literature, such as heat capacities, enthalpy of transformation and Gibbs energies of formation, as well as phase equilibria data. Alongside recently reported thermodynamic models of neighboring phases, such as high-temperature bornite and chalcopyrite, it is now possible to perform phase equilibria computations around the composition Cu5FeS4 for the first time in the low-temperature regime of the Cu-Fe-S system. A topological analysis under consideration of binary CuS phase relations is conducted to investigate the consistency between predicted and experimental equilibria by calculating joins according to CuxS5 – Cu5FeS4 with x = 9.0, 9.2 and 9.3. Phase diagram analysis of the digenite-bornite join can now be supplemented from a thermodynamic point of view. A computed phase diagram section along the join Cu2S – CuFeS2 from ambient to liquidus temperatures provides a broader perspective on the phase relations around the composition Cu5FeS4.

title: Release and recapture: Limited carbon mobilization in sediment adjacent to Central Atlantic Magmatic Province sills, Florida, USA
description: Publication date: 5 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 725 Author(s): Lindsi Allman, E.M. Stewart, Kanwa Sengupta, Mainak Mookherjee, Miles Kelsey, Paul Hackley, Ryan McAleer, Aaron M. Jubb, Rebecca Stokes
abstract: Large Igneous Provinces (LIPs) are associated with dramatic changes to the Earth system; their rapid release of carbon may initiate catastrophic climatic changes causing mass extinction. This carbon release is often associated with volcanic emissions, yet metamorphic carbon production is poorly constrained. Metamorphic carbon devolatilization occurs as intrusions interact with host sediment, potentially releasing substantial sedimentary carbon. While this process has been modeled, few studies use an observational approach. Here, we apply geochemical analysis, petrographic analysis, Raman spectroscopy, vitrinite reflectance, and thermodynamic modeling to understand carbon devolatilization in sediment adjacent to Central Atlantic Magmatic Province basaltic intrusions using two boreholes that penetrate the Florida basement. We find geochemical and petrographic evidence for CO2 release from carbonates below a 10 m thick sill, with upward fluid transport and recapture of mobilized CO2 at the top of the sill. Ultimately, we estimate 220 mols/m2 to 9900 mols/m2 of carbon were mobilized from sedimentary carbonate. Uncertainties in the extent of re‑carbonation suggest that anywhere from 0 mols/m2 to 7100 mols/m2 may have escaped to the surface. We find little evidence of organic carbon mobility, due partly to the increased activity of CO2 from carbonate devolatilization. Discrepancies between measured temperatures and 1D thermal models suggest complexities in heat transport through aqueous pore fluid flow and short (hundred to thousand year) heating timescales. These results highlight that further field-based study can help clarify the roles that heating timescales, fluid flow, sediment chemistry, and other factors play in releasing and capturing carbon during LIP emplacement.

title: Age and origin of the Bynoe Li-Cs-Ta Pegmatite Field, Northern Territory, Australia; a multi-isotopic dating approach
description: Publication date: 5 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 725 Author(s): Samuel Chalmers, Carl Spandler, Jarred Lloyd
abstract: Through multi-mineral geochronology, this study investigates the age and evolution of Li-Cs-Ta (LCT) pegmatites in the Bynoe Pegmatite Field, Northern Territory, Australia. In situ, LA-ICP-MS based radiometric dating techniques utilised for pegmatite geochronology include U–Pb of zircon, apatite, cassiterite and columbite-group minerals, Lu–Hf of apatite, and Rb–Sr of muscovite. Additionally, migmatites of the Welltree Metamorphics, adjacent to the pegmatites, were dated by zircon U–Pb and apatite Lu–Hf to constrain the timing of anatexis within the region. Zircon U–Pb dating proved to be ineffective due to significant metamictisation of individual grains. Apatite Lu–Hf and cassiterite U–Pb give respective crystallisation ages for the pegmatites of ca 1750–1745 Ma and 1755–1740 Ma. Uranium–Pb dating of columbite-group minerals returned reversely discordance data of poor precision, though a broadly accurate age of 1754 ± 27 Ma (n = 18, MSWD = 3.3) was calculated. Apatite U–Pb ages of 1700–1670 Ma and muscovite Rb–Sr ages in the range of 1680–1620 Ma are interpreted as preserving either an extended cooling history or later-stage hydrothermal events. This research has conclusively shown that the timing of emplacement of LCT pegmatites within the Bynoe Pegmatite Field occurred at ca 1755–1740 Ma, demonstrating the successful application of numerous geochronometers to LCT pegmatite style Li deposits. We also show that the formation of these pegmatites post-dates the currently recognised extent of plutonism in the Pine Creek Orogen, challenging the theory that they formed by fractional crystallisation of a local granite. Instead, a previously unrecognised crustal melting event that was coeval with pegmatite formation gives credence to a possible anatectic origin for the pegmatites.

title: Decoupling of gallium and aluminum in bauxite deposits: Constraints from simulation experiments and Ga isotopes
description: Publication date: 5 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 725 Author(s): Yuxu Zhang, Haifeng Fan, Kunyue Ling, Chuanwei Zhu, Hong Yang, Shengjiang Du, Hanjie Wen
abstract: Given the chemical and crystallochemical similarities between gallium (Ga) and aluminum (Al), Ga is typically enriched in Al-bearing minerals (e.g., aluminum hydroxides and clay minerals) via isomorphism, resulting in a strong Ga-Al correlation in Al-rich sedimentary rocks such as bauxite. Bauxite is generally enriched in Ga and serves as the primary industrial source, contributing ∼90% of global Ga production. However, some bauxites with substantial Ga enrichment exhibit notable Ga-Al decoupling, the mechanism of which remains unclear. Here, a comprehensive study was carried out on the Houcao bauxite deposit in Zunyi, Central Guizhou, SW China, which displays decoupled Ga and Al contents. Ga/Al ratios of samples from the H1 profile and the upper part of the H2 profile range from 2.30 × 10−4 to 2.93 × 10−4, broadly consistent with the range of potential source rocks (shales and carbonate rocks with ratios of 2.47–3.43 × 10−4). In contrast, samples from the lower part of the H2 profile show a gradual increase in Ga/Al ratios from 3.35 × 10−4 to 5.54 × 10−4, with the five lowermost, Ga-rich samples (Ga/Al = 4.35–5.54 × 10−4) exhibiting pronounced Ga-Al decoupling. These decoupled samples uniquely contain pyrite intergrown with illite, indicating an acidic depositional environment. Soaking experiments show that Al is more readily leached and mobilized than Ga at pH ∼6. Furthermore, the leachate is enriched in heavy Ga isotopes compared to the residues. A negative correlation between δ71Ga and Ga content in the two studied profiles suggests that isotopically heavy Ga was released during bauxite formation, leaving lighter Ga in the residual bauxites. We conclude that environmental pH is a key control on Ga-Al decoupling, with acidic conditions (pH < ∼5.5) favoring Ga enrichment and neutral to alkaline conditions promoting Ga depletion, providing a new framework for understanding Ga enrichment mechanisms in bauxite deposits.

title: Insights into the long-term preservation of buried marine cadmium derived from micro-scale observations of Cd distribution and speciation in organic-rich shales
description: Publication date: Available online 2 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Hannah C. Elms, Anthony Chappaz, Olivier Mathon, Tobias Salge, Alexander J. Dickson
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) is a nutrient-like trace metal whose burial in marine sediments influences both the long-term (103–104 yr) oceanic Cd mass balance and the interpretation of Cd-based paleoceanographic records. However, the sedimentary host phases that preserve Cd in the rock record remain poorly constrained. Here, we present the first direct micro-scale observations of Cd distribution and speciation in organic-rich marine shales from the Cape Verde basin (Hatteras Fm, ~94 Ma) and the North Sea basin (Sele Fm, ~56 Ma). Synchrotron micro-X-ray fluorescence (μXRF) maps show heterogeneous Cd distributions, ranging from diffuse matrix-bound Cd to discrete Cd-rich hotspots, but no consistent spatial association between Cd and Fe-rich phases, indicating that pyrite is not a major repository for Cd in these samples. Cadmium K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy and linear combination fitting show that Cd is dominated by cadmium sulfide (CdS), which accounts for 33–100% of the Cd in analysed spots; Cd sulfate forms most of the remainder, with minor Cd carbonate in one non-sulfidic sample. We interpret Cd sulfate chiefly as a secondary oxidation product of originally-reduced Cd sulfide, and infer that CdS is the dominant long-term burial phase under euxinic to anoxic conditions. These results indicate that ancient Cd records may reflect diagenetic redistribution and stabilisation in sulfide phases rather than the full diversity of initial Cd host phases buried at the seafloor. Direct speciation constraints are therefore essential for linking sedimentary Cd enrichments and Cd isotope records to marine redox conditions, productivity, and the long-term oceanic Cd cycle. Synopsis The burial of cadmium in marine sediments is a primary control on the global cycle of this important trace metal. Using micro-imaging and X-ray speciation techniques, we show that ancient marine sedimentary deposits are likely dominated by cadmium sulfide.

title: Common controls on Na and Sr in modern and fossil brachiopod shells: Long-term stability of biomineralisation and use for seawater Sr/Ca reconstruction
description: Publication date: Available online 1 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Clemens V. Ullmann, Carsten Lüter, Luís Vítor Duarte, Benito Andrade, Emma Court, Trevor Bailey, Martin Aberhan
abstract: Robust reconstructions of element cycles are important for a quantitative understanding of the evolution of the Earth system. Fossil shells of marine macroinvertebrates are abundant and constitute valuable archives of past environmental conditions, which can be tied into precise chronostratigraphic schemes. However, complex, species-specific biomineralisation influences on the expression of geochemical proxies in their shells hinder their use for the reconstruction of seawater chemistry. Here, we investigate the variability and co-variation of element/Ca ratios in the shells of modern and Early Jurassic brachiopods belonging to the orders Rhynchonellida, Terebratulida, and Thecideida. We show that within modern and fossil brachiopods of the orders Rhynchonellida and Terebratulida, shells display uniform and strong co-variation of strontium and sodium content. This co-variation is offset and less well expressed in the thecideide Pajaudina atlantica. The coupling of Na/Ca and Sr/Ca in shells of low-Mg calcite secreting taxa can be explained by joint controls on both elements. The comparability of the NaSr co-variation in modern and fossil examples suggests that biological controls on the uptake of these elements in Rhynchonellida and Terebratulida have remained essentially unaltered since at least the Early Jurassic. The Sr/Ca ratio of past seawater can be calculated using a Na-corrected Sr distribution coefficient of 0.051 established from modern terebratulide and rhynchonellide brachiopods. Based on this calibration, late Pliensbachian - late Toarcian (c. 185–175 Ma) seawater Sr/Ca ratios of 8.8 mmol/mol to 10.3 mmol/mol with uncertainties of 2 to 15% (95% confidence) are reconstructed.

title: Tourmaline chemistry and boron isotopes record multistage magmatic-hydrothermal evolution of the Beimulang porphyry Cu deposit, Tibet
description: Publication date: Available online 1 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Song Wu, Peng Liu, Shuyuan Chen, Sudong Shi, Jiancuo Luosang, Qiong Ci, Yayun Zhao, Xiaofeng Liu, Youye Zheng, Jianzhuang Zhao, Jiazhen Li
abstract: The Beimulang deposit, a newly discovered porphyry Cu deposit in the post-collisional Gangdese porphyry Cu belt, is distinguished by abundant tourmaline spanning late-magmatic crystallization to phyllic alteration. This occurrence is uncommon among other porphyry systems in the belt. We integrate petrography with in situ major-element, trace-element, and boron-isotope analyses of six texturally defined tourmaline types to reconstruct the magmatic-hydrothermal evolution and Cu mineralization of the deposit. Tur1-M formed during the late-magmatic crystallization, Tur2-O records the magmatic-hydrothermal transition, and Tur3-Po through Tur6-Ph represent potassic veining, tourmaline brecciation, propylitic alteration, and phyllic veining. Cu mineralization is principally associated with Tur3-Po and Tur6-Ph. Hydrothermal tourmaline contains approximately eight times more Cu than Tur1-M, whereas Tur1-M is enriched in Mn, Pb, Zn, Y, and rare earth elements. Systematic variations in Na, Ca, Ti, Sr, FeMg exchange, and FeAl exchange record changes in fluid composition, fluid-rock interaction, redox state, and salinity. Mineralized Tur3-Po and Tur6-Ph crystallized from relatively oxidized and saline fluids favorable for Cu transport and deposition. Tourmaline δ11B values range from −10.1 to −5.2‰. Boron-isotope modeling records monzogranitic fluid exsolution followed by Rayleigh fractionation from Tur1-M to Tur4-B. The lighter isotopic signature and Ca-Ti-Sr enrichment of Tur5-Pr record diorite-related input during propylitic alteration, whereas Tur6-Ph records renewed felsic magmatic-fluid discharge. Beimulang therefore developed as an open, multistage system in which wall rock interaction and recurrent inputs from compositionally distinct magmatic sources controlled fluid evolution and Cu mineralization. These results demonstrate that tourmaline provides a mineral-scale record of episodic magmatic-fluid processes in porphyry systems.

title: Magmatic water and Fe-Ti oxide mineralization in the Wajilitag intrusion, Tarim large Igneous Province
description: Publication date: Available online 1 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Huan Chen, Jia-Min Zhong, Yao Bi, Mo-Qi Wu, Qun-Ke Xia
abstract: Fe-Ti oxide deposits represent important global resources of titanium and vanadium, yet the factors controlling their formation remain debated. Here we investigate the role of magmatic water in Fe-Ti oxide mineralization using clinopyroxene-hosted hydrogen concentrations from the Wajilitag Fe-Ti oxide-bearing intrusion in the Tarim Large Igneous Province. Early-crystallized clinopyroxene with Mg# > 80 records approximately 1.3–2.3 wt% H₂O in the early-stage melts with which it equilibrated. Samples at the high-Ti/Y end of the dataset are also characterized by relatively high H₂O/Ce ratios, indicating an association between magmatic water and Fe-Ti oxide enrichment in the Wajilitag intrusion. Previous experimental and modeling studies show that dissolved H₂O depresses the liquidus temperatures of major silicate minerals and may allow Fe-Ti oxides to reach saturation earlier relative to these silicate phases. In light of these previous studies, our observations suggest that elevated magmatic water contents may have contributed to Fe-Ti oxide enrichment at Wajilitag by modifying the crystallization sequence.

title: Controls of Fe Mn cycling on polymetallic enrichment in Early Cambrian black shales: Evidence from the Huanglongshan manganese deposit, South China
description: Publication date: Available online 30 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Wan'er Wang, Zerui Ray Liu, Xiyao Li, Zhengwei Qin, Zhen Yang, Chenglin Liu, Mei-Fu Zhou
abstract: Early Cambrian black shales contain exceptionally high concentrations of polymetallic elements, such as V and Mo. Scavenging and particle-mediated transport by FeMn (oxyhydr)oxides have been widely proposed to explain this enrichment, yet geological constraints on the carrier stage remain limited. The Early Cambrian Huanglongshan manganese (Mn) deposit in the northern Yangtze Block provides a rare archive for evaluating this mechanism and associated metal sources. Although Mn ores in this deposit are dominated by Mn carbonates, particularly rhodochrosite and kutnahorite, their close stratigraphic association with phosphorites and strongly positive Ce anomalies (Ce/Ce* = 1.14–2.11) support Mn-oxide-rich precursors. Markedly negative δ13Ccarb values are consistent with organic-matter-driven reduction of these precursors and early-diagenetic Mn‑carbonate precipitation. Polymetallic enrichment and covariation with MnO further support scavenging by precursor FeMn (oxyhydr)oxides and particle-mediated transfer from the water column to sediments, followed by reductive release and diagenetic redistribution. LogTh–logU relationships, Zn enrichment relative to Co, and negative δ57Fe values collectively suggest additional non-detrital, potentially regional hydrothermal, inputs that increased metal availability in the basin. Similar polymetallic enrichment patterns and MoEF–UEF relationships in the Niutitang Formation black shales are consistent with a possible contribution from Fe–Mn-mediated particulate metal transfer. We therefore propose a coupled source–transport–sink model in which enhanced metal supply, Fe–Mn-mediated particulate transfer, and authigenic fixation under reducing conditions jointly promoted polymetallic enrichment. The Huanglongshan preserves a complementary record of the otherwise poorly preserved FeMn carrier stage.

title: Potassium and sulfur isotope geochemistry of jarosite in sulfur–rich sediments in Victoria, Australia
description: Publication date: Available online 28 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Yuqi Li, Andrew J. Frierdich, Tao Yang, Anne J. Whitworth, Weiqiang Li
abstract: Jarosite is a critical K–bearing indicator mineral of acidic and oxidizing sulfate–rich environments. While S isotope geochemistry of jarosite has been extensively studied, K isotopes remain largely unexplored despite their potential to trace alkali dynamics, mineral formation processes, and fluid–mineral interactions. This study presents a systematic investigation of K and S isotopes in morphologically diverse jarosite samples from two coastal sites in Victoria, Australia: Fossil Beach (FB) and Southside Beach (SB). The jarosite samples exhibit a wide range of δ41K values, from −1.70‰ to +1.14‰. A positive correlation (R2 = 0.42) exists between K/(K + Na) ratios and δ41K values. This trend, where K–rich jarosite is enriched in 41K, contradicts equilibrium fractionation theories and suggests Rayleigh−type fractionation during progressive precipitation. Sulfur isotopes show distinct site variations: FB samples display highly positive δ34S values (+15.47‰ to +40.30‰) that are consistent with closed−system sulfate reduction in a sulfate−limited reservoir with no external sulfate input, while SB samples range from −5.54‰ to +23.39‰ and lack extreme positive enrichments, consistent with a marine-buffered system oxidation and marine sulfate influx. Integrating the K and S isotope data from this study with previously published Fe isotope data thus distinguishes between the environment (recorded by S) and mineral formation mechanism (recorded by K and Fe), enabling a holistic reconstruction of jarosite formation pathways. This work showcases the use of K, Fe, and S isotopes as tracers for reaction pathways in acid–sulfate systems, with significant implications for both interpreting weathering intensity in terrestrial environments and understanding jarosite formation in analogous Martian settings.

title: Testing the chromium isotope redox proxy in a South China Permian-Triassic succession: Validation and limitations
description: Publication date: Available online 26 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Yuqiu Wei, Anping Hu, Thomas J. Algeo, Qiankun Hu, Anjiang Shen, Feng Liang, Hao Li, Lanping Feng, Lian Zhou
abstract: Chromium (Cr) stable isotopes have emerged as a powerful redox proxy for reconstructing the Earth's oxygenation history. Marine carbonates serve as an important archive of sedimentary Cr-isotopic data, providing critical insights for tracing changes in paleo-oceanic redox conditions. However, whether the δ53Cr values of carbonates can faithfully record the information of ambient seawater at the time of deposition remains a subject of debate. To further evaluate the potential of this proxy, we present a high-resolution Cr-isotope (δ53Cr) record for both the bulk rock and authigenic Cr fractions in a carbonate succession spanning the Permian-Triassic Boundary (PTB) at Meishan, a classic shallow-water section in South China. We show that the bulk-rock and authigenic Cr and δ53Cr profiles exhibit not only consistent stratigraphic trends but also synchronous abrupt shifts. These observations are consistent with control of δ53Cr variation by contemporaneous changes in the redox state of the oceanic water column. Due to the influence of widespread anoxic conditions in the latest Permian ocean, the reduction of Cr(VI) to Cr(III) in seawater was significantly enhanced. This process drove a kinetic fractionation of Cr isotopes in the pre-extinction Upper Permian interval, yielding significantly positive δ53Cr values (δ53Crbulk: +1.24 ± 0.55 ‰, 2SD; δ53Crauth: +1.86 ± 0.21 ‰, 2SD), which is markedly higher than the δ53Cr compositions of Phanerozoic marine carbonates. In contrast, owing to a rapid expansion of oceanic anoxia during the PTB crisis interval, seawater Cr(VI) was quantitatively reduced and sequestered in the eastern Paleotethys, leading to a sharp negative excursion in δ53Cr values (δ53Crbulk: +0.08 ± 0.60 ‰, 2SD; δ53Crauth: –0.06 ± 0.24 ‰, 2SD). A two-endmember mixing model suggests that the pronounced negative shift in the clay-rich boundary horizon (Bed 26) may, in part, record detrital Cr inputs associated with intensified continental weathering. Based on a comprehensive multifactor evaluation, the Meishan δ53Cr records demonstrate the suitability of Cr isotopes as a robust proxy for tracking geological changes in ocean-redox conditions subject to certain limitations.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of superposition effects of rainfall-induced urban waterlogging and levee breach flooding
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Ye Zhang, Xin Su, Guanghua Qin, Leizhi Wang, Jinhui Li, Lingjie Li, Yintang Wang, Xiting Li
abstract: Extreme rainfall and rapid urbanization have significantly exacerbated coupled riverine–pluvial flooding hazard interactions in urban areas, driven by the joint effects of pluvial flooding, river flooding, and levee instability. However, existing studies fall short of fully revealing the nonlinear interaction effects, hazard sources, and underlying driving mechanisms of “Pluvial flooding – Levee breach – Urban waterlogging” coupled riverine–pluvial flooding hazards. To address this gap, this study proposes an integrated framework using explainable machine learning to quantify and attribute the hazard superposition effects of this specific coupled riverine–pluvial flooding hazard chain. Taking the Yundong polder area in Wuxi City as a typical case study, we constructed single-rainfall, single-levee-breach, and coupled riverine–pluvial flooding hazard scenarios under recurrence intervals ranging from 20 to 200 years. By coupling hydrodynamic modeling with the Flood Superposition Index and Flood Superposition Increment, we categorized three types of superposition phenomena and seven classes of dominant-factor hazard zones. Combined with a coupled riverine–pluvial flooding hazard interaction transfer matrix and the XGBoost-SHAP approach, we quantitatively characterized the spatiotemporal evolution of hazard interaction types, as well as their dominant drivers and threshold behavior. The results indicate that coupled riverine–pluvial flooding interaction is not a simple linear combination of independent rainfall and levee breach events but exhibits pronounced nonlinear amplification effects under high recurrence intervals; the superposition effects show substantial spatiotemporal heterogeneity, characterized by hazard lag effects, severe inundation near the breach, strong amplification at the impact margin, and shifts in hazard attributes with increasing recurrence intervals; furthermore, the compound superposition effects are jointly governed by topography, distance to the breach, pluvial inundation depth, and breach inundation depth, with dominant drivers gradually shifting from breach dynamic factors to topographical factors under extreme scenarios. Overall, this study reveals the evolution and driving mechanisms of coupled riverine–pluvial flooding hazard interactions, supporting urban flood risk management and mitigation.

title: Regionalization of mountainous catchments in China for flash floods based on natural and anthropogenic disaster-causing factors
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Shenghao Xu, Jiyang Tian, Jianzhu Li, Yuefen Zhang, Ping Feng, Ting Zhang, Jiacheng Duan
abstract: China experiences frequent flash flood disasters due to its extensive mountainous terrain and complex monsoon climate, posing serious threats to lives and property. Existing national-scale flash flood regionalization studies are limited by insufficient evaluation of regionalization effectiveness, a lack of validation using historical flash flood disasters and inadequate consideration of anthropogenic influences. To address these limitations, a regionalization method based on multiple natural and anthropogenic disaster-causing factors was developed. A total of 88,006 small mountainous catchments across China were regionalized to identify areas with similar environments for flash flood formation and triggering. Eleven key disaster-causing factors were selected through VIF and Pearson correlation analyses, and a SOM-K-means clustering method was applied to delineate regions. Regionalization effectiveness was then evaluated using PERMANOVA and non-parametric tests of the rainstorm concentration index (RCIt ) derived from historical flash flood disasters. The results indicate that: (1) The 15 primary flash flood regions are consistent with China’s major topographic steps and key hydrological and climatic boundaries, while the 81 sondary regions capture finer-scale spatial differences in natural and anthropogenic disaster-causing factors. (2) PERMANOVA and non-parametric tests confirm significant heterogeneity among regions (P ≤ 0.001). (3) After controlling for population density, the partial Spearman correlation between bridge-culvert density and disaster frequency is 0.48 (P < 0.001), indicating a significant statistical association. The resulting scheme provides a basis for selecting suitable flash flood models by region and for parameter regionalization in ungauged areas, and it supports region-specific prevention and mitigation.

title: Deep learning with upstream-aware terrain representations and rainfall adapter for generalizable pluvial flood prediction
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Thomas Lutonsky, Viktor Birschitzky, Stefan Jeschke, Andreas Buttinger-Kreuzhuber, Nils Wandel, Daniel Cornel, Viola Haase, Reinhard Klein, Jürgen Waser, Michael Wimmer
abstract: Deep learning-based surrogate models can substantially accelerate pluvial flood simulations. However, most existing approaches struggle to generalize across heterogeneous terrains or modified topographies, limiting their applicability for real-world flood risk assessment unless retrained for each specific terrain. In this work, we investigate how deep learning flood surrogates can be designed to achieve robust spatial generalization across previously unseen terrain configurations without retraining. We train an attention-enhanced U-Net on diverse terrain and introduce upstream-aware input maps that propagate terrain properties into downstream regions, allowing the model to capture long-range spatial dependencies and supporting the learning of generalizable spatial features. In addition, we add architectural design choices to improve the model’s capacity to generalize beyond the training domain. We further propose a two-stage training strategy with an adapter-like rainfall encoder that enables efficient adaptation to previously unseen rainfall intensities while preserving spatial generalizability. The resulting model predicts maximum water depths and is evaluated on unseen catchments in Germany, Austria and Denmark, as well as on artificially modified terrains, such as terrains with added dikes. Our results demonstrate that combining a large training dataset with upstream-aware terrain representations and a generalization-oriented architectural design enables accurate flood predictions across unseen terrains, reaching an RMSE of 0.05 m and CSI0.3 of 0.83 over all test domains.

title: Hydrological flux effectiveness index for assessing rainfall partitioning and hydrological functioning under climate change
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Rahul Sharma, S. Sreekesh
abstract: This study proposes a novel Hydrological Flux Effectiveness Index (HFEI) to quantify rainfall partitioning effectiveness and evaluate watershed hydrological functioning under changing climatic conditions. Unlike conventional hydrological assessments that emphasize precipitation magnitude or isolated flux components, the HFEI integrates key gain and loss processes controlling subsurface storage and runoff generation into a single framework. The index is formulated using four dimensionless hydrological ratios derived from Soil and Water Assessment (SWAT) simulated fluxes: evaporation loss ratio (ELR), surface runoff to water yield ratio (SWR), recharge ratio (RR), and base-flow contribution ratio (BCR). The framework is implemented in the Chaliyar River Basin (CRB), with multi-site calibration–validation using Sequential Uncertainty Fitting algorithm (SUFI-2). Future climate simulations are driven by bias-corrected CMIP6 projections under SSP2 and SSP5 for 2025–2095. Annual sub-basin hydrological fluxes are used to compute HFEI independently for each GCM, and inter-model uncertainty is quantified using ensemble statistics (mean and standard deviation). For comparability, historical and future HFEI series are standardized using z-scores based on the historical baseline, enabling detection of deviations from historical hydrological functioning. Results show that HFEI effectively captures strong spatial heterogeneity in hydrological effectiveness, distinguishing subsurface-dominated sub-basins from runoff-dominated systems. Ensemble results indicate robust but spatially variable climate-driven shifts in hydrological partitioning. Sensitivity analysis confirms the stability of the equal-weighting structure and the robustness of the index formulation. Overall, HFEI provides a physically based and scalable framework for assessing hydrological resilience under changing climatic conditions.

title: Pore-structure-mediated effects of incorporated Festuca arundinacea roots on water retention and unsaturated infiltration in loess
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Xiaochan Wang, Hengxing Lan, Shijie Liu, Enlong Liu, Bei Zhang, Weifeng Sun, Pan Wang, Xuanchen Ren, Langping Li, Han Bao
abstract: Herbaceous roots can substantially alter soil water retention and unsaturated infiltration by modifying pore structure, yet the quantitative relationship between root-associated pore-structure changes and hydraulic behavior remains unclear. In this study, remolded root–soil composites were prepared by incorporating mature Festuca arundinacea roots into loess at five root mass ratios (RB). Soil-water characteristic curve (SWCC) measurements, soil column infiltration experiments, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) were conducted to investigate water retention, pore structure, and unsaturated infiltration. Increasing RB promoted the development of medium and large pores, resulting in a more heterogeneous and multiscale pore structure. These pore-structure changes were associated with nonlinear variations in hydraulic parameters, characterized by increases in saturated water content θ s and the air-entry-related parameter α , accompanied by decreases in residual water content θ r and the shape parameter n . Based on quantitative relationships between pore-structure descriptors and hydraulic parameters, a structure-constrained parameter modification method for the van Genuchten (VG) model was proposed. To evaluate the proposed method, the modified parameterization was incorporated into the Richards equation, and infiltration under five uniform RB conditions and one condition representing the vertical root distribution of mature F. arundinacea was simulated using HYDRUS. The simulations reproduced the measured water-content dynamics and wetting-front migration well under different root configurations, demonstrating the applicability of the proposed method. These findings highlight the role of root-associated pore-structure changes in soil hydraulic behavior and provide parameter support for understanding vegetation–soil–water interactions and unsaturated infiltration in the Loess Plateau.

title: A physics-informed, soft-causal ensemble deep neural network for robust probabilistic water quality assessment in arid regions
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Keyvan Habibi, Mohammad Reza Nikoo, Reza Kerachian, Rouzbeh Nazari, Jiří Šimůnek, Amir H. Gandomi
abstract: Because reservoirs are critical assets for water supply in arid and semi-arid environments, safeguarding these resources is essential. Water quality assessment in such systems therefore requires predictive models that are not only accurate but also interpretable and capable of quantifying uncertainty. In this study, a Physics-Based Soft-Causal Ensemble Probabilistic Deep Neural Network (PBSCEP-DNN) was developed to predict the Water Quality Index (WQI), using 16,096 field measurements from an AAQ-RINKO Conductivity-Temperature-Depth (CTD) profiler. The model was constructed using a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), ensuring that the network topology reflects hypothesized environmental dependency pathways, both direct predictive relationships and confounder-related influences, rather than an unrestricted, fully connected structure. The proposed framework’s novelty lies in combining a network architecture based on hypothesized environmental dependencies, regularized through an L2 penalty on direct-path weights, with a deep ensemble of five probabilistic neural networks to capture both point predictions and associated uncertainty in reservoir water quality dynamics. The proposed framework achieved RMSE = 1.324 ± 0.222, MAE = 0.452 ± 0.110, R2 = 0.795 ± 0.075, and empirical coverage of Prediction Interval Coverage Probability (PICP) = 0.996 ± 0.003 for nominal 95% prediction intervals, indicating conservative overcoverage. Rather than optimizing point-prediction accuracy alone, the PBSCEP-DNN offers a more physically grounded and uncertainty-aware alternative to purely data-driven prediction.

title: Recirculation tracer tests in long uncased boreholes: a simple way to identify hydraulic conductivity
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Adam Laayoune, Philippe Pasquier
abstract: Standing column wells are ground heat exchangers that offer significant energy-saving potential, yet their optimal design requires accurate site-specific hydrogeological data. While continuous groundwater recirculation tests are routinely performed for thermal assessments, their potential to characterize aquifer hydrogeological properties remains underexploited. In this study, we improve the exploitation of these tests by injecting a conservative tracer to estimate the effective hydrogeological parameters of a fractured aquifer. A field protocol was deployed in a 215 m deep well located in Varennes, Canada, where fluorescein was injected during continuous recirculation and monitored in real time. To interpret the tracer signal, a 2D-axisymmetric finite-element model simulating groundwater flow and solute transport was developed and coupled with an inverse optimization algorithm. The numerical model accurately reproduced the experimental breakthrough curve, capturing the early-time homogenization oscillations with high accuracy and a characteristic period of 31.3 min. This enabled the simultaneous estimation of the rock mass flow and transport properties, identifying hydraulic conductivity with high precision. The hydraulic conductivity estimated from the recirculation tracer test was consistent with independent pumping-test estimates obtained at the same site, demonstrating that the proposed method can recover realistic hydraulic properties from a simple operational test. These results show that this new tracer-test method can transform a routine recirculation procedure into a high-precision and reliable hydrogeological characterization tool.

title: Pore-network structure and transport responses across textures and salinization levels in seasonally frozen saline soils: evidence from CT scanning and lattice Boltzmann simulations
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Fan Wang, Jianmin Bian, Zhiqi Gu, Dongmei Ruan
abstract: Salinization alters soil pore architecture and transport behavior in seasonally frozen regions; however, the relationships between three-dimensional pore structure and pore-scale flow and solute spreading remain poorly understood. We combined high-resolution X-ray computed tomography, pore-network analysis, and lattice Boltzmann simulations on six undisturbed cores representing three soil textures and two salinization levels, collected after spring thaw in western Jilin, China. A 600 × 600 × 600 voxel representative elementary volume was used for pore-scale characterization. Intrinsic permeability ranged from 2.56 × 10−11 to 3.88 × 10−10 m2 and was higher in the heavily salinized core of each texture pair. Longitudinal dispersion ranged from 1.51 × 10−9 to 2.83 × 10−9 m2 s−1, exhibiting the same heavy-to-light ordering. Heavily salinized cores consistently exhibited higher specific surface area, two-dimensional and three-dimensional fractal dimensions, and anisotropy, along with lower sphericity, whereas coordination number showed no consistent directional response across textures. Intrinsic permeability was most strongly correlated with anisotropy (Spearman ρ = 1.00, p = 0.003); associations involving dispersion were weaker, and the reduced redundancy analysis was not significant. Comparison with laboratory and field measurements revealed that the salinization-related contrast in flow capacity reversed at larger scales, while dispersion maintained the same ordering from the pore to laboratory scale but not at the field scale. Longitudinal dispersion increased sublinearly to approximately linearly with observation scale (n = 0.71–1.05). These results demonstrate that pore geometry provides a valuable structural basis for interpreting scale-dependent water and solute transport in seasonally frozen saline soils.

title: Deep learning meets spectral analysis: reproducing long-term persistence in synthetic streamflow
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Francesco Granata, Fabio Di Nunno, Senlin Zhu
abstract: Synthetic streamflow generation requires simultaneous reproduction of flow distributions and temporal dependence across multiple scales, including long-term persistence (LTP). This study evaluates a three-stage framework that combines latent-space generation with a temporal convolutional network (TCN), low-frequency spectral adjustment, and quantile-based rank reordering. The framework was applied to daily discharge records from 24 UK river basins and benchmarked against autoregressive moving average (ARMA), k-nearest-neighbor (k-NN), and long short-term memory (LSTM) generators. Marginal distributions were reproduced closely (median Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic = 0.00069; 99th-percentile ratios = 0.986–0.999). The median absolute difference in the rescaled-range persistence estimate was 0.028, with 79% of basins within a tolerance of 0.05. Detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA) produced a median scaling-exponent difference of 0.076; Monte Carlo tests showed that part of the R/S-DFA discrepancy reflects estimator-specific finite-sample behavior. The same experiments indicate that a 0.05 tolerance is approximately a two-standard-deviation band at the 7,300-day synthetic-series length, and that shorter records tend to inflate persistence estimates. ARMA produced a statistically indistinguishable median R/S error (0.024). For the nine records with no missing days, the proposed framework and k-NN showed very similar paired low-flow spell-duration errors. The proposed framework is therefore not uniformly superior to simpler alternatives; its main value is the combination of close marginal matching with an explicit spectral mechanism for controlling long-term persistence. Remaining limitations include weaker short-lag autocorrelation reproduction and incomplete recovery of threshold-conditioned spell clustering.

title: The impact of numerical error on hydrological model performance
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Jianfei Zhao, Yanan Duan, Jialu Huang, Yiming Hu, Binquan Li, Jun Wang, Zhongmin Liang
abstract: The simple yet crucial question of what impact numerical error has on performance of hydrological model has not received consistent answers. Discrepancies in previous studies can be attributed to model structural changes and insufficient watershed sample sizes. In this study, we focus on the Xinanjiang model, a widely used hydrological model in China. Two mathematical forms are considered: the original discrete equation form (DTE-XAJ), which prone to numerical error, and the differential equation form (ODE-XAJ), which serves as an reference with controlled numerical error. To assess structure consistency, we propose a convergence validation method by gradually shorting time step of the DTE-XAJ model and checking for convergence to numerical solution of the ODE-XAJ model. To address sample size limitations, we apply both models to 547 watersheds from the CAMELS dataset. The results show that: (1) state variables and fluxes of the DTE-XAJ model converge to those of the ODE-XAJ model under time step refinement, demonstrating structural consistency and the effectiveness of the convergence validation method; (2) numerical error significantly degrades Xinanjiang model performance during both calibration and validation period, meaning its negative effects cannot be fully compensated by the calibration procedure; (3) controlling numerical error leads to systematic performance improvements even for a mature model such as XAJ, providing empirical evidence of its non-negligible contribution to model uncertainty. This study proposes the convergence validation method to rigorously assess structural consistency, providing a theoretical foundation for future research. The findings underscore the importance of addressing numerical error in hydrological models.

title: Regional site suitability assessment for groundwater dams in South Korea using AHP-GIS
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Min Seo Bae, Jaehee Kim, Dayoung Kang, Jian Kim, Hanjoo Kwak, Soonjae Lee
abstract: Groundwater dams are increasingly considered a sustainable means of augmenting water-supply reliability and buffering climate-driven hydrological variability. In South Korea, 80 groundwater dam candidate sites have been identified through demand-driven national investigations, yet a standardized basis for inter-site comparison has been lacking. This study develops the AQCEG model, a regional site suitability assessment framework, which evaluates five criteria — water abundance, water quality, constructability, ecological compatibility, and governance — and expresses the result as a relative suitability index (0–5). National spatial datasets were compiled from public sources and preprocessed to a resolution of 100 m × 100 m grid. Ecological suitability and governance are applied as non-compensatory binary exclusion masks that separate technical suitability from legal and institutional acceptability, while the remaining criteria are calculated by weighted summation. The criterion weights were derived through the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) from pairwise-comparison survey of 25 experts in water resources, hydrogeology, environmental science, and policy. Water Abundance received the highest group weight aggregated across the 25-expert panel (0.66), and present-state indicators were consistently preferred over forward-looking risk indicators across all criteria (CR < 0.04). GIS-based weighted overlay produced a nationwide suitability map whose high-suitability watersheds concentrate in mountainous headwaters of the eastern and southern uplands, outside major exclusion zones. Retrospective benchmarking against 80 pre-selected candidate sites showed that these sites occupy reaches of significantly above-average water abundance – while their separation from the national background weakened once all criteria were integrated, consistent with the assessment’s role as a permissive first-pass screen rather than a sharp site classifier. The AQCEG framework offers a transparent, reproducible, data-driven screening tool for groundwater dam planning at national and regional scales.

title: Probabilistic sensor placement in water distribution networks: a Dynamic Residual Masking framework using game-theoretic pseudo-Jacobians
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Elvio Damonti, Giancarlo Bernasconi
abstract: Optimal sensor placement in Water Distribution Networks (WDNs) traditionally relies on rigid sensitivity matrices requiring computationally prohibitive white-box hydraulic simulations. While data-driven alternatives utilizing game-theoretic machine learning, specifically, Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), offer computational relief, they inherently suffer from a “dimensional trap.” Raw SHAP values mathematically inherit the target variable’s dimensions, creating a dimensional incompatibility when applied to network hydraulics. To resolve this, a fully data-driven, probabilistic sensor placement framework is proposed. Random Forest (RF) regressors are trained on stochastic, non-stationary network data to extract these game-theoretic marginal contributions. Crucially, a novel “pseudo-Jacobian” transformation is derived that restores the physical dimensional integrity of the SHAP-derived sensitivities. These mathematically valid sensitivities are then mapped through a Gaussian noise Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) to create a strict estimated probability of detection landscape, abandoning arbitrary deterministic thresholds. Finally, a Dynamic Residual Masking algorithm is introduced. A soft-masking greedy search tracks unmet network estimated probabilities to naturally repel highly correlated sensor pairs, commonly referred to in optimization literature as the “evil twin” phenomenon. Validation on the publicly available 500-scenario Hanoi WDN benchmark demonstrates that the proposed framework bypasses the computational bottleneck of traditional finite-difference simulations. Furthermore, the methodology achieves a 91.60% accuracy in faulty/non-faulty scenario detection with highly sparse coverage (5 sensors), closely approaching the 93.80% accuracy yielded by full network coverage (31 sensors). Concurrently, a 2.5% reduction in false positives is achieved compared to the classical explicit-Jacobian baseline. This establishes a rigorous, mathematically valid bridge between game-theoretic artificial intelligence and physical hydraulic engineering.

title: Seasonal reversals in surface environmental gradients and a novel phytoplankton bloom risk assessment framework in the trans -Arctic Ocean
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Chaofeng Wang, Bo Li, Hengchang Du, Longwen Fu, Sixian Huang, Yuhang Zhang, Xinyuan Chang, Juanling Zhou, Xiaoyu Wang
abstract: The Arctic Ocean is undergoing unprecedented environmental changes driven by global warming, with profound consequences for biogeochemical cycles and ecosystem functioning. However, high-resolution spatiotemporal characterization of surface physicochemical heterogeneity and quantitative phytoplankton bloom risk assessment remain limited, hindering informed environmental management.
