When only sparse discretized bed information is available, the framework is extended to simultaneously reconstruct water depth, bottom pressure, bed topography, and discharge within a unified learning process. The proposed approach is evaluated through representative numerical experiments. Results demonstrate that the framework can reliably estimate discharge and reconstruct hydraulic states under limited observation conditions. In scenarios with sparse bed information, the method successfully recovers bed topography while maintaining accurate discharge estimation and consistent hydraulic state reconstruction. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of using SGN-constrained physics-informed learning for observation-limited hydrodynamic inversion, discharge estimation, and bed-topography recovery in controlled benchmark cases.

title: A coupled flood forecasting framework of HYDRUS-1D and Xinanjiang models based on the transfer of physically-based soil moisture fields
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Qiaoling Li, Yang Wang, Hongde Li, Xingwen Liu, Zhijia Li, Yang Xiao
abstract: Initial soil moisture is a critical state variable influencing the accuracy of event-based flood forecasting. The Xinanjiang (XAJ) model often suffers from error accumulation and spatial homogenization when estimating initial soil moisture through recursive water balance calculations. To address this limitation, this study utilizes the physically-based HYDRUS-1D (H1D) model to support a more physically consistent initialization of the XAJ model and proposes a flood forecasting framework (XAJ-H1D) based on the transfer of physically-based soil moisture fields. By establishing a water balance-based soil moisture state variable transfer mechanism, the framework links the H1D model with the XAJ model for flood forecasting. In the near-dam area of the Wuqiangxi Reservoir, reliable soil moisture observations were obtained from the monitoring network after sensor calibration and used to support the calibration of H1D soil hydraulic parameters through an improved NSGA-II multi-objective optimization algorithm. Based on a virtual–actual integration strategy, the calibrated H1D model was extended from the in-situ monitoring stations to selected virtual stations, thereby increasing the spatial density of soil moisture simulation points across the basin. Soil moisture simulated at the 34 in-situ and virtual stations was subsequently averaged within each sub-basin to construct multilayer soil moisture fields. Physical conversion relationships were then applied to transform H1D-simulated volumetric water content into the soil water storage required by the XAJ model, allowing physically-based soil moisture information to be transferred into the subsequent recursive water balance calculations of the XAJ model. Results show that the optimized H1D model captures point-scale soil moisture dynamics with a mean root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.025 cm3·cm−3. Across 8 flood events in 2023 and 2024, the XAJ-H1D framework reduced the mean relative error of flood volume from 12.99% to 5.27% and that of peak discharge from 17.35% to 9.00%, while increasing the mean Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) from 0.53 to 0.75 compared with the conventional XAJ initialization. More pronounced improvements were found during the early flood season or under relatively dry antecedent conditions. These results suggest that the proposed state variable transfer mechanism can mitigate initialization bias in conceptual hydrological models and improve basin-scale flood forecasting performance under the evaluated conditions.

title: Analyzing hydrological degradation vulnerability of non-perennial rivers shaped by groundwater stress, geogenic hazard and limited storage potential
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Thallam Prashanth, Sayantan Ganguly
abstract: Hydrological degradation, which poses a significant threat to river segments in a basin/watershed, manifests as a substantial decline in total water storage (TWS) in the river basin owing to rising climatic & anthropogenic stress, and formation of subsurface erosional landforms. Assessing and analyzing spatiotemporal variations of hydrological degradation vulnerability (HDV) across heterogeneous watersheds remains challenging in data-sparse semi-arid environments. In this context, the present research aims to assess the HDV in ungauged river segments using the proposed novel approach (S4H). The HDV computed using the S4H approach is validated using the proposed depth-duration curve-based river aquifer stress index (DDC–RASI). The HDV estimated by the proposed method is cross-validated using a newly proposed hypsometric-integral-based standardized TWS anomaly (HI–STWSA) duration curves derived from the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) and GRACE Follow-On (FO) satellite missions. To improve spatial patterns of hydrological stress & recovery, the HI–STWSA computed at the basin scale is downscaled to the watershed scale. The study finds that certain segments of the Pennar River in southern India exhibit high vulnerability, primarily due to intensive groundwater extraction and extensive sinkhole development, which severely disrupt subsurface storage and flow accumulation. In contrast, the downstream reach of the river near Nellore shows comparatively lower vulnerability, reflecting a lower stage of extraction and better groundwater-surface water connectivity. These findings highlight the urgent need for region-specific water management strategies to mitigate hydrological degradation.

title: Stomatal conductance dominates land surface hydrological responses to rising CO 2 concentrations in the Yellow River Basin
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Jinkai Luan, Ning Ma, Jun Ge, Fengxue Gu, Yunfei Wang, Wei Li, Qingyu Jia, Yuanyuan Yang, Hua Li, Zhihui Wang, Zhiguo Yu
abstract: Rising atmospheric CO2 concentrations are known to perturb the terrestrial hydrological cycle, yet the relative roles of CO2-driven vegetation physiological and structural change in shaping land surface hydrology remain unclear. Here we use a process-based ecohydrological model to quantify how these two pathways modulate evapotranspiration (ET) and runoff (Q) across the Yellow River Basin (YRB) in northern China. We show that CO2-induced stomatal conductance (ΔETstomata and ΔQstomata) and vegetation structure (ΔETstructure and ΔQstructure) reductions suppress ET but enlarge runoff, while the impact of changes in stomatal conductance is substantially greater than that of structural modifications. By contrast, their interaction increases ET (ΔETinteraction) and decrease runoff (ΔQinteraction). Within the controlled CO2-sensitivity experiments, the LAI-mediated contribution to ET change was substantially smaller than the fixed LAI physiological contribution. Basin-wide sensitivity analysis indicates that a 100 ppm increase in atmospheric CO2 reduces ET by ∼6.7 mm, primarily due to a ∼7.6 mm reduction in ΔETstomata, with a marginally offset (<1 mm) from decreased ΔETstructure and 1.8 mm increase in ΔETinteraction. Runoff showed a comparable but opposite sensitivity, dominated by the stomatal conductance component. The influence of increasing CO2 on hydrological variables varies substantially in space, with larger effects in the southeastern YRB than in the northwestern and western regions, and across ecosystem types, with the highest and the lowest sensitivities occurring in forests and deserts, respectively. By explicitly separating plant physiological and structural effects, our results clarify the pathways by which rising CO2 reshapes hydrological processes in a typical dryland basin, providing valuable insights for reducing uncertainty in water resource projections across semi-arid and arid regions.

title: Threshold-like bacterial community reorganization and microbial health risk along phosphorus-enrichment gradients in urban rivers
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Kun Shi, Jiafeng Zhang, Kexuan Zhang, Shilei Zhou
abstract: Whether phosphorus enrichment is associated with threshold-like reorganization of urban river bacterial communities and how this relates to microbial health risk remain poorly understood. We integrated DOM characterization, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, machine learning, life-history analysis, microbial health risk assessment, and metagenomics across an urban river network in Shijiazhuang. Two distinct community states were identified, with total phosphorus emerging as the strongest measured environmental predictor and 0.025–0.039 mg L−1 representing a putative, survey-specific transition interval. State B showed stronger deterministic reassembly, greater contributions of rapidly responding r-strategists, and weaker cohesion-based structural buffering. Path modeling supported an association cascade linking phosphorus-associated nutrient conditions with DOM and life-history reorganization, potential pathogen accumulation, and increased microbial health risk. Consistently, the potential pathogen health risk index increased from 41.33 ± 7.78 to 54.39 ± 9.52, accompanied by enrichment of resource-acquisition, antimicrobial-resistance, and virulence-related functions. Overall, phosphorus enrichment was associated with a coordinated nutrient–community–risk cascade from ecological reorganization to elevated microbial health risk, providing a basis for early warning and nutrient management in urban rivers.

title: A physically constrained multivariate bias correction framework for projecting compound drought and heatwave risk in the Yangtze River Basin
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Yue Zhuo, Zhiyong Wu, Hai He, Salvatore Pascale, Zhenchen Liu, Yuqing Feng, Yangqian Li, Shuhao Mei
abstract: Compound drought and heatwave (CDHW) events pose growing threats to water security and ecosystems in the Yangtze River Basin. Reliable projections require an accurate representation of the joint behavior of precipitation and temperature. However, biases in CMIP6 simulations and conventional univariate correction may distort this dependence, increasing projection uncertainty. This study developed a physically constrained, dependence-preserving multivariate bias-correction framework integrating CycleGAN, BiLSTM, and quantile delta mapping (QDM) to jointly correct daily precipitation, maximum temperature (Tmax), and minimum temperature (Tmin) from 13 CMIP6 models. The framework improved CDHW-relevant hot-dry dependence and reproduced the observed spatial pattern of historical normalized cumulative CDHW intensity with a correlation of 0.64. QDM compensation improved preservation of the raw CMIP6-projected Tmax warming signal, while CycleGAN–BiLSTM reduced Tmax–precipitation dependence errors relative to QDM alone. Under a fixed historical-reference heatwave threshold, projected CDHW occurrence increased, particularly under SSP5-8.5, mainly because more days exceeded the historical heat threshold. In contrast, under period-adaptive thresholds, CDHW occurrence conditional on concurrent heatwave and drought did not increase relative to the historical period. Sensitivity analyses showed that the magnitude and interpretation of projected CDHW changes depended on the heatwave-threshold definition and potential evapotranspiration formulation.

title: Improving flood forecasts: the combined impact of data assimilation and machine learning post-processing
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Gustavo Gabbardo dos Reis, Paul C. Astagneau, François Bourgin, Vazken Andréassian, Charles Perrin
abstract: Accurate streamflow forecasts are essential for flood risk management and impact mitigation. Coupling hydrological models with machine learning techniques has gained increasing attention as a means to improve forecast skill, with post-processing emerging as a promising approach to correcting systematic model residuals. However, the interaction between machine-learning post-processing, data assimilation and calibration strategies remains insufficiently explored. In this study, we assess the contribution of machine-learning-based post-processing to hourly streamflow forecasts for 687 catchments in metropolitan France, generated using a GR-family hydrological model (GR5H-RI) under three forecasting approaches differing in calibration strategy and use of data assimilation. Random Forest and Multilayer Perceptron models are used to post-process forecasts at lead times of 3, 6, 12 and 24 h. Forecast performance is evaluated using both continuous skill metrics relative to persistence and threshold-based metrics for flood event detection. Results show that (1) post-processing consistently improves forecast skill at short lead times, especially for slower-response catchments, with the median persistence score increasing from 0.33 to 0.54 at a 3-h lead time in the highest-skill forecasting setup and performance improving in 89.7% of catchments; (2) the largest gains occur for forecasts without data assimilation, suggesting that post-processing can partially compensate for the lack of state updating but cannot fully replace it; and (3) neural network-based post-processing slightly outperforms tree-based models in continuous metrics, while differences are more limited for event detection. Overall, results highlight the complementary roles of data assimilation and machine-learning post-processing and demonstrate the potential of such frameworks for operational flood forecasting.

title: Inverse modeling for post-wildfire hydrologic process understanding over snow-dominated watersheds
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Trevor F. Partridge, Michelle A. Walvoord, Sheila F. Murphy, Michael N. Fienen, Aubrey L. Dugger, Brian A. Ebel
abstract: Wildfire-induced changes to vegetation and soil properties can alter snowpack dynamics and hydrologic processes in ways that complicate predictions of post-wildfire water availability. To better understand these effects, we coupled the Parameter ESTimation in C++ (PEST++) software with the Weather Research & Forecasting Hydrologic model (WRF-Hydro) across three burned, snow-dominated watersheds in the western United States. We incorporated three burn-severity-based land cover categories into WRF-Hydro and used an iterative Ensemble Smoother (iES) within PEST++ to estimate model parameters controlling snow accumulation and melt, infiltration, and streamflow generation. This framework supported three complementary objectives: (1) assessing parameter sensitivities under pre- and post-wildfire conditions, (2) comparing pre- and post-wildfire parameter ensembles to identify wildfire-driven shifts in hydrologic processes, and (3) using counterfactual simulations to isolate the hydrologic response to wildfire from interannual climate variability. Our findings indicate that model parameter sensitivity varied by domain and shifted following wildfire. Maximum snow albedo and snow albedo decay were most influential in the higher-elevation East Troublesome domain, while the rain-snow partitioning temperature threshold dominated in the lower-elevation Chippy Creek and Las Conchas domains. Following wildfire, streamflow sensitivity shifted away from snowpack parameters toward soil hydraulic parameters, consistent with wildfire-driven reductions in evapotranspiration and increases in soil moisture. Incorporating wildfire effects led to complex changes in simulated snowpack accumulation and streamflow timing, generally leading to earlier snowmelt freshet initiation and cessation and reduced late season flows. Simulations were more sensitive to interannual climate variations than wildfire land cover changes. These results highlight both the potential and challenges of ensemble-based inverse modeling for understanding post-wildfire hydrologic change in snow-dominated watersheds.

title: Multi-objective optimization of best management practices in agricultural watersheds using single-step deep reinforcement learning
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Jinuk Kim, Byeongchan Yun, JongCheol Pyo, Li-Chi Chiang, Jin Hwi Kim, Kyeong Hwa Cho
abstract: Optimal placement and intensity of best management practices (BMPs) in watershed management needs balancing pollutant reduction with implementation cost. We proposed a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework for cost-aware, SWAT-based BMP implementation, applied to the Namyang estuarine reservoir watershed in South Korea. The framework jointly optimized continuous application intensities of four structural BMPs, vegetative filter strip (VFS), grassed waterway (GWW), terrace, and detention pond (DTP), across 31 subbasins in a single-step optimization environment. Three DRL algorithms and NSGA-Ⅱ were compared under an identical budget of 1,000 SWAT simulations. Among the algorithms, proximal policy optimization (PPO) achieved the highest final reward, approximately 66% and 68% higher than those of TD3 and SAC, respectively. The best PPO solution achieved 92.4% of the maximum attainable combined reduction of suspended sediments (10.2%) and total phosphorus (82.2%) at a cost of $5.02 million, corresponding to 9.6% of the full implementation cost, whereas NSGA-Ⅱ required $14.62 million to reach the same reduction level. Consequently, PPO was approximately 2.9 times more cost-efficient than NSGA-Ⅱ under the identical evaluation budget. Additionally, the learned PPO policy showed a spatially differentiated pattern. The VFS was broadly applied across the watershed, GWW was selectively combined with VFS in steeper subbasins, and DTP was concentrated in a single key subbasin. Thus, PPO-based DRL provides a cost-efficient and interpretable alternative to conventional multi-objective evolutionary optimization for direct SWAT-in-the-loop applications.

title: Propagation from precipitation extremes to root-zone soil moisture and attribute changes in dry and wet events: A global paired event analysis
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Yanhui Zheng, Sile Li, Peng Wang, Lina Wang, Xihui Gu, Jiangchao Qiu, Xiaohong Chen
abstract: Precipitation extremes do not invariably correspond to soil moisture extremes, yet propagation studies emphasize occurrence and timing rather than attributes of matched events. Using calendar month standardized anomalies, we compared monthly dry and wet events in precipitation from the Global Precipitation Climatology Centre (GPCC) and surface and root-zone soil moisture from the Global Land Evaporation Amsterdam Model (GLEAM) over land between 60°S and 60°N during 1981–2024. Same sign events were matched independently one-to-one along three pathways: precipitation to surface soil moisture (P → SMs), precipitation to root-zone soil moisture (P → SMrz), and surface to root-zone soil moisture (SMs → SMrz). Propagation probability was the matched fraction of all source events, matched pair changes in duration, severity, and peak intensity were expressed as log2(target/source). Area-weighted mean P → SMrz propagation probabilities were 0.370 for dry events and 0.405 for wet events. Duration changes were + 0.672 and + 0.452, respectively. Peak intensity changes were positive for dry events (+0.222) and negative for wet events (−0.260), while severity increased for both. P → SMs showed the same peak contrast but smaller duration increases. In GLEAM, SMs → SMrz events matched more frequently but had smaller duration changes. Propagation probability and attribute changes varied across four aridity regimes without a common monotonic gradient, but the dry-positive/wet-negative peak contrast persisted in every regime. Redefining event boundaries using 1- and 3-month standardized precipitation and soil moisture indices retained the P → SMrz duration and peak directions. ERA5-Land reproduced the duration and peak directions in both precipitation-to-soil moisture comparisons, whereas SMs → SMrz peak directions differed between products. Monthly precipitation and soil moisture extremes therefore exhibit incomplete event correspondence and sign-dependent attribute differences among successfully matched pairs; occurrence, persistence, and peak intensity describe distinct aspects of their relationship.

title: Regional landslide early warning through machine-learning-based rainfall threshold and hydromorphological slope units
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Muqi Xiong, Youcun Qi, Zhanfeng Zhao, Xun Li
abstract: Regional landslide early warning (LEW) remains a fundamental challenge because of the spatial heterogeneity of hydrological–geomorphological units and the nonlinear responses inherent in rainfall-triggering processes. This study develops an integrated LEW framework that combines landslide susceptibility prediction (LSP) with rainfall-threshold modeling based on machine learning (ML) to advance the quantitative characterization of regional-scale rainfall-landslide hydrology. For spatial characterization, we propose a novel LSP model that integrates hydrological analysis (HA) and multi-scale segmentation (MSS) to better represent hydromorphological controls on the spatial distribution of slope failures. The HA–MSS model demonstrates strong spatial discriminability: “very high susceptibility” zones capture 69.33 % of observed landslides while occupying only 6.76 % of the total area. For temporal prediction, an ML-based rainfall-threshold model trained jointly on triggering and non-triggering events achieves a probability of detection of 0.82, an accuracy of 0.85, a probability of false detection of 0.13, and a Hanssen–Kuipers index of 0.69, substantially outperforming the empirical E–D baseline. Feature-importance analysis identifies event cumulative rainfall (ECR), maximum intensity (Imax), intensity (I), and duration (D) as dominant predictors, whereas antecedent rainfall variables (AR3, AR5, AR7) contribute 35.2 % of the total feature importance, highlighting the importance of antecedent wetness conditions in rainfall-induced landslide triggering. The integrated framework supports dynamic warning updates at hourly resolution through a spatiotemporal warning matrix. Retrospective assessment of the integrated LEW showed that approximately 87 % of historical landslides were associated with red or orange alert levels, while the August 2021 hindcast reproduced the temporal escalation and spatial evolution of warning levels during an intense rainfall event.

title: A dual-scale optimization framework linking annual assessment with event-based erosion risk for watershed conservation
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Xinyu Zhang, Fan Zhang, Shouhong Zhang, Yufei Ren
abstract: Soil erosion in small watersheds is influenced by both long-term hydro-climatic conditions and short-term extreme rainfall events, challenging robust conservation strategy design. However, most optimization studies are limited to annual assessments, which may underestimate erosion risks under extreme rainfall and obscure trade-offs among soil conservation, water yield, and carbon storage. In this study, we propose a multi-objective framework integrating annual ecosystem service assessment and event-based erosion constraints. It integrates RUSLE and InVEST with 0–1 integer programming to optimize conservation configuration considering soil retention, water yield, carbon storage, and cost. An event-based soil loss model is further applied to stress-test the optimized configurations under annual maximum rainfall. The framework was applied to a severely eroded watershed on the Loess Plateau. The initial assessment revealed an alarming mean soil erosion rate of 4885.73 t·km−2·yr−1, alongside suboptimal water yield and carbon storage. Results show that the optimized configuration reduces annual soil erosion to 13.34% of the baseline level, decreases soil organic carbon loss to 13.24%, and increases carbon storage by approximately 4%. These improvements are achieved with a moderate reduction in water yield (to 93.78% of the baseline) and under the constraint of acceptable implementation costs. Furthermore, the supplementary event-based optimization mitigates erosion risks under rainfall events, ensuring soil loss remains below the tolerable threshold. This study demonstrates that integrating event-based erosion constraints with annual optimization improves the robustness of conservation planning under hydrological variability. The proposed framework provides a spatially explicit and computationally efficient decision-support tool for watershed management, particularly in erosion-prone regions with limited data.

title: Warm-wet shift reshapes hydroclimatic synchronization networks across the Arid Area of Northwest China
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Jiayou Wang, Zhi Li, Yaning Chen, Ruiting Wu, Lingxin Kong
abstract: Global warming has profoundly reshaped hydroclimatic regimes in the Arid Area of Northwest China (AANC), yet how the regional warm–wet shift reorganizes hydroclimatic synchronization and drought propagation dynamics remains poorly understood. Based on multi-timescale SPEI records (1962–2021) from 114 stations, we built constrained hydroclimatic synchronization networks via normalized mutual information. Temporal autocorrelation was accounted for through prewhitening, while spatial dependence was assessed and statistically controlled using topography-constrained null models, allowing us to examine stage-varying network topology and propagation dynamics. The warm–wet transition was initiated by an abrupt precipitation increase in 1987, followed by a stepwise temperature rise in 1997. During the transition period (1988–1996), short-timescale synchronization networks became highly fragmented, with sharply reduced connectivity, enhanced community partitioning and strongly inhibited propagation, indicating a temporary breakdown of regional hydroclimatic coherence. In contrast, long-timescale networks remained relatively integrated, with weaker community boundaries and more efficient large-scale propagation driven by persistent low-frequency hydroclimatic variability. Across all stages, longer SPEI accumulation timescales consistently strengthened network connectivity while weakening community partitioning and propagation barriers, revealing robust timescale-dependent reorganization of hydroclimatic synchronization. Comparisons between raw and residual networks further confirm the robustness of observed patterns and highlight notable long-timescale biases induced by temporal persistence. These findings demonstrate that the AANC warm–wet shift represents a nonlinear reorganization of hydroclimatic synchronization through coordinated reorganization of network topology, community structure and propagation dynamics, rather than a simple regional wetting process, providing new insights into drought synchronization mechanisms and hydroclimatic risk propagation in arid regions.

title: Recirculated and fresh submarine groundwater discharge fluxes of dissolved carbon in a temperate seagrass lagoon
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Yusi Wang, Bangjian Zhang, Qiangqiang Zhong, Xu Ren, Shiqing Sun, Yuda Chen, Miao Li, Ronggen Jiang, Jinzhou Du, Fenfen Zhang, Isaac R. Santos
abstract: Submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) is a critical hydrological process linking coastal aquifers, sediments, and ocean waters. However, bulk SGD estimates often cannot distinguish the relative contributions of fresh submarine groundwater discharge (FSGD) and recirculated submarine groundwater discharge (RSGD) to dissolved carbon export. In this study, we employ a modified pathway-specific Ra model that separates FSGD from RSGD by contrasting mixed porewater Ra endmembers. By coupling these partitioned water fluxes with measurements of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), dissolved organic carbon (DOC), and fluorescent dissolved organic matter (FDOM), we quantify pathway-specific dissolved carbon export within a temperate seagrass lagoon. The dual-Ra (223Ra and 224Ra) model revealed that RSGD was substantially higher than FSGD, with fluxes of 2.6 (2.2–3.3) and 0.9 (0.7–1.5) cm d-1, respectively. Porewater DIC and DOC concentrations were approximately 1.7 and 2.0 times greater than those in seawater. Consequently, RSGD accounted for approximately 82% and 87% of the total net SGD-associated DIC and DOC fluxes, respectively, corresponding to RSGD-associated area-normalized fluxes of 71 (41–101) and 12 (9–15) mmol m−2 d-1. Optical analyses further revealed that SGD transported both humic-like and protein-like fluorescent DOM components, with humic-like components dominating the exported FDOM pool. Together with the enrichment of DIC and DOC in porewater relative to seawater, these findings provide evidence that RSGD drives the advective export of carbon-enriched porewater into the lagoon. Our results demonstrate that pathway-specific separation of FSGD and RSGD is essential to attribute dissolved carbon fluxes in coastal aquifers and to properly evaluate groundwater-mediated lateral exchange in coastal blue carbon budgets.

title: S-GRHyMoLAP: A stochastic extension of the GRHyMoLAP model with different diffusion mechanisms for probabilistic rainfall-runoff modeling
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Sianou Ezéckiel Houénafa, Lionel Cédric Gohouede, Romuald Daniel Boy-ngbogbele, Melissa Latella, Olatunji Johnson, Cenk Sezen
abstract: Probabilistic rainfall-runoff modeling in watershed hydrology is strongly affected by uncertainties in inputs, model structure, parameters, and their potential interactions. In this study, we investigate alternative representations of these uncertainties by extending the recently released GRHyMoLAP into S-GRHyMoLAP, a stochastic differential equation (SDE) formulation with hydrologically motivated diffusion mechanisms. The proposed framework represents uncertainty through input-driven, internal-state-driven, and flow-driven diffusion formulations, while additionally introducing an input-state interaction-driven diffusion formulation. Evaluation across 526 catchments from the Catchment Attributes and Meteorology for Large-sample Studies-France (CAMELS-FR) dataset shows that input-driven diffusion provides the best probabilistic representation among the single-variable diffusion formulations, while the interaction-driven diffusion performs best in 70% of catchments. The framework matches the predictive interval score of the heteroscedastic Gaussian residual (HGR) benchmark method for GRHyMoLAP, while outperforming it for the Génie Rural à 4 Parameters (GR4J). Explainable machine learning combining Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) reveals that, although the major catchment predictors are similar across diffusion formulations, their relative influence depends on the considered diffusion. The input-driven diffusion formulation favors catchments with strong hydroclimatic forcing, while the interaction-driven formulation remains sensitive to external factors and exhibits enhanced responsiveness to internal flow organization. These findings indicate that incorporating an interaction-driven diffusion formulation can improve probabilistic streamflow prediction and highlight the potential of S-GRHyMoLAP for investigating how uncertainty propagates through rainfall–runoff dynamics.

title: Grid-based optimization for irrigation and water quality synergies
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Yingshan Chen, Qiang Fu, Vijay.P. Singh, Yijia Wang, Zhaoqiang Zhou, Yaowen Xu, Luchen Wang, Mo Li
abstract: Water scarcity and agricultural non-point source pollution increasingly challenge irrigation management under climate change, yet existing approaches rarely capture climate-driven pollutant transport and spatially heterogeneous irrigation needs. We develop a grid-scale simulation–optimization framework coupling SWAT, DSSAT, and a cellular automata-based multi-source irrigation model, and apply it to the Sanjiang and Songnen Plains to assess water-saving and pollution-reduction synergies under current and future climates. Results show that optimal irrigation strategies vary markedly among regions because of spatial differences in pollutant emissions and water-use efficiency. Overall, optimized water-saving irrigation reduces pollutant emissions by approximately 12.96% and irrigation water use by 24.57%. In western regions, a 49.25% expansion of water-saving irrigation improves the coordination among economic, environmental, and water-resource objectives by 33.07%. Under future climate scenarios, precipitation strongly influences pollutant transport, while pollutant migration is inversely related to water-saving irrigation potential. These findings provide a spatially explicit basis for climate-resilient irrigation planning and coordinated agricultural water and pollution management.

title: Quantitative monitoring of DNAPL source zone evolution in heterogeneous aquifers via deep-learning fusion of time-lapse surface and cross-borehole ERT with borehole constraints
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Fansong Meng, Yuting Zhang, Dejin Wang, Yaping Qi
abstract: Dense non-aqueous phase liquids (DNAPLs) persist for decades in heterogeneous aquifers, where characterizing source-zone evolution is essential for contamination control and remediation assessment. Borehole sampling is sparse and invasive, while individual electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) configurations suffer inherent resolution limits. This study presents a borehole-constrained, multi-source time-lapse electrical fusion inversion framework that couples multiphase flow and petrophysical simulation with a deep-learning architecture, allowing reconstruction of DNAPL saturation fields from time-lapse surface ERT, time-lapse cross-borehole ERT, and sparse borehole concentration data. Coupled simulations supply physically consistent training data unavailable from real contaminated sites. Relative to single-ERT approaches, the fusion strategy reduces the mean source-zone area estimation error from 29.41 to 49.64% to 20.67% and the mean migration-front error from 18.77% to 5.42%, reductions of up to 58.4% and 71.1%, respectively. Incorporating borehole concentration data as spatial constraints further reduces the boundary displacement error by 37.4% and the saturation mean squared error by 28.6%. In a heterogeneous laboratory sandbox experiment, the borehole-constrained fusion reached a mean intersection over union of 0.682, reduced the mean boundary error by 69.6% relative to standalone surface ERT, and lowered the source-area overestimation from 148% to 33%. A borehole-spacing analysis further identifies a practical drilling-density threshold of about 1.5 m for the tested configuration. The method may inform soil and groundwater protection efforts, including identification of high-risk source zones, the placement of remediation wells, and the estimation of contaminant mass flux for risk assessment, and provides a basis for further studies on monitoring complex contaminated sites.

title: Seasonal responses of chemical oxygen demand and dissolved oxygen to dam regulation in the Yangtze and Yellow Rivers during 1988–2018: Role of altered flow regimes
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Anqi Huang, Guangyao Gao, Yadu Pokhrel, Liqiang Yao, Hong Zhang
abstract: The riverine chemical oxygen demand (COD) and dissolved oxygen (DO) dictate water quality and biogeochemical health. Mega-dams substantially alter the flow regimes in large river basins, yet their impacts on seasonal COD and DO dynamics in the long term remain unclear. This study examined the changes in annual and monthly COD and DO exports from the Yangtze and Yellow Rivers during 1988–2018, and quantified the influences of natural and anthropogenic factors in the pre- and post-dam periods using the machine learning (ML) approach and partial least squares-structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). There was a pronounced decrease in annual average COD in Yellow (−35.0%) but an increase in Yangtze (3.7%), and DO increased substantially in Yellow (9.8%) but remained stable in Yangtze from pre- to post-dam period. The seasonal variation of COD substantially weakened in Yellow, and the peak of COD and DO flux occurred one month earlier in Yellow but later in Yangtze in the post-dam period. The relationships of COD and DO fluxes with discharge became stronger in the post-dam period, especially in the Yellow. The COD-discharge coupling shifted toward enrichment in the Yangtze River and weakened in the Yellow River during the post-dam period. From the pre- to post-dam period, the relative contribution of hydroclimatic and vegetation factors in the Yangtze increased to 72.62% for COD flux and dominated COD and DO concentration variability in the Yellow over the Yangtze (56.60% vs. 38.02%). Altered flow regimes under dam regulation changed the timing and magnitude of COD and DO flux responses, and amplified the role of sediment as a carrier of organic pollutants. Furthermore, vegetation greening improves water quality in the Yellow, whereas increasing precipitation and discharge enhance pollutant mobilization in the Yangtze. This study reveals that dam regulation is strengthening the flow-water quality connection and elevating the relative importance of hydroclimatic and vegetation factors in explaining water quality variation, with important implications for sustaining riverine health in heavily regulated basins including the Mekong and Amazon.

title: A dual post-processing framework for probabilistic streamflow forecasting using deep learning ensembles: Integrating residual correction and Vine Copula-based BMA
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Wen-jie Liu, Zhong-kai Feng, Yang Xiao, Tie-sheng Guan, Tao Yang, Wen-jing Niu, Hong-wu Tang
abstract: Quantifying forecasting uncertainty and providing probabilistic streamflow forecasts are fundamental for flood and drought mitigation, reservoir operation, and water resources management. However, existing post-processing approaches usually address either residual error modeling or multi-model ensemble fusion, while few studies integrate them both. This study proposes a dual post-processing framework termed RC-VCBMA for multi-step probabilistic streamflow forecasting. To account for input, structural, and parameter‑related sources of ensemble diversity, ensemble forecast members are generated using GEFS forecast precipitation, three deep learning architectures, and multiple objective functions. A Mixture Density Network utilizing Countable Mixtures of Asymmetric Laplacians with LSTM backbone is then developed to generate time-varying mixture distributions of member-level hydrological residuals, enabling deterministic residual correction via the conditional expectation while capturing non-Gaussianity, autocorrelation, and heteroscedasticity. Building on the corrected members, a Vine Copula-based Bayesian Model Averaging method is further introduced to derive member-wise conditional posterior distributions by characterizing the three-dimensional dependence among baseline, observed, and forecast flows, and fuse them into an ensemble posterior distribution. The proposed framework is evaluated for 6-hourly multi-step inflow forecasting from 6 h to 48 h ahead for the Three Gorges Reservoir. Results show that compared with RC-HUPBMA, RC-VCBMA reduces WIS and CRPS by 15.3% and 13.5%, respectively. Compared with CMAL-DBMA, RC-VCBMA improves WIS and α_index by 8.1% and 6.8%, respectively, and reduces IGN by 3.713 on average, while remaining competitive in CRPS. Overall, RC-VCBMA achieves a favorable trade-off among distributional accuracy, interval sharpness, reliability, and predictive density concentration, highlighting its effectiveness as a probabilistic post-processing framework.

title: Ecological-priority multi-objective water allocation under hydrological and restoration scenarios in the Heihe River Basin
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Lianqing Xue, Hongcong Guo, Yuanhong Liu, Youjia Zhang, Guang Yang, Shushan Li
abstract: Water scarcity in arid inland river basins requires allocation strategies that reconcile downstream ecological restoration with intensive socioeconomic water use in midstream regions. This study developed an ecological-priority, scenario-constrained multi-objective water allocation framework for the middle and lower reaches of the Heihe River Basin. Three downstream ecological restoration levels (L1–L3) were combined with dry, normal, and wet hydrological conditions derived from Pearson Type Ⅲ frequency analysis to construct nine hydrological–ecological scenario boundaries. Yingluoxia runoff and local Zhangye precipitation were treated as independent hydrological inputs, defining midstream surface-water availability and agricultural effective rainfall, respectively. Scenario feasibility was screened using sectoral water-use quotas, a 29.32% agricultural water-saving target, effective rainfall utilization, and a groundwater-abstraction limit of 3.93 × 108 m3. An ecological–social–natural benefit-conversion and multi-criteria evaluation module was subsequently coupled with NSGA-Ⅲ to maximize comprehensive benefits while minimizing allocation-related carbon emissions and water-shortage rates within the feasible scenario space. The ecological release required at Zhengyixia increased to 11.59 × 108 m3 under L3, approximately 22% higher than under L1, thereby reducing the surface water available for midstream allocation. Conventional supply conditions were insufficient to satisfy peak irrigation demand, whereas improved irrigation efficiency and effective rainfall substantially reduced agricultural demand and residual groundwater dependence. Under the groundwater constraint, P1, P8, and P9 were retained as representative feasible scenario boundaries for dry, normal, and wet conditions, with groundwater requirements of 3.62, 2.43, and 0.33 × 108 m3, respectively. These scenarios represent feasible water-supply boundaries rather than final allocation solutions. Within each boundary, NSGA-Ⅲ generated non-dominated solution sets, from which representative compromise allocations were selected using normalized ideal-point distance and final constraint verification. Sensitivity analysis indicated that dry-condition feasibility was particularly vulnerable to reduced irrigation performance, while objective-ablation analysis showed that excluding the carbon objective shifted compromise selection toward higher-emission allocations. The framework provides a case-specific decision-support basis for coordinating ecological restoration, water-use benefits, shortage risk, and allocation-related carbon emissions in arid inland river basins with comparable water-management conflicts.

title: A dual-channel framework for video-based rainfall intensity estimation using weakly supervised rain streak extraction
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Jiarui Xu, Naliang Guo, Fubao Sun, Feng Wu
abstract: High-spatiotemporal rainfall data are essential for hydrological analysis and urban flood early warning. By leveraging existing urban surveillance cameras, video-based rainfall intensity estimation is a potential high-resolution complement to traditional rainfall observations. However, most recent video-based methods feed the raw video clips into an end-to-end model for rainfall intensity estimation, and existing rain streak extraction algorithms cannot adapt to complex real-world daytime scenes. This impairs the capture of useful visual rainfall features, ultimately limiting estimation performance. To address these limitations, we first develop a weakly supervised rain streak extraction framework. It employs a self-learning network to generate rain-streak pseudo-labels, enabling adaptive extraction with weak supervision and knowledge distillation. Second, we design a dual-channel rainfall intensity estimation network grounded in an analysis of the formation mechanisms of visual rainfall features. This network independently extracts global visual features from raw frames and high-frequency features from rain streak layers. These features are then fused spatially and temporally for rainfall intensity estimation. Experiments on surveillance videos from two cameras with different imaging conditions demonstrate that the rain extraction framework can adaptively extract rain streaks while reducing interference from background disturbances. The dual-channel model was evaluated on six independent rainfall events recorded by a fixed surveillance camera, covering rainfall intensities from 0 to 1.1 mm/min, and achieved an NSE of 0.894, outperforming the raw-clip-only end-to-end baseline. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed dual-channel concept for video-based rainfall intensity estimation and may provide a potential rainfall sensing approach for future hydrological applications.

title: Physics-informed hydrological graph neural network for distributed daily streamflow prediction in directed river networks
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Tao Wang, Dingzhi Peng, Yuwei Gong, Xingtong Chen, Qianxue Yang, Linghua Qiu, Yunqing Xuan
abstract: The basin in high-altitude mountainous areas is constrained by sparse station networks, complex river networks, and significant non-stationary hydrological processes, making it difficult for traditional time series models to simultaneously consider spatial connectivity and physical consistency. To address this issue, we propose Physics-Informed Hydrological Graph Neural Network (PI-HydroGNN) for distributed daily streamflow prediction in directed river networks. It combines temporal feature extraction, upstream connectivity and topological inflow aggregation, graph-based topology message passing, and physical constraints in a unified framework to represent temporal dynamics, river-network connectivity, and local mass conservation. The model was evaluated through comparisons with independent station-wise LSTM, regional multi-output LSTM, GCN and SWAT, together with ablation experiments, multi-step forecasting, analysis of Quality Balance Violations and ungauged basin extrapolation. The results showed that PI-HydroGNN outperformed the benchmark models in the training, validation, and testing periods, with an average NSE of 0.84 during the testing period and a RMSE reduction of about 16% compared to station-wise LSTM. The ablation experiment results showed that all the modules we considered made significant contributions to the predictive performance and exhibited significant spatial heterogeneity. At Yangbajing, the model still maintains good simulation ability, with an NSE of 0.79 and an R2 of 0.80, providing preliminary evidence of its spatial extrapolation capability. Overall, this study demonstrates that combining prior knowledge of hydrological physics with graph learning offers a promising approach for streamflow prediction in complex river networks, and suggests potential for application in ungauged basins that should be further validated under broader hydro-climatic conditions.

title: Isotopic responses of hot and cold groundwaters to the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes: Evidence from oxygen-18 (δ 18 O), deuterium (δ 2 H), and tritium ( 3 H, TU)
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Emine Aktaş, Muhittin Karaman, Yusuf Uras, Sercan Öztürk, Cihan Yalçın, Oktay Canbaz, Emre Özelkan, Mustafa Kumral
abstract: The extensive surface ruptures created by the February 6, 2023, Kahramanmaraş earthquake sequence (Mw 7.7 and Mw 7.6) along the East Anatolian Fault Zone have provided data for the detailed evaluation of earthquake-induced hydrogeochemical responses in groundwater systems. This study investigates the spatial variability of groundwater responses in a structurally complex tectonic setting by assessing post-seismic changes in hot and cold springs using stable isotopes (δ18O and δ2H) and radioactive isotope (3H) data. The isotopic compositions indicate that the studied waters are mainly of meteoric origin and lie between the Global Meteoric Water Line and the Mediterranean Meteoric Water Line. Tritium data were further evaluated using a piston-flow model and Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis to provide a comparative assessment of apparent groundwater ages. Comparison of isotope data before and after the earthquake showed that the groundwater responses were very heterogeneous spatially. Three typical response patterns were identified: (i) large changes in tritium with no associated shifts in stable isotopes, (ii) large shifts in stable isotopes with no detectable changes in tritium, and (iii) no measurable change in either tracer. The different response patterns suggest that stable isotopes and tritium can be used as tracers for different characteristics of the groundwater system and may have different responses to seismic disturbances. Variable isotope responses were observed even for springs near the mapped surface rupture, suggesting that proximity to the rupture alone does not govern post-seismic hydrogeochemical behaviour. Instead, the observed responses reflect the influence of local geological and hydrogeological conditions on the groundwater systems. Results emphasise the utility of combining stable isotopes and tritium to characterise pre- to post-earthquake differences in groundwater systems and provide a regional isotopic baseline for future post-seismic hydrogeochemical studies in tectonically active areas.

title: Assessment of multi-driver human interventions on streamflow and its components based on information and complexity metrics
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Xinyue Du, Tian Lan, Huanhuan Li, Wenzhe Feng, Tianling Qiao, Tongyong Wang, Haoyan Wei, Huijie Li, Yanwei Lu
abstract: Human activities increasingly modify river systems, yet quantifying their independent and combined effects on streamflow remains challenging due to nonlinear, multi-driver interactions and time-lagged hydrological responses. This study proposes a framework that combines information-theoretic and complexity metrics to evaluate how diverse human interventions affect total streamflow and its components. Total streamflow was decomposed into fast-streamflow, intermediate interflow, slow-streamflow, and dry-weather flow through an improved multi-component streamflow separation method. Complex relationships between anthropogenic drivers and streamflow components were assessed through a Multi-Source Human Intervention Index (MSHI) derived from information-theoretic dependence, with human activities represented by remote-sensing indicators. Case-study results show that fast-streamflow and dry-weather flow are most sensitive to human activities, with mean MSHI values exceeding 0.6 in study cases. Night-time light and impervious surface percentage were the most influential drivers. Basin complexity was further employed to examine the consistency and interpretability of the assessment results. Building on these findings, this study provides a scalable approach for assessing the complex, nonlinear impacts of human interventions on river systems.

title: Influence of water network structure on regional water allocation under supply variability
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Yalin Zhang, Xin Li, Wenyan Wu, Lixiang Dong, Guohua Fang, Huayu Zhong
abstract: Regional water systems are increasingly shaped by interannual variability in allocatable water supply and growing interconnection across spatial scales. While existing studies primarily treat water availability as an exogenous constraint, the role of water network structure in conditioning allocation outcomes under variable supply remains insufficiently understood. This study treats regional water allocation as a structurally constrained process, in which network topology influences resource accessibility, transmission pathways, and redistribution capacity. An integrated framework has been developed to link supply uncertainty characterization, complex network-based structural representation, and multi-objective allocation modeling. Using the coupled system of the Taizhou water network and the Eastern Zhejiang Water Transfer Project as a case study, a series of water network structure scenarios have been constructed to represent different development pathways. Results show that network structure strongly affects allocation performance under supply variability: enhanced connectivity and path redundancy improve shortage mitigation and equity without increasing total supply, while also enabling more efficient utilization of externally introduced water resources. Moreover, the effects of supply expansion depend strongly on the underlying network configuration, highlighting the interdependence between infrastructure development and allocation outcomes. These findings indicate that water network structure strongly influences allocation performance and supply utilization under uncertainty. The proposed framework provides a systematic basis for evaluating structural interventions and supports the transition from supply-centric planning toward structure-informed optimization of regional water systems.

title: Energy mechanism and modeling of watershed water–sediment event variations on the Loess Plateau
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Lu Jia, Zhanbin Li, Mingjiang Deng, Kunxia Yu, Peng Li, Jiwei Zhu, Guoce Xu, Jiao Zhang, Shengde Yu, Siyi Tang
abstract: The Loess Plateau constitutes the primary sediment source of the Yellow River basin, where water–sediment event dynamics are shaped by complex interactions among erosion energy, terrain and human activities. Here, a research framework for watershed water–sediment events grounded in runoff erosion energy theory is developed, and applied to 16 typical watersheds across the Loess Plateau to elucidate the energy mechanisms underlying water–sediment event variations and improve the accuracy of sediment modelling. Quantitative analyses reveal that runoff erosion power, which quantifies event-scale runoff erosion energy acts as the primary driver of sediment load during event-scale water–sediment events, with the event-scale R2 for their relationship spanning 0.54 to 0.82, and its values exceeding 0.70 in 52% of the studied watersheds. This explanatory power far surpasses that of precipitation, for which the maximum R2 is less than 0.43, and runoff alone. Runoff surge shows an extremely significant positive correlation with sediment load, with R2 greater than 0.70 in 81.25% of watersheds (p < 0.001). Its integration into the energy-sediment model elevates simulation accuracy by an average of 10.98% and by as much as 26.79% in the most pronounced cases. In contrast, vegetation, characterized by the NDVI, exerts only a limited influence on sediment simulation and average contributes just 4.94% to the explained variance in sediment load. Runoff surge and runoff erosion power are identified as the primary drivers of sediment dynamics for watershed water–sediment events, with respective average contributions of 38.56% and 33.06% to the variance in sediment load. Parameters of the energy-sediment model display a nonlinear decrease–increase–decrease response to increasing watershed area, with two critical thresholds at 9400 km2 and 62,000 km2 governing shifts in their controlling factors. This work establishes a conceptual framework that links climate change and ecological restoration to watershed water-energy-sediment processes, delivering evidence-based insights to inform sustainable watershed management strategies in the Loess Plateau and analogous erodible regions worldwide.

title: Ecological water replenishment reshapes the spatiotemporal patterns of groundwater hydrochemistry in the North China plain
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Ziyue Yin, Jianfeng Wu, Xiaomin Sun, Jian Song, Yun Yang, Jichun Wu
abstract: Groundwater depletion and the associated ecological degradation have become critical challenges worldwide. Integrated water management and targeted policy interventions have proven effective in stabilizing or even restoring groundwater storage. However, the hydrochemical responses and potential environmental trade-offs associated with such interventions remain insufficiently understood. In this study, groundwater hydrochemical data from three key pilot river systems (i.e., the Hutuo, Fuyang, and South Juma Rivers) in the North China Plain (NCP) were analyzed for the period 2017–2019. Statistical analyses, principal component analysis, and non-metric multidimensional scaling were employed to examine groundwater hydrochemical changes associated with ecological water replenishment. The results revealed pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity in groundwater hydrochemical responses. Temporally, the groundwater system exhibited clear stage-dependent hydrochemical variations, with marked hydrochemical perturbation in 2018 followed by comparatively constrained adjustment in 2019. Spatially, hydrochemical responses varied substantially among river systems and aquifer types. Horizontally, distinct river-specific hydrochemical trajectories were observed: the Hutuo River groundwater system showed a relatively systematic longitudinal evolution, whereas the Fuyang River groundwater system displayed more fragmented and spatially reorganized hydrochemical hotspots. Vertically, the unconfined aquifer showed stronger and more stage-dependent hydrochemical variations, consistent with greater sensitivity to hydrodynamic perturbations, while the confined aquifer exhibited weaker and less systematic temporal differentiation. These findings indicate that evaluating groundwater restoration should extend beyond groundwater storage recovery to account for hydrochemical restructuring and associated water quality risks. This study provides a process-oriented basis for optimizing large-scale replenishment efforts and supports a quantity-quality coupled paradigm for long-term sustainability.

title: Assessing future soil erosion responses to freeze–thaw cycle representation in SWAT in the seasonally frozen Songhua River watershed
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Beibei Ding, Siying Huangyi, Junyu Qi, Srinivasulu Ale, Puyu Feng, De Li Liu, Raghavan Srinivasan, Yong Chen
abstract: Freeze-thaw cycles (FTCs) significantly contribute to the hydrological cycle and soil erosion in a seasonally frozen watershed in northeastern China, making their representative simulation essential. An enhanced Soil and Water Assessment Tool with a physically-based FTCs module (SWAT-FT) was applied to comprehensively investigate the impacts of future climate change on soil hydrothermal dynamics and soil erosion in the Songhua River watershed in northeastern China. The results demonstrated that SWAT-FT substantially improved soil temperature simulation throughout the year compared to the original SWAT, particularly during the freeze–thaw season. SWAT-FT simulated more realistic liquid soil water content (3-7 percentage points lower than the original SWAT) and consistently better streamflow performance during March to June. Unlike the original SWAT model, which uses a simple empirical soil temperature equation, SWAT-FT represents the insulation effect of snow cover and the soil water-phase changes during the freeze–thaw process, which is the reason for the improvements. These improvements further led to large differences in simulated hydrological and erosion responses. Consequently, the SWAT-FT model predicted substantially lower surface runoff (55%-57%) and soil erosion (34%-70%) than the original SWAT during the freeze–thaw season. Relative to the historical period, future global warming was projected to exacerbate soil and water loss, with the SWAT-FT model forecasting a 51% to 66% increase in surface runoff and a 91% to 292% increase in soil erosion under three SSP scenarios by the end of the 21st century. Overall, SWAT-FT provided a more physically based representation of soil hydrothermal dynamics and runoff partitioning, which in turn modified the MUSLE-based soil erosion estimates, thereby enhancing its applicability for soil and water conservation policymaking in cold regions worldwide.

title: Assessment of agricultural drought resilience in China based on coupled drought propagation and recovery processes
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Ziyi Yan, Zhiming Han, Limin Duan, Wenrui Zhang, Fang Yang, Dexin Cui, Xiaolan Yu, Hu Liu, Jianan Wang, Zhi Li
abstract: As extreme drought events become more frequent and intense, the recovery process has emerged as a critical component of drought risk assessment. However, existing studies have focused primarily on drought propagation, while the recovery process and its linkage to system resilience remain largely underexplored. Here we propose a logistic regression-based framework for identifying agricultural drought recovery thresholds. It incorporates initial soil moisture conditions to quantify the meteorological drought conditions required for agricultural drought to recover to normal conditions. Building on this framework, we construct a novel resilience indicator that integrates the propagation and recovery thresholds of agricultural drought. The results show that, compared with northwestern China, agricultural drought in southern China is more easily triggered by meteorological drought. Agricultural drought recovery thresholds and resilience exhibit a pronounced spatial pattern across China, with higher values in the northwest and lower values in the southeast. As initial soil moisture decreases, the standardized precipitation evapotranspiration index (SPEI) threshold required for agricultural drought recovery increases, whereas it gradually decreases with increasing lead time. Furthermore, the conditional probability of agricultural drought recovery rises markedly with higher SPEI thresholds. Agricultural drought resilience in China is predominantly governed by the propagation process. By coupling drought propagation and recovery processes, this study provides a new drought resilience indicator based on propagation and recovery thresholds. This framework provides a new perspective for assessing drought resilience and offers a scientific basis for refining drought risk assessment and improving the accuracy of drought early warning.

title: Grain size and thickness of event layers in relation to the flood magnitude: examples from floodplains in the middle and lower Yangtze River, China
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Xiu Juan Liu, Albert J. Kettner, Hui Ling Li, Feng Yang Min, Dao Sheng Wang
abstract: River floodplain deposition occurs typically when floodplains inundate. It is widely used for reconstructing historical floods. However, linking specific deposition event layers to specific flood magnitudes is still challenging. We analyzed the responses of suspended sediments and their sedimentary records to flood events of various magnitudes in the middle and lower Yangtze River. Results indicate that the 2020 large flood and 2012 and 2016 moderate floods do not cause coarsening of suspended sediment or increases of sand content in suspended sediment compared to the floods of smaller magnitudes. However, these three floods resulted in coarser and thicker flood event layers for the floodplains. The coarsest sections of event layers correspond to flood peak periods. We speculate and verify that both grain size and sand content of floodplain deposits correlate to flood magnitude by variation of the settling probability of different components of suspended sediment during high water discharge of moderate and large floods, rather than by changes in grain size composition of suspended sediment. In addition, the 2012 event deposition layer is thicker than the 2016 that was formed under higher flood magnitude conditions. This is most likely due to differences in sediment source areas for these two floods, i.e., event layer thickness of flood deposits is determined by both the magnitude and source area of flood event. These findings improve the understanding of the relationship between the characteristics of floodplain deposits and the magnitudes of flooding events, and accuracy of the interpretation of floodplain deposition.

title: Improvement and testing of the SWAT model for simulating hydrological processes and non-point source pollution in the paddy-dominated polder
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Haitao Wu, Zenglin Peng, Meng Xiang, Yufeng Luo, Yuanlai Cui
abstract: Paddy-dominated polders are critical agricultural landscapes in low-lying regions, where integrated irrigation-drainage management plays a decisive role in hydrological processes and non-point source (NPS) pollution dynamics. However, widely used watershed models like SWAT often oversimplify the unique structural and operational features of polders. This study developed SWAT-PP (SWAT for paddy-dominated polders) by incorporating key processes, including paddy water storage dynamics, sluice-gate-regulated water diversion, pumping-station-controlled drainage, and spatially distributed pond combinations. The SWAT-PP model was applied and tested in the Dongwan Polder (DWP) within China’s Chaohu Lake Basin. Results showed that SWAT‑PP effectively simulated field‑scale hydrology and nutrient dynamics (R2 > 0.6, NSE > 0.5, PBIAS 0.5, NSE > 0.4, PBIAS < 15%). Water balance analysis indicated that irrigation contributed nearly 30% of total inflow, with about 17% of diverted water returning to ditches as tailwater. Nutrient source apportionment revealed that external river diversion and sediment resuspension each accounted for roughly 10% of total TN/TP loads, while ponds retained approximately 80%–90% of nutrients from residential runoff. SWAT-PP provides a promising tool for simulating coupled hydrological and water quality processes in polder systems, supporting improved water management and NPS pollution control in these vulnerable agro-hydrological settings.

title: Leveraging deep learning and kernel density representations for transformation-based regional flood frequency analysis
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Sukhsehaj Kaur, Sagar Rohidas Chavan
abstract: This paper leverages deep learning (DL) and kernel density representations to determine design flood estimates at ungauged or sparsely gauged sites through transformation-based regional flood frequency analysis (T_RFFA) approach. A critical preliminary step in conventional RFFA approaches is to identify an appropriate regional frequency distribution through an effective regional goodness-of-fit (GOF) test. However, conventional regional GOF tests involve sample mean–based normalization of at-site peak flow data, which can violate key assumptions of RFFA. To address this, the proposed method reformulates regional GOF test as a classification problem wherein peak flow data from each site are transformed into a dimensionless space using mathematical transformations. Kernel density estimator (KDE) plots are then generated and used as inputs to a pre-trained Deep Neural Network (DNN) classifier that selects the most suitable regional distribution among the five widely recognized peak flow distributions, viz., Generalized Extreme Value, Generalized Pareto, Generalized Logistic, Generalized Normal, and Pearson Type 3 distributions. The DNN classifier achieved classification accuracies of 95.09% and 94.86% on training and test datasets, respectively. The effectiveness of the proposed DL-based RFFA approach is evaluated through Monte Carlo simulation experiments and real-world applications to catchments in the United States and peninsular India. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach yields comparable or better design flood estimates relative to conventional T_RFFA approach. Furthermore, the proposed DL-based GOF test is observed to be approximately 18 to 27 times faster than the conventional L-moment-based approach, offering a computationally efficient and robust alternative for RFFA.

title: Multi-scale mapping of GDEs from remote sensing and field surveys in the Urumqi River–Chaiwopu Basin
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Ye Zhihao, Zhou Qiang, Zheng Mingxia, Zhang Peng, Sun Hao, Zhang Xiaoyu, Zhou Xin, He Liansheng, Huang Longhao, Meng Rui
abstract: Groundwater-Dependent Ecosystems (GDEs) are widely distributed in arid and semi-arid regions and provide critical ecological services. However, their precise identification and mapping remain challenging due to insufficient integration of geospatial technologies with field measurement techniques. This study selected the terminal year of a prolonged drought and the most recent year for analysis, covering the period 2001–2023. We employed key indicators including Fractional Vegetation Cover (FVC), the difference between evapotranspiration and precipitation (ET-P), the Terrain Wetness Index (TWI), and the Vegetation Groundwater Accessibility Index (VGUI). The K-means clustering algorithm was applied for classification, and spatial overlay analysis was conducted in the Urumqi River–Chaiwopu Basin in Xinjiang, China, to assess the spatial distribution and temporal variations of GDEs. The results were validated by integrating wetland distribution data with field investigations. The findings indicate that areas classified as “likely” or “very likely” GDEs are predominantly concentrated around Dongdao Haizi, Chaiwopu Lake, the salt lakes, and adjacent regions, covering 45.4% of the potential area (4,197.89 km2). Wetland-based validation yielded a producer’s accuracy of 84.1%. Over time, the area classified as “unlikely” or “very unlikely” for GDEs showed an increasing trend. After incorporating VGUI, the likelihood class decreased across 41.0% of the typical areas, with cultivated and built-up land accounting for 64.9% of this decrease. By incorporating field-based VGUI data, the study reduced interference from anthropogenic factors such as irrigation in the identification of GDEs within typical areas, enabling refined mapping.

title: Controls on carbon and nutrient transport in a tidal creek across a coastal forest-marsh transition under sea-level rise
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Nathaniel Spicer, Brian Moyer, Dannielle Pratt, Holly A. Michael, Ashleigh R. Montgomery, Angelia L. Seyfferth, Katherine Tully
abstract: Sea level rise (SLR) and saltwater intrusion (SWI) drive ecological and biogeochemical changes in coastal forests that alter solute fluxes between marshes and estuaries. Tidal creeks mediate transport of carbon (C), iron (Fe), and nitrogen (N) during flood and ebb tides, yet quantifying elemental fluxes is challenging due to bidirectional tidal flow and frequent bank overtopping. We quantified surface-water transport of C, Fe, and N during spring tides and storm events (2022–2023) in a tidal creek draining a transitioning coastal forest along the Delaware Bay. Discharge was estimated using a novel rating-curve model that incorporates bank overtopping dynamics. Groundwater wells and redox probes along a marsh-to-forest transect monitored water table elevation, salinity, and redox potential. We observed net imports of dissolved organic carbon (DOC), dissolved organic nitrogen (DON), dissolved Fe, and ammonium (NH4-N). DOC hourly loads were positively correlated with dissolved Fe loads, suggesting microbial dissolution of C-bearing Fe oxides during flood tides, and re-precipitation and C retention on ebb tides. Plant uptake and nitrification drove NH4-N and DON imports, as plant uptake during high tide could remove N from the water column. There was no import or export of nitrate (NO3-N), but NO3-N hourly loads were positively correlated with marsh redox potential, consistent with denitrification under reduced conditions. As the coastal zone responds to accelerating SLR, dissolution of Fe protected C will inhibit C sequestration and marsh loss to SLR could increase N delivery to coastal waters as plants uptake less N, with downstream implications for eutrophication.

title: Dual urban runoff response to urbanization and contradictory precipitation trends driven by climate change
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Raz Nussbaum, Moshe Armon, Efrat Morin
abstract: Urban flooding poses a growing threat to cities worldwide, driven by the compounding effects of climate change and urbanization. This study examines the effect of urbanization and contradictory precipitation trends, defined as increasing storm intensity and decreasing total precipitation, on urban runoff. Analyzing CMIP6 projections, we show that contradictory precipitation is projected to impact 26% of urban areas globally. To examine how these trends manifest at finer scales, we analyze changes in heavy precipitation events at both regional and catchment scales using convection-permitting WRF simulations. Their hydrological implications are then assessed using a calibrated SWMM urban runoff model driven by an ensemble of over 5,300 spatially shifted simulations. We find that future storms become more spatially confined while their short-duration maximal intensities increase at both regional and catchment scales. Consequently, from a catchment-scale hydrological perspective, weak runoff peaks become weaker, while strong peaks become stronger, a pattern that is amplified by urbanization. Furthermore, peak runoff is increasingly governed by short-duration rainfall intensities under future conditions, an effect amplified by urbanization. Additionally, we suggest a mechanism whereby more compact future storms suppress runoff when they miss the catchment, yet amplify peaks when they overlap with it. Concurrently, drier antecedent conditions suppress runoff from weak events while intense bursts rapidly exceed infiltration and storage capacities. This contrasting urban hydrological response to climate change poses a critical challenge for urban flood management.

title: Spatial heterogeneity and drivers of PFASs distribution in an arid-semiarid city waters system
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Xuemei Zhu, Wenjing Sun, Ying Sun, Xiaotao Fu, Bing Sun, Yihan Li, Changwei Lü, Shenghu Zhang, Xin Wang, Chengmei Liao
abstract: Investigating the occurrence of emerging per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) in diverse urban surface water bodies of Hohhot, a representative arid and semi-arid city, is essential for understanding their environmental behavior and potential ecological risks under water-scarce conditions. This study systematically characterized the occurrence, spatial distribution, compositional profiles, and environmental factors associated with the spatial heterogeneity of PFASs. The concentrations of ΣPFASs exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity (6.3–81.4 ng/L), with elevated levels observed in water bodies more strongly influenced by anthropogenic activities. PFASs compositional profiles differed among water body types, with short-chain PFASs constituting a substantial proportion of the overall PFASs composition. Long-chain PFASs nevertheless remained widely detectable across the studied waters. PFASs covaried with multiple hydrochemical characteristics, but these associations weakened after accounting for functional water-body type, highlighting water-body differentiation as an important context for PFASs spatial heterogeneity. Despite the higher concentrations of short-chain PFASs in several water bodies, ecological risk was primarily associated with residual long-chain PFASs, particularly perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS). Collectively, these findings highlight the need for source-oriented monitoring and region-specific PFASs management in arid–semi-arid urban watersheds, while the potential influence of hydroclimatic conditions requires quantitative hydrological validation.

title: Understanding hydrological drought recovery patterns in a changing environment: Insights from a non-stationary multivariate analysis
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Yeting Chen, Tao Peng, Vijay P. Singh, Ji Liu, Xiaohua Dong, Qingxia Lin, Jiali Guo, Chao Song, Changwen Li, Yinghai Li, Dan Yu, Chong Wei, Yan Huang
abstract: Understanding hydrological drought recovery under non‑stationary conditions is critical for water management in a changing environment, yet remains poorly quantified. This study presented a novel grid‑based, daily‑scale framework that integrated non‑stationary drought identification, multivariate probabilistic recovery assessment, and machine learning driver analysis. Applied to the four sub‑basins of the Dongting Lake basin (DLB), a non‑stationary Standardized Runoff Index (NSRI) was constructed using the GAMLSS framework with large‑scale climate indices as covariates. Drought recovery characteristics, including recovery time, water requirement (WR), and recovery probability, were estimated using run theory and a copula‑Bayesian approach, with random forest (RF) used to rank the influencing factors. Results showed that NSRI captured drought onset and peak more sensitively than the stationary SRI. The average recovery time ranged from 83.5 days in the Zi River (ZR) to 97.3 days in the Li River (LR), revealing notable spatial heterogeneity across the basin. WR increased sharply under severe and extreme drought conditions, while recovery probability dropped below 0.61 for extreme drought.
