Thermodynamic calculations further showed that Stage I nucleation barriers favored Lp and Gt over direct Mt formation, whereas during Stage II, higher temperature enhanced the nucleation driving force and lowered the nucleation barrier for Lp-to-Mt conversion, while the corresponding thermodynamic parameters for Lp-to-Gt conversion remained nearly unchanged. Fe(II) speciation further showed that higher temperatures promoted Fe(II) adsorption and structural Fe(II) incorporation, facilitating the formation of mixed-valence Mt. The delayed appearance of Mt after Lp accumulation, together with rapid Lp consumption and enhanced Fe(II) incorporation, indicates that temperature-promoted Mt formation proceeds mainly through dissolution-reprecipitation rather than direct Fh-to-Mt solid-state conversion or oriented-attachment-dominated growth. The resulting Mt particles displayed temperature-dependent morphological and magnetic characteristics. These findings demonstrate that moderate warming expands the Fe(II)aq window for Mt formation by altering both the thermodynamic accessibility and kinetic competition of secondary mineralization pathways, providing new constraints for predicting Fe mineral phase selection in thermally dynamic biogeochemical environments.

title: From source to sink: complex dual role of the Kairei hydrothermal plume in deep ocean trace metal cycling at the Central Indian Ridge
description: Publication date: Available online 21 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Nico Fröhberg, Katja Schmidt, Sandra Poehle, Ignacio Pedre, Maren Walter, Jonathan Mette, Sebastian Fuchs, Dieter Garbe-Schönberg, Charlotte Kleint, Andrea Koschinsky
abstract: Hydrothermal venting represents a significant source of trace metals to the deep ocean, but key aspects of these fluxes remain poorly constrained. Whether high-temperature hydrothermal venting at a particular site represents a net source for fluid-sourced trace metals to the open ocean is determined by complex processes during plume mixing, which can also make them sinks for (seawater-derived) elements. We present a comprehensive dataset of dissolved trace metals (Cd, Co, Cu, Fe, Ga, Mn, Mo, Ni, Pb, U, V, and REY) for endmember fluids and from water column profiles covering the buoyant plume and the non-buoyant plume up to 30 km away from the mixed ultramafic/mafic-hosted Kairei Hydrothermal Field (KHF) at the Central Indian Ridge and a background station at 56 km distance. The non-buoyant plume was sampled with a newly developed autonomous trace metal rosette (TMR) for contamination-free hydrocasts. The KHF acts as a significant source of Fe, Mn, Co, and to a lesser degree of Ga to the deep Indian Ocean, with size fractionation revealing Fe being present predominantly as small particles (53 % at 0.2–0.8 µm) and large colloids (28 % at 0.015–0.2 µm) which are removed quickly near the source, while the soluble fraction (<0.015 µm) is more stable and exported to the deep ocean. Similarly, Pb was found to be largely present in the small particulate fraction (95 %) close to the source and being rapidly removed as particulate sulfides with little effect on dissolved concentrations, while all other investigated elements were found largely in the soluble fraction (<0.015 µm). Conversely, the plume effectively scavenges REY, V, and notably Cd from the water column as well as the fluid-sourced contributions, with near-quantitative Cd removal observed in the plume despite ∼100-fold endmember enrichment. Copper and Ni exhibit complex non-conservative behavior, both being depleted relative to background seawater in the near-field, likely reflecting initial sulfide precipitation; Cu is subsequently re-enriched in the far-field via oxidative release during plume aging, while any comparable Ni release likely falls below our detection limit given its lower endmember concentration, making the plume an apparent net sink for Ni. The relatively low H2S/Fe ratio of 0.90 at Kairei compared to other hydrothermal systems likely favors greater metal transport to the water column. These findings demonstrate that hydrothermal contributions to marine trace metal budgets are highly system-specific, controlled by endmember chemistry and plume processes, highlighting the need for detailed multi-element investigations across diverse hydrothermal settings.

title: Metal complexions in growth-related crystal defects in pyrite
description: Publication date: Available online 20 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Lin Yang, Qingfei Wang, Denis Fougerouse, Steven M. Reddy, Huajian Li, Kunfeng Qiu, Qihai Shu, William D.A. Rickard, Yiwei Song, Paul Guagliardo, David W. Saxey, Chaoyi Dong, Yushan Zeng, Xiao Sun, Jun Deng
abstract: Element segregation into crystal defects formed during mineral growth rather than post-growth deformation is of fundamental interest in earth science but remains poorly understood. The micro-, to nano-scale textures and geochemical composition of pyrite from a gold deposit were studied to elucidate crystal defect-mediated element segregation. The pyrite consists of a core and a rim, with tetrahedrite inclusions distributed between the two. Our findings reveal a series of planar defects (with low angle misorientation >0.3°) consistent with plane in the pyrite rim. The characteristics of the defects indicate that they are nucleated due to the lattice mismatch during overgrowth of pyrite on the tetrahedrite. Nanoscale observations indicate the presence of a separate interstitial Sb–Cu-bearing inclusion along the planar and linear crystal defects. The interstitial inclusion has a cubic crystal structure and is enriched in Au and other trace elements like Ni, Cu, Sb, Pb, and Bi, with a combined concentrations reaching 8.6 at.%. Such composition cannot be attributed to any definitive mineral phase and is thus interpreted as phase-like, stable complexions. The thermodynamic modelling reveals that the pyrite with trace element-bearing defects formed at ∼250 °C under pH of 3.8 to 4.6 and logfO2 of –36.0 to –31.8 conditions. Lack of visible Au within the studied pyrite indicates that Au was segregated into these complexions from undersaturated ore fluids, revealing a growth-related, defect-driven incorporation mechanism of Au. These tetrahedrite and metal-rich complexions may act as a precursor for the Au nanoparticles or other sulfide inclusions in pyrite during superposed deformation and mineralization. This study highlights that the role of the growth-induced defects in the element segregation may be underestimated in previous studies.

title: The role of sediments in calc-alkaline differentiation of thickened arc magmas and bulk crust compositions
description: Publication date: Available online 18 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Jun Wang, Chris J. Hawkesworth, Qiang Wang, Peng Sun, Wan-Long Hu, Shaohao Zou
abstract: Calc-alkaline magmas in thickened arcs (>45 km) are characterized by ultra iron (Fe) depletion, having lower FeO contents at a given MgO content than those in thinner arcs, and this is a feature of bulk continental crust. Previous interpretations of ultra-Fe depletion have focused on closed-system differentiation of mantle-derived magmas, but magmatic flare-ups during crustal thickening result in ultra-Fe depletion in open systems incorporating fertile crustal materials from retroarc underthrusting. We evaluate ultra-Fe depletion in a garnet-bearing magmatic flare-up in the Tethyan arc and a global database of arc lavas and arclogitic garnets with thermodynamic-geochemical modeling. Our case study shows that thickened arc magmas undergo sediment assimilation and garnet crystallization at ∼1 GPa. The important role of sediment assimilation in thickened arc magmas is further supported by global Sr–Nd–O isotopic data. Magma differentiation at relatively shallow depths (<45 km or 1.2 GPa) is essential for reproducing the range of Dy/Yb and La/Yb ratios observed in global thickened arc magmas, because it suppresses early garnet crystallization and limits the extent of late garnet crystallization. The late crystallization of minor amounts of garnet (<5 wt%) from low-MgO (<4 wt%) magmas exerts little effect on magma oxidation. The lack of early garnet crystallization indicates that garnet has no bearing on the early Fe depletion in high-MgO magmas. At depths of <45 km, assimilated felsic rather than more mafic sediments, would have lower densities than the basaltic magma, and this low-density sediment barrier confines magma stagnation and differentiation to this depth interval. Integrating previous interpretations of the tectono-magmatic cyclicity in Cordilleran arcs, we propose that felsic sediments were underthrust into the deep crust during crustal thickening, thereby fueling flare-ups of ultra-Fe-depleted magmas. These felsic sediments may represent residues left after the loss of mafic components from ancient retroarc continents due to prolonged chemical weathering. Our results highlight that intracrustal recycling of highly weathered, felsic sediments provides a significant control on the development of ultra-Fe-depleted calc-alkaline magmas in thickened arcs, emphasizing the role of weathering in the generation of bulk continental crust.

title: Multiple lithium sites in kaolinite revealed by high-resolution 7 Li nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) calculations
description: Publication date: Available online 16 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yan Wang, Shifeng Dai, David French, Ian Graham, Yu Liu
abstract: Lithium (Li) is a critical metal resource underpinning the development of the new energy sector and constitutes an essential material basis for green technologies such as Li-ion batteries, energy storage systems, and electric vehicles. As the global energy system accelerates towards decarbonization, the strategic importance of Li resources and market demand continue to increase. Clay-hosted Li in coal-bearing strata has therefore attracted increasing attention as a potentially important Li reservoir. Here, we combine high-resolution 7Li magic-angle spinning nuclear magnetic resonance (7Li MAS NMR) spectroscopy with density functional theory (DFT) calculations to resolve the local environments and migration characteristics of Li in natural kaolinite from Li-enriched coal-bearing strata. The experimental 7Li MAS NMR spectra first revealed multiple distinguishable Li local environments in the natural kaolinite-bearing sample. However, because spectral deconvolution alone cannot uniquely determine the corresponding crystallographic sites, representative Li-bearing kaolinite configurations were independently constructed according to the crystal structure of kaolinite, available structural sites, Li–O coordination requirements, charge-compensation considerations, and crystal-chemical plausibility. These configurations include octahedral substitutional Li ( L i s u b ), interlayer and siloxane-hole-related Li ( L i i n t and L i h o l e ), and several defect complexes ( L i s u b + i n t , L i s u b + h o l e , L i i n t + h o l e , L i s u b + i n t + h o l e , L i s u b + 2 H ). DFT calculations were then performed to evaluate their relative binding energies, local coordination environments, migration barriers, and isotropic chemical shifts. The experimental 7Li MAS NMR spectra and peak deconvolution results were subsequently used to constrain the interpretation of the theoretically predicted Li local environments through a three-band calibration scheme spanning low-, intermediate-, and high-shift regions. The combined spectroscopic and computational results indicate that Li is predominantly hosted at octahedral substitutional sites, which define the principal Li reservoir and are characterized by low chemical shifts, strong shielding, and a relatively stable lattice framework. A smaller but spectroscopically resolvable fraction of Li occurs in interlayer/siloxane-hole-related environments and associated defect complexes, generating intermediate- to high-shift components that reflect structurally perturbed local environments governed by multisite coupling. DFT-derived migration pathways further suggest that L i s u b is the most stable and least mobile Li configuration, whereas L i i n t and L i h o l e -related environments represent subordinate configurations subject to distinct energetic and kinetic constraints. These results establish a lattice-scale framework for understanding Li storage and local migration in kaolinite from coal-bearing strata and provide new constraints on Li occurrence mechanisms and resource potential in clay-rich coal systems.

title: Microbial substrate formation via thermal alteration of organic matter in sediments of the Nankai Trough
description: Publication date: Available online 16 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Victoria Kürzinger, Verena B. Heuer, Christian T. Hansen, Wolfgang Bach, Shuchai Gan, Kai-Uwe Hinrichs
abstract: Deep marine sediments play a critical role in global biogeochemical cycles, serving as a vast reservoir of organic carbon. Carbon turnover in these environments is governed by biotic and abiotic processes, with high temperatures promoting the latter. To determine the upper temperature limit of life in the deep biosphere, it is necessary to distinguish between thermal limits and energy constrains. Although microorganisms are known to be able to survive at the putative temperature limit of up to 122°C, it remains unclear whether this is due to a fundamental temperature limit or to insufficient in-situ productions of metabolic substrates at higher temperatures. In particular, the temperature dependence of abiotic formation of low-molecular-weight organic compounds, which are important substrates for microbial metabolism, is essentially unknown. To investigate the abiotic formation of low-molecular-weight substrates and their implications for carbon cycling in organic-poor sediments, we conducted hydrous pyrolysis experiments under high-pressure (25 MPa) and high-temperature (150‒250°C) conditions. A sediment sample from International Ocean Discovery Program Site C0023 in the Nankai Trough was chosen for the experiments (i.e., 88°C, see “Materials and Methods”), where in-situ temperatures reach 120°C at 1.2 km sediment depth. The experimental approach was combined with geochemical analyses followed by thermodynamic modeling to rate the abiotic formation of low-molecular-weight organics as potential substrates for microbial metabolism under high-pressure and high-temperature conditions. Experimental results revealed elevated concentrations of dissolved inorganic carbon and hydrogen relative to in-situ porewaters. In contrast, acetate and CH4 concentrations remained below those measured in genuine porewater samples. Acetate appears to function both as a degradation product of longer-chain compounds and as a precursor for smaller molecules such as CO2 and CH4. The low CH4 concentrations produced during the experiments relative to in-situ conditions can be explained by the absence of active methanogenic microorganisms that convert acetate or CO2 to CH4. Furthermore, isotopic analyses revealed that CH4 produced experimentally exhibits a distinct abiotic δ 13C signature around −34‰, in contrast to the microbial CH4 observed in the Nankai Trough sediments. Dissolved organic matter shows a clear decrease in oxygen- and sulfur-bearing compounds with increasing temperature. This trend reflects enhanced thermal decarboxylation and breakdown of thiols, thioethers and thiophene structures, releasing volatile sulfur species, predominantly H2S. These results indicate that abiotic reactions in deep marine sediments can provide a limited supply of metabolic substrates even near and beyond the currently known thermal limit of life. This implies that substrate availability, rather than temperature alone, may contribute to defining the upper boundary of the deep biosphere.

title: Experimental constraints on niobium mobility and pyrochlore crystallization in evolved carbonatite liquids
description: Publication date: Available online 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Qi Li, Xiao-Chun Li, Xue-Yin Yuan, Daniel E. Harlov, Hong-Rui Fan, Xian-Hua Li, Ming-Guo Zhai
abstract: Carbonatite-related niobium (Nb) deposits account for the majority of global Nb resources, with pyrochlore [(Ca,Na)Nb2O6(F,OH)] as the principal Nb-hosting phase. Pyrochlore is commonly regarded as an early-crystallized magmatic mineral in carbonatite, yet it is increasingly reported from late-stage, highly evolved lithologies. As Nb is commonly considered to be relatively immobile in H2O-rich media, the extent to which highly evolved, H2O-rich liquids enhance Nb mobility and govern pyrochlore crystallization remains poorly constrained in carbonatite systems. To address this issue, we conducted hydrothermal diamond anvil cell experiments to investigate pyrochlore dissolution and precipitation in alkali-rich (Na, K) solutions containing various salt components (carbonate, bicarbonate, fluoride, chloride, and sulfate), chemically analogous to evolved carbonatite melts. Pyrochlore was nearly insoluble in SO4 2-- and Cl--rich liquids throughout the heating process even at ∼ 850 °C. In contrast, CO3 2–- and F--rich liquids induced pyrochlore dissolution at much lower temperatures (590–705 °C). Using dissolution temperature as a qualitative indicator of Nb mobility, these results demonstrate that carbonate and fluoride are highly effective components promoting Nb mobility. For liquids containing the same type of volatile component, pyrochlore exhibited lower dissolution temperatures in K-rich than in Na-rich systems, because Na+ can stabilize the crystal lattice of pyrochlore and retard its breakdown. In experiments showing substantial Nb dissolution, Nb-rich precipitates formed upon liquid cooling were further characterized. Pyrochlore crystallized only from F- and Na-rich systems, whereas Na-rich but F-poor liquids produced lueshite (NaNbO3) and F- and Na-poor liquids yielded fersmite (CaNb2O6). Chemical variations in liquid also affect pyrochlore composition, with increased Na/Ca ratio of the liquid enhancing Na, REE, and U incorporation into pyrochlore. These findings provide the first direct experimental evidence that highly evolved carbonatite melts or brine-melts can sustain appreciable Nb mobility and precipitate pyrochlore, thereby expanding the formation window for pyrochlore beyond early magmatic crystallization.

title: Hydrothermal experiments reveal methanol, ammonia, and methylamines as tracers of pH and temperature with potential application to Enceladus, Europa, and other icy ocean worlds
description: Publication date: Available online 13 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Kirtland J. Robinson, Everett L. Shock, Sean P. Sylva, Jeffrey S. Seewald
abstract: Icy ocean worlds in our solar system are prime targets in the search for extraterrestrial life. Enceladus and Europa are icy moons with evidence of global subsurface oceans in contact with rocky interiors, which may provide habitable environments for chemotrophic life. However, the interaction between water and rock and any changes in fluid chemistry are poorly constrained because the icy shells of these moons inhibit direct sampling of subsurface aqueous environments. Characterization of subseafloor processes may depend on chemical signatures in materials that are transported to accessible sampling locations near the surfaces of these icy ocean worlds. Here we present a theoretical framework where organic compounds likely to be present at icy ocean worlds can be utilized as tracers of geochemistry if they approach metastable equilibrium abundances, which we test with laboratory experiments. We use thermodynamic calculations of aqueous solutions to demonstrate that abundances of methanol, ammonia, and methylamines (compounds selected based on Enceladus’ plume data) should approach steady state ratios based on reversible substitution reactions that are systematically controlled by pH and temperature. We test these calculations by performing laboratory hydrothermal experiments ranging in temperature (175-325℃) and pH (∼3.5–7.0), demonstrating that chemical concentration measurements alone can be used in predictive models to accurately constrain the different conditions across experimental systems. As examples, with experiments conducted at 250℃, we demonstrate that the chemical tracers in a pH ∼ 3.5 solution predict a pH ≤ ∼5.0 and a temperature of ∼ 225-250℃, while the tracers in a solution at pH ∼ 7.0 predict a pH of ∼ 6.0–7.5 and a temperature of ∼ 200-275℃. Notably, all of our high-temperature experiments are cooled to room temperature prior to analysis, indicating that the hydrothermal signal (i.e., the ratio of chemical species) is preserved due to the slowing of reaction kinetics at lower temperatures, which may be analogous to hydrothermal fluids that vent into icy oceans. Similarly, we also performed a partial-cooling experiment that shows a tracer signal produced at 325℃ remains largely preserved for a year after the experiment was cooled to 175℃. We compare experimental results from gold reaction vessels to experiments previously conducted in glass vessels to assess the effects of experimental vessel type and find only minor differences in product distributions over time. Overall, our findings provide additional motivation to target small organic molecules for analysis on future missions to icy ocean worlds in order to constrain subsurface geochemical parameters critical to habitability

title: The iron mineralogy of Bennu samples: similarities and variations among CI chondritic materials
description: Publication date: Available online 11 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Kana Amano, Jean-Christophe Viennet, Pierre Beck, Sergey Yaroslavtsev, Dimitrios Bessas, Aleksandr Chumakov, Jean-Philippe Celse, Ludovic Delbes, Tomoki Nakamura, Yuma Enokido, Kanako Sakamoto, Shogo Tachibana, Mathieu Roskosz
abstract: Recent findings from sample-return missions targeting carbonaceous asteroids suggest that CI-like (Carbonaceous Ivuna-type) small bodies are more common in the solar system than previously thought. However, the general redox characteristics and variations among CI materials remain largely unexplored due to their limited availability on Earth. Moreover, CI meteorites have likely undergone irreversible terrestrial oxidation, resulting in modifications of the iron speciation and the redox states. In this context, the iron mineralogy of samples from the carbonaceous asteroid Bennu allows us to reassess the redox conditions of CI materials during its formation. We performed X-ray diffraction and Mössbauer spectroscopy of two Bennu particles from the hummocky group, as well as Oued Chebeika 002 CI meteorite. We compare their iron speciation to that of other CI and CI-like materials, including samples from the asteroid Ryugu, Orgueil CI meteorite, and Oued Chebeika 002 CI meteorite. The results show that Bennu particles contain substantial amounts of Fe sulfides (pyrrhotite, mackinawite, and pentlandite), along with Fe oxide (magnetite) and Fe-bearing (Mg-rich) phyllosilicates, similar to Ryugu samples. Cryogenic Mössbauer analysis indicates no significant contribution from ferric oxyhydroxides (i.e., ferrihydrite) in Bennu and Oued Chebeika 002 samples, confirming the previous electron microscopy observations of those samples. These observations imply that Fe3+ forming ferrihydrite observed in historical CI meteorites (e.g., Orgueil, Alais) results from long-term terrestrial oxidation of Fe2+ in sulfides, especially submicron-sized ones. This further strengthens the view that the actual CI materials and their formation environments are less oxidizing than previously estimated from old CI meteorite falls. The Fe3+/(Fe3++Fe2+) ratios in phyllosilicates in the hummocky particles range from 50 to 70%, indicating local heterogeneity within individual particles. Whereas similar values have been reported for Bennu samples (determined by X-ray Absorption Near-Edge Structure spectroscopy), Ryugu samples, and Oued Chebeika 002 samples (i.e., ∼50–65% of Fe3+/(Fe3++Fe2+)phyllosilicates), there may be slightly Fe3+-rich sub-regions (close to ∼70%) in our Bennu particles. Furthermore, we found two distinct mineral assemblages among CI and CI-like materials: (i) relatively well-crystallized phyllosilicates without mackinawite but with pyrrhotite, and (ii) disordered phyllosilicates coexisting with mackinawite, a metastable Fe sulfide. The latter finding is consistent with recent studies of mackinawite in Bennu and Ryugu samples, which suggest its formation at the early stages of CI alteration. Together with previous studies of Bennu, Ryugu, and Orgueil samples, our results suggest that different phyllosilicate assemblages preserve distinct Fe valence states, potentially recording redox conditions associated with different stages of formation. The CI materials have conventionally been regarded as relatively equilibrated and homogeneous, however, our results demonstrate the potential of combining clay mineral crystallinity and Fe valence states to unravel formation histories at a finer scale.

title: The importance of deep reactions between ascending komatiite and pre-existing protocratonic lithosphere for the chemistry of Archaean peridotites and greenstone belt volcanics: insights from reaction experiments
description: Publication date: Available online 9 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Rodrigo Freitas Rodrigues, Balz S. Kamber, Gregory M. Yaxley, Emma L. Tomlinson, Sandra Piazolo, Nathan R. Daczko
abstract: The cratonic lithospheric mantle is the buoyant 200–250 km deep root that enabled ancient continents (cratons) to survive for billions of years. The root stabilised due to extensive melting, erupting magnesian magmas at surface. However, peridotite xenolith samples from the cratonic mantle exhibit far more variable olivine/orthopyroxene and MgO/SiO2 ratios than expected from residues after melting of fertile mantle, exemplified by enigmatic dunites and orthopyroxene-rich harzburgites. Similarly, Archaean ultramafic lavas (komatiites) also show wider MgO/SiO2 variability than could be expected from shallow olivine fractionation. In addition, many komatiites have unexpectedly complex radiogenic isotope systematics, inconsistent with high-degree melting of refractory mantle. Thermodynamic modelling has suggested that these complexities could arise during deep (2–5 GPa) melt-solid reactions. Here, we present high-pressure layered experiments (3 GPa) involving the reaction between komatiite juxtaposed against harzburgite. The melt-bearing reactions yielded layered charges, wherein the initial komatiite layer (original, unreacted composition) was transformed into orthopyroxene-rich harzburgite following the reaction, and the original harzburgite layer resulted in the formation of dunite, with mineral modes and Mg-number depending on temperature. The solid residues of the reacted layers (orthopyroxene-rich and olivine-rich) are compositionally and mineralogically analogous to natural cratonic harzburgites and dunites, respectively. Thermodynamic modelling indicates that the MgO/SiO2 variability of the residues could be further increased by reacting the komatiite with fertile lherzolite instead of harzburgite. Solid-melt reactions markedly altered the composition of the incoming komatiite melt, with basaltic komatiite and komatiitic basalt formed at lower temperatures and modified high-Mg komatiites at higher temperatures. The melts exhibit the very wide range of MgO/SiO2 seen in ultramafic lavas in Archaean greenstone belts. Consideration of rare earth element and Hf partitioning suggests that assimilation of protocratonic ancient harzburgite into invading komatiite will be much more strongly seen in radiogenic Hf than Nd (or Ce) isotope ratios. Although both the original solid (harzburgite) and the incoming melt (komatiite) are ultramafic, their chemical contrast is sufficient to drive metasomatic reaction, likely partly due to the presence of a percolating melt. The reactions require higher temperatures than attained in the post-Archaean mantle, explaining both the sharp demise of komatiites after 2.5 Ga and the highly refractory nature of Archaean harzburgites and dunites. Ancient proto-cratonic mantle is one plausible candidate harbouring radiogenic signatures of Hadean silicate differentiation. The reason why these signatures are most commonly found in Archaean mafic and ultramafic igneous rocks may relate to the secular drop in maximum plume temperature, which has compromised the capacity of younger melts to sample this reservoir via assimilation

title: Negative 182 W anomalies in geochemically-depleted kimberlites reveal a common primordial component
description: Publication date: Available online 8 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Nao Nakanishi, Andrea Giuliani, D. Graham Pearson, Lori Willhite, Richard J. Walker
abstract: Certain kimberlites from worldwide localities are characterized by small negative μ182W anomalies (Nakanishi et al., 2021), where μ182W is the part per million difference in 182W/184W between sample and standards. This study re-evaluates the origin of the isotopically anomalous reservoir accessed by these kimberlites by analyzing an expanded range of kimberlites. Because Nd-Hf isotopic compositions are affected by crustal and lithospheric mantle contamination, which could also strongly attenuate an anomalous μ182W value, kimberlite samples with the highest initial 143Nd/144Nd and 176Hf/177Hf ratios, and therefore least affected by the addition of subducted or assimilated lithospheric material, may provide the most accurate constraint on the μ182W value of the anomalous reservoir. New W isotope data for 18 kimberlites from seven regions with variable Nd-Hf isotope compositions are reported. These kimberlites, combined with data from the prior study, indicate a broad correlation between μ182W and initial 143Nd/144Nd and 176Hf/177Hf ratios, projecting to an anomalous endmember composition with a μ182W value of ∼−8 at the highest initial 143Nd/144Nd and 176Hf/177Hf ratios. The inferred endmember μ182W value requires that the anomalous W signature originated in a reservoir isolated from the bulk silicate Earth very early in Earth history. Similar to proposed explanations for negative μ182W values in some modern ocean island basalts (OIBs), the isotopically anomalous mantle domain was most likely either infused with core-derived W characterized by strongly negative μ182W, or created as the result of silicate fractionation during the first 60 Myr of Solar System history, for example during magma ocean crystallization. Regardless of the origin of the anomalous W, the observations support an interpretation that some kimberlites and modern OIBs may share similar mantle components probably located in the lowermost mantle.

title: Iron isotopes reveal the transition from magmatic to hydrothermal systems in highly evolved granites
description: Publication date: Available online 6 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yikang Quan, Jiaru Sheng, Gengxin Deng, Yan Jing, Xiangyu Yan, Fang Huang
abstract: In granitic systems, compositional variations in major elements are relatively limited, especially during the highly evolved granite stage. Although fluid influx or exsolution after saturation can drive continued magma evolution, traditional geochemical methods cannot accurately identify these processes, hindering further understanding of highly evolved granites. Here, we use iron isotope (δ56Fe) and trace element data from four-stage granites (NL-1 to NL-4) from a common transcrustal magmatic system in the Nanling Range, Southeast China, to decipher evolutionary processes of highly evolved granitic systems. The δ56Fe exhibits a systematic increase from NL-1 (0.08‰-0.19‰) to NL-2 (0.14‰-0.25‰), remains constant from NL-2 to NL-3 (0.14‰-0.24‰), and shows a large variation in NL-4 (0.07‰-0.30‰), whereas Nb/Ta, Zr/Hf, and K/Rb decrease with increasing evolution. These geochemical observations most likely reflect the magmatic-hydrothermal transition. Quantitative modeling indicates three distinct stages: (1) an early magmatic stage (NL-1) characterized by < 15% fractional crystallization of Fe-bearing minerals accompanied by < 10% fluid exsolution; (2) a magmatic-hydrothermal transition stage (NL-2 and NL-3) involving progressive magmatic differentiation (<20%) coupled with fluid metasomatism (<15%), and (3) a late hydrothermal stage (NL-4) dominated by 0–30% fluid metasomatism. Concentrations of fluid-mobile elements (e.g., Rb) increase moderately during the magmatic stage, more during the transition stage, and sharply in the hydrothermal stage. Our findings delineate two distinct stages in the evolution of highly evolved granitic magma. The early magmatic stage is governed by fractional crystallization, whereas the late hydrothermal stage is controlled by fluid metasomatism. This demonstrates that fluid is the primary driver of trace-element migration during highly evolved granites.

title: Beyond the Urey-Craig diagram: a ternary framework for iron redox evolution during aqueous alteration of carbonaceous chondrites
description: Publication date: Available online 3 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Damanveer S. Grewal, Zhongtian Zhang
abstract: Water-rock reactions during aqueous alteration were critical in establishing the redox state of early Solar System planetesimals. The Urey-Craig (UC) diagram, which plots “reduced Fe” (metallic Fe + sulfide Fe) against “oxidized Fe” (silicate- and oxide-bound Fe), is the canonical framework for interpreting redox variations among chondrites. Historical CI chondrites, assumed to be metal-free with their sulfur residing in sulfate, were assigned no “reduced Fe” and long regarded as the oxidized endmember. However, the finding that the returned Ryugu and Bennu samples, along with fresh CI material, host sulfides rather than sulfates, revises their position in the UC diagram, placing them closer to the more reduced CR, L, and LL chondrites. This shift has been interpreted as evidence that CIs are more reduced, challenging their long-standing role as the oxidized endmember. This interpretation, however, conflates two distinct Fe reservoirs. Under the low-Eh conditions of planetesimal alteration, metallic Fe oxidizes readily whereas sulfides persist, so only the non-sulfide fraction of bulk Fe is accessible to water-driven oxidation. Because bulk S content increases with matrix fraction, the proportion of non-sulfide Fe decreases, making matrix-rich CIs the group with the smallest “oxidizable” Fe reservoir. By quantifying the mean valence state and oxygen associated with the non-sulfide Fe, we show that CI chondrites, although they appear reduced in the revised UC diagram, record pervasive oxidation of the non-sulfide Fe pool, comparable to or greater than that of the most altered CM lithologies. This convergence occurs despite mineralogically distinct alteration pathways on the CM and CI parent bodies, consistent with the endpoint Fe valence being set by the redox potential of the alteration fluid rather than by specific reaction pathways. The lower total O uptake by Fe in CIs reflects not reduced conditions but a smaller initial reservoir of “oxidizable” Fe, itself limited by high bulk S. We introduce a Fe0-FeS-Feox (metallic Fe-sulfide Fe-oxidized Fe) ternary framework that reconciles extensive oxidation in CIs with their misleading UC position and provides a more accurate basis for tracing aqueous redox pathways in carbonaceous chondrite parent bodies.

title: Granitoid diversity in the early Archean felsic crust revealed by geochemical data from detrital and igneous Paleoarchean apatite
description: Publication date: Available online 29 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Jean-Baptiste Combaz, Oscar Laurent, Gary Stevens, Emilie Bruand, Philippe de Parseval
abstract: The chemistry of detrital apatite has increasingly been employed for provenance studies and to constrain the composition of the parent magma, yet this tool has to date rarely been applied to the topic of Archean crustal evolution. In this study, we present new halogen and trace element compositions analyzed via EPMA and LA-ICP-MS in detrital apatites collected from Paleoarchean metasediments in the Barberton Greenstone Belt (BGB), South Africa, and in magmatic apatites of the surrounding tonalite-trondhjemite-granodiorite (TTG) granitoid-gneisses. Detrital apatites from both the Hooggenoeg (deposited at ∼ 3.43 Ga) and Schapenburg (deposited at ∼ 3.24 Ga) (meta-)sedimentary rocks retained trace element chemistry consistent with a primary igneous origin. They show strong fractionation of their REE spectra (LaN/LuN = 29.4 and 5.43 respectively) and low Eu/Eu* (∼0.5 and 0.8 respectively). On the other hand, the Hooggenoeg apatites have high Sr (600–1200 ppm) and moderate Mn content (400–800 ppm), are F-rich (∼2.2 wt%) and have Cl content ∼ 0.4 wt%; whereas the Schapenburg apatites have uniformly low Sr (∼200 ppm), higher Mn (800–1800 ppm) together with higher F (∼3.2 wt%) and lower Cl (∼0.01 wt%) contents. Strikingly, the characteristics of neither of these populations match with those of apatites from the Barberton TTGs but rather overlap well with apatites crystallized in Neoarchean granitoids, notably sanukitoids, either low-SiO2 ones in the case of the Hooggenoeg apatites, or high-SiO2 for the Schapenburg ones. Therefore, rocks akin to the sanukitoid suite were already present and exposed to surface alteration in the Paleoarchean felsic crust at the time the sediments were deposited. This implies that the felsic crust around the BGB at 3.43–3.24 Ga was more compositionally diverse than the exposed rock record (dominated by TTGs) suggests. In turn, we propose that the onset of observed granitoid diversity in the Neoarchean is an artifact related to a preservation bias, i.e. the higher (upper crustal) emplacement level of K-rich granitoids compared with mid-crustal TTGs made them more prone to erosion before ca. 3 Ga, while the onset of collisional processes at 3.0–2.5 Ga allowed to “shield” these high-level intrusions in the newly amalgamated continental masses and preserve them to our time.

title: New insights into the formation of sediment-hosted volcanogenic massive sulfide deposits by quadruple sulfur and multiple strontium isotopes
description: Publication date: Available online 18 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Tomoaki Koya, Akizumi Ishida, Yuichiro Ueno, Daisuke Araoka, Hideko Takayanagi, Al Kurihara, Yumiko Watanabe, Yasufumi Iryu, Takeshi Kakegawa
abstract: Submarine hydrothermal activity has produced volcanogenic massive sulfide (VMS) deposits on ancient and modern seafloors. Whereas most VMS deposits are hosted in volcanic rocks, some have been found in complexes of sedimentary and volcanic rocks. However, the influence of sediments, particularly sedimentary organic matter, on the mineralogy and geochemistry of such VMSs is unclear. Therefore, we investigated the sediment-hosted Kuroko-type VMS deposits in Kowarizawa and Shinsawa, Japan, to elucidate the role of organic matter in ore formation. Sulfide and sulfate minerals are commonly found in mudstones, indicating ore fluid infiltration into soft sediments in both deposits. Kowarizawa barites exhibit a wide range of δ34S values exceeding the δ34S value of Miocene seawater sulfate. This can be explained by Rayleigh fractionation via sulfate reduction in the shallow sediments. δ13C values of organic matter and calcite suggest oxidative decomposition of organic matter in the sediments. δ34S and Δ33S values of barites suggest that thermochemical sulfate reduction (TSR) occurred. The δ 88/86Sr geothermometer is consistent with the temperature range of TSR. Quadruple sulfur isotope compositions were analyzed for the ore samples and associated rocks. Analyses were conducted on acid-volatile sulfur (AVS), chromium-reducible sulfur (CRS) derived from sulfides, and Kiba-extracted sulfur from barites. The relationship between δ34S and Δ33S indicates that AVS, which is partitioned in major ore minerals, was generated at depth when the isotope equilibrium temperature exceeded 300 ℃. CRS, which is mainly derived from pyrite, shows different characteristics between the Kowarizawa and Shinsawa deposits. In particular, Kowarizawa samples show that quadruple sulfur isotopes were equilibrated at ≤ 250 ℃ or not equilibrated. These characteristics can be explained by CRS generation through TSR by organic matter in the sediments. These findings highlight the role of organic matter in the evolution of ore-forming fluids in sediment-hosted VMS deposits.

title: PM 2.5 exposure and retinal neurovascular dysfunction: clinical and mechanistic evidence for complement C3/C3aR pathway involvement
description: Publication date: Available online 4 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Yi Tian, Yixiang Zhu, Xinyao Yu, Ji Zhou, Haidong Kan, Xinghuai Sun, Yuan Lei
abstract: PM2.5 is a pervasive environmental toxicant associated with retinal neurodegeneration, yet the mechanisms remain unclear. This study combined clinical, animal, and cellular approaches to investigate whether C3/C3aR signaling mediates PM2.5‑induced retinal neurovascular damage. In retrospective longitudinal glaucoma cohort, a linear mixed‑effects model analyzed PM2.5 effects on inflammatory markers. In mice, we examined PM2.5 effects on retinal complement, microglia activation, neurovascular function, and vision. The protective effect of the C3aR blocker SB290157 was also evaluated. BV2 and retinal endothelial cells were used to study C3‑dependent microglial polarization and its vasoregulatory effects. In clinical experiment, we identified a significant association between short-term PM2.5 exposure and systemic complement dysregulation, characterized by a decrease in serum C3c. In mice, PM2.5 exposure induced marked retinal C3 activation. This change was characterized by microglial activation, vascular dysfunction, and retinal structural and functional impairment. In vitro, PM2.5 directly induced C3/C3aR-dependent microglial M1 polarization and stimulated endothelial vasoconstrictor secretion via microglial crosstalk. Treatment with C3aR inhibitor attenuated the vicious cycle, preserving retinal structure and visual function. In conclusion, C3/C3aR axis serves as a key mechanistic link between PM2.5 exposure and retinal neurodegeneration. Targeting this pathway may offer a therapeutic strategy for mitigating pollution-related retinal damage.

title: Soil Nanoparticles and Agricultural Ligands Remobilize Cadmium Sulfide Colloids through Composition–Dependent Heteroaggregation in Saturated Porous Media
description: Publication date: Available online 4 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Junda Shi, Nan Xu, Xin Shu, Xing Yan, Yuji Li, Jinglei Li, Ming Chen
abstract: Cadmium sulfide (CdS) formation can attenuate dissolved Cd mobility in reducing or sulfur–enriched agricultural soils, yet the remobilization risk of CdS nanoparticles by natural soil nanoparticles and agricultural ligands remains poorly understood. Here, we show that soil–derived nanoparticles (SNPs) and common ligands can remobilize CdS as colloidal particles rather than dissolved Cd2+, creating a potentially overlooked pathway for Cd transport in saturated porous media. Saturated quartz sand column experiments, effluent speciation, colloidal characterization, fluorescence microscopy, FTIR spectroscopy, XDLVO calculations, and two–site kinetic attachment modeling were integrated to determine how nanoparticle size, soil–derived composition, humic acid, and phosphate regulate CdS transport. Smaller SNPs promoted CdS breakthrough by forming smaller, more negatively charged, and more stable CdS–nanoparticle heteroaggregates. Nanoparticle composition exerted contrasting effects: organic matter–rich black soil nanoparticles and paddy soil nanoparticles enhanced CdS mobility, with black soil nanoparticles producing the highest transport percentage of 58.27%, whereas loessial soil nanoparticles reduced CdS transport to 35.45% by promoting aggregation and retention, likely through Ca–mediated cation bridging. Humic acid and phosphate further increased CdS–nanoparticle transport, with humic acid showing the stronger effect by enhancing colloidal stability and increasing interaction energy barriers. XDLVO calculations and kinetic attachment modeling linked enhanced CdS breakthrough to higher repulsive energy barriers and lower irreversible retention. These findings demonstrate that naturally occurring soil nanoparticles and agricultural ligands can convert immobilized CdS into mobile colloidal carriers, highlighting an important colloid–facilitated pathway for Cd migration and groundwater contamination risk in agricultural soils.

title: Risk assessment of antibiotic-resistant bacteria in global lakes and their hotspots
description: Publication date: Available online 2 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Xiruo Li, Zhenyan Zhang, Mingke He, Yicheng Jin, Dandan Li, Bingfeng Chen, Xinyu Chen, Huihui Yang, Yinhua Ni, Tao Lu, Haifeng Qian
abstract: Freshwater lakes are crucial hotspots that have fueled the global antimicrobial resistance crisis. However, the distribution patterns and health risks of antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARB) in lakes remain largely unexplored at the global scale. In this study, we comprehensively examined 1,268 metagenomic samples from lakes globally and identified 12,866 ARBs spanning 28 phyla. Furthermore, based on the co-carriage of resistance genes, mobile genetic elements, and virulence factors, we developed a three-tiered risk framework. This framework distinguishes a critical-risk group comprising six species (belonging to Enterobacteriaceae, Aeromonadaceae, and Pseudomonadaceae) that are phylogenetically closely related to known pathogens, exhibiting the highest resistance, mobility, and pathogenic potential. Geographically, these critical-risk ARBs are primarily concentrated in low-latitude lakes (Amazon Basin, Central Africa, South/Southeast Asia, and Central America). Using machine learning, we identified temperature and wind speed as the primary driving factors. From a One Health perspective, our results inform a clear action plan and pinpoint low-latitude lakes as the priority targets for surveillance. This highlights the urgent need to include ARB risk stratification in security frameworks for global aquatic ecology.

title: Targeted Capture of Thallium by Cerium Sulfate Enables Efficient NOx Reduction in Poisoned SCR Catalysts
description: Publication date: Available online 2 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Lingqin Meng, Lu Wei, Yali Wang, Duan Zhang, Feng Zhang, Suping Cui
abstract: Severe thallium (Tl) contamination released from cement kiln flue gas profoundly deactivates commercial selective catalytic reduction (SCR) catalysts, restricting their long-term service stability. Highly volatile Tl species preferentially bind to essential V=O redox active sites to form inert V-O-Tl structures, aggressively disrupting surface acidity and redox synergy. Herein, we report a targeted modification strategy where surface sulfate groups on a Ce(SO4)2-modified vanadium-based catalyst act as sacrificial sites. Even under conditions of severe Tl poisoning, this modified catalyst maintains the NO x conversion rate exceeding 95% within the high-temperature window, in contrast to the catalytic failure of the unmodified catalyst. Tl species preferentially bind and immobilize onto surface sulfate sites of the catalyst, and this targeted capture mechanism spatially and electronically isolates toxic Tl from V active centers. The DFT calculations indicate that the formation of thallium sulfate is thermodynamically more favorable, and this sacrificial trapping mechanism restores surface acid and redox sites, maintaining intact NOₓ adsorption intermediates and unobstructed SCR reaction pathways. This study provides new mechanism regarding the Tl tolerance of SCR catalysts, and these insights for the rational design of highly stable catalysts for industrial NO x removal under complex flue gas conditions.

title: Ag and Cu Partitioned on SSZ-13/γ-Al 2 O 3 Composites: Synergistic Enhancement of NH 3 -SCO
description: Publication date: Available online 2 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Mengyi Kou, Yao Cheng, Guizhen Zhang, Liyun Song, Shuzhen Li, Xi Huang, Hong He
abstract: SSZ-13 and γ-Al2O3 were composited by ball milling, and the Ag/Cu-AlS3 catalyst was successfully prepared, exhibiting excellent catalytic performance and high economic efficiency. The introduction of γ-Al2O3 effectively modulated the reaction mechanism of the Ag/Cu-SSZ-13 catalyst. More importantly, a significant synergistic effect between Ag and Cu was observed across different temperature regions. At low temperatures (<200 °C), surface Ag species primarily activated NH3 to generate NOx, thereby lowering the reaction energy barrier, while Cu species within the pores served as the primary active centers, dominating the internal-selective catalytic reduction (i-SCR) mechanism and endowing the catalyst with excellent low-temperature activity. When the reaction temperature exceeded 200 °C, the reaction mechanism switched to the N2 - mechanism, which was dominated by the Ag/Al2O3 component. Meanwhile, Cu species further lowered the reaction energy barrier through synergy, ensuring a smooth transition of the N2 - mechanism after the i-SCR process and achieving efficient NH3 elimination over a wide temperature range.

title: Tunable Pore Architectures in Programmable DNA Hydrogels for Ultrasensitive Magnetic Relaxation Sensing of Pb²⁺ over a Wide Dynamic Range
description: Publication date: Available online 2 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Yudie Hu, Shaoyi Yu, Jiazhuo He, Pei Jia, Keyu Xing, Liguang Xu, Yunhui Cheng, Li Yao, Zhou Xu
abstract: Magnetic relaxation switch (MRS) sensors are widely used in analytical applications due to their excellent performance. Gel-MRS offers enhanced stability, making it particularly advantageous. However, existing stimuli-responsive hydrogel-based MRS sensors are often limited in detection range and limit of detection (LOD) by the physicochemical constraints of the gel network. Herein, we demonstrate wide-range, ultrasensitive MRS detection of Pb²⁺ using programmable DNA hydrogels with tunable pore architectures. By systematically varying the crosslinking linker design, three hydrogels with pore sizes of 0.72, 1.12, and 4.28 μm were fabricated. As pore size increased, the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) decreased from 2.03 × 10⁻³ to 1.65 × 10⁻³ mm²/s, while the transverse relaxation time change (ΔT₂) increased proportionally, establishing a quantitative structure–property relationship among pore size, ADC, and T₂ response. Leveraging this relationship, the optimized MRS-DNA hydrogel biosensor achieves a detection limit of 8.4pg/mL and a linear range spanning four orders of magnitude (0.01–100ng/mL) with a correlation coefficient of 0.99. Validation in complex matrices yields spike recoveries between 95.21% and 109.21%, underscoring the method's robustness. This programmable pore-engineering strategy offers a new pathway toward reliable, decentralized screening of hazardous contaminants.

title: Hydrodynamic Forcing Controls Denitrification-DNRA Competition and Groundwater-derived Nitrate Contaminant Attenuation
description: Publication date: Available online 2 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Xue Ping, Yonghui Zhu, Yang Xian, Zhang Wen
abstract: River stage fluctuations regulate river aquifer interactions and subsurface biogeochemistry in upstream and midstream rivers. Nevertheless, how diel river-groundwater stage fluctuations impact surface subsurface mixing and the fate of groundwater derived nitrate remains poorly understood in downstream gaining rivers, critical hotspots for nitrogen accumulation and ecological risks. This study develops a coupled hydro-biogeochemical numerical model to evaluate how diel stage fluctuations govern nitrate attenuation via denitrification and dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA) competition. The model represents a typical dune-shaped streambed, where nitrate-polluted groundwater discharges into organic-carbon-rich stream. Diel surface water fluctuations propagate into the aquifer, inducing groundwater responses with 10–90% amplitude attenuation and 3–24h time lags. Diel hydrological fluctuations expand surface-groundwater mixing zones, regulate in-situ C/N stoichiometry, alter nitrate reduction rates, and govern denitrification-DNRA competition. Under C/N ratios of 0.5–2, moderate hydraulic-head offsets (30–50%) and 6–18h out-of-phase subsurface fluctuations favor DNRA, whereas large head differences (>70%) shift competition toward denitrification. Baseline simulations reveal that hydrological fluctuation regimes exert stronger control over this competition than C/N ratios, although biogeochemical kinetic properties may mask these fluctuation‑driven signals and limit the generalizability of such patterns. These results indicate targeted hydrodynamic‑regime regulation can enhance nitrate attenuation and mitigate nitrogen pollution risks in lowland rivers.

title: Functional characterization of PeNRAMP5 implies its potential role in controlling cadmium accumulation in plants
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Fan Yang, Wanyu Ni, Jinyao Li, Linzhou Huang, Ji Feng Shao
abstract: Reducing cadmium (Cd) accumulation in plants by disrupting transporter genes involved in Cd uptake or transport often compromises normal plant growth due to the co‑transport of essential elements. Therefore, identifying genes that specifically reduce Cd accumulation without impairing micronutrient uptake remains challenging. Here, we identified and functionally characterized two duplicated Moso bamboo genes, PeNRAMP5–1 and PeNRAMP5–2. Both genes are predominantly expressed in roots, downregulated by Cd, and encode plasma membrane‑localized transporters. Immunostaining revealed non polar distribution of PeNRAMP5 proteins in all root cells. Yeast assays demonstrated their ability to transport both Cd and Mn. Expression them in rice mutant osnramp5 increased root Cd uptake but reduced Cd accumulation in shoots and grains. In contrast, root Mn uptake and accumulation in shoots and grains were largely restored. When expressed in the mutant atnramp1 or wild‑type Arabidopsis, these genes markedly enhanced root Mn uptake and its accumulation in shoots. Conversely, although Cd accumulation in roots increased, shoots Cd accumulation was strongly inhibited. These results suggest that PeNRAMP5 can limit Cd accumulation in shoots while restoring Mn uptake in plants. This work identifies PeNRAMP5 as a promising genetic resource for inter‑species application to minimize Cd accumulation and maintain Mn nutrition in plants.

title: High-density carboxylated magnetic “gluttonous snake” (HDCMGS): A rapid, efficient, and recyclable adsorbent with mild desorption for methylene blue removal
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Xiaorong Song, Linli Qin, Zhihui Chai, Songlin Fan, Xinquan Liang
abstract: In this work, a high-density carboxylated magnetic “gluttonous snake” (HDCMGS) was developed via UV curing and magnetic assembly for the removal of methylene blue (MB). The structural evolution of HDCMGS during the magnetic‑assembly process was investigated using SEM. The physicochemical properties of HDCMGS were systematically investigated via FTIR, BET, VSM, and TGA. The effects of pH, HDCMGS dosage, and contact time on MB adsorption were then investigated. HDCMGS exhibited ultra-fast MB adsorption kinetics (87% removal within 10 s, 90%–97% removal within 1 min). Ethanol served as an effective eluent for desorbing MB from MB‑loaded HDCMGS. After 15 adsorption-desorption cycles, the MB removal efficiency of HDCMGS remained above 95% of its initial value. Furthermore, the maximum adsorption capacity of HDCMGS for MB was 434.78 mg⋅g–1. The MB adsorption process onto HDCMGS was best described by the pseudo‑second‑order kinetic and Freundlich isotherm models. Thermodynamic analysis revealed that the adsorption process was physical, exothermic, and spontaneous. Finally, density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that MB adsorption onto HDCMGS was dominated by electrostatic attraction and hydrogen‑bonding interactions. Overall, this work suggests HDCMGS is a promising high‑performance adsorbent for wastewater remediation.

title: Alkaline cementitious matrix effects on the fate of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in recycled plastic aggregates
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Hasanthi H. Kosgahakumbura, Will P. Gates, Damien L. Callahan, Susanne Charlesworth, Ivan Kourtchev
abstract: Recycled plastics, including polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) and high-density polyethylene (rHDPE), are increasingly used as construction materials in response to sustainability and circular-economy goals, to repurpose waste streams and reduce natural-resource demand. This study provides the first assessment of PFAS adsorption by recycled plastic aggregates (rPA) and subsequent desorption in simulated cement pore solution (SCPS) by evaluating sorption-desorption mechanisms as functions of polymer type, surface chemistry, exposure duration, and perfluoroalkyl chain length (C4–C11). Batch experiments quantified indicative multi-analyte PFAS loading under neutral pH and PFAS desorption under construction-relevant exposure to high pH (>12.5) and ionic strength (0.85–1.0 M) SCPS. PFAS with carbon chain lengths >C8 showed strong adsorption affinity for rHDPE over rPET (6.2–106.5% greater mass-normalised adsorption (pg/g)), with competitive uptake increasing with chain length and contact time up to 28 days. Desorption into near-neutral ultrapure water was negligible (<LOD), confirming rPA as effective short-term sinks for PFAS. However, SCPS induced substantial PFAS desorption from rPA, particularly of short-chain perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA) from rPET, and (less so) rHDPE. These findings challenge the long-term viability of rPA in concrete, highlight their potential as transient PFAS sinks or enduring leaching sources, and emphasise the need for risk-based guidelines for rPA use in cementitious matrices.

title: Assessing the removal of microplastics, nanoplastics, and tire derived contaminants using chemically enhanced primary treatment
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Laura M. Hernandez, Sinan Abi Farraj, Mathieu Lapointe, Nathalie Tufenkji
abstract: This study assesses the performance of chemically-enhanced primary treatment (CEPT) for removing micro- and nanoplastic contaminants from surface water and wastewater influent under different treatment conditions and varying environmental factors. Four contaminants were tested including polyester microfibers, polyethylene microspheres, tire crumb rubber, and polystyrene nanoplastics. Alternative coagulants, including ferric sulfate (FS) and aluminum chlorohydrate (ACH) improved treatment under conditions that were challenging for alum (pH > 8). In wastewater at pH 7, FS and ACH effectively removed tire crumb rubber (83% and 93%, respectively) compared to alum (27%). FS was an effective coagulant for treating surface water at pH 8.5 with high removal across all micro-sized plastic contaminants. Jar tests also showed that environmental factors such as the presence of laundry detergent and UV-irradiation impacted the extent of plastic contaminant removal. The highest nanoplastic removal were observed using alum (51%; pH 8.5; wastewater) and ACH (83%; pH 7; surface water). Results from this work offer new insights into the impact of treatment conditions, environmental factors, and plastic type and morphology on the performance of CEPT in plastic contaminant removal.

title: Integrated modelling framework for predicting microplastic build-up on urban surfaces
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Mihiri Indunil Gunasekara, James McGree, Prasanna Egodawatta, Godwin A. Ayoko, Ashantha Goonetilleke
abstract: Urban impervious surfaces are major accumulation zones for microplastics, with deposited urban dust as a key carrier matrix facilitating their retention, redistribution, and transport from terrestrial to aquatic environments. However, processes governing microplastic build-up and the ability to predict its spatial distribution remain poorly understood. This study quantified the key factors influencing microplastic build-up and created a catchment-scale spatial predictive framework. Using dust samples from typical urban land uses in Brisbane, Australia, five influential predictors were identified, including dust loading, mineralogical composition, wind speed, land use, and population and were integrated using principal component analysis, multivariate regression, and spatial response surfaces modelling. Population was defined as the number of residents within a 1 km radius of each sampling site. Site-based observations combined with spatial predictor layers generated a continuous microplastic build-up surface across the study area. The resulting model has strong explanatory and predictive performance (R² = 0.91; cross-validated R² = 0.84). The novelty of this work lies in the integration of dust mineralogy and environmental drivers within a spatially explicit predictive framework, enabling identification of microplastic build-up at unsampled locations. The proposed framework improves understanding of terrestrial microplastic dynamics, providing a practical tool to support targeted monitoring and mitigation.

title: Machine learning-assisted ratiometric Zr-MOF-based fluorescent probe for intelligent detection of uranyl ions
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Qing Wang, Haixia Quan, Peipei Liao, Meifeng Li, Yonggang Lv
abstract: Uranium contamination in aquatic environments poses potential threats to ecosystems and human health due to the high radioactive and chemical toxicity of uranyl ions (UO2 2 +), necessitating the development of accurate and rapid detection strategies for the monitoring of UO2 2+. Herein, a zirconium-based metal-organic framework (NH2-PCN-134) was constructed through a one-pot hydrothermal method and employed as a ratiometric fluorescent probe for the detection of UO2 2+. The ratiometric fluorescence response of NH2-PCN-134 toward UO2 2+ featured emission quenching at 655 nm and enhancement at 515 nm, enabling quantitative analysis based on the I515/I655 intensity ratio. Furthermore, the probe exhibited a broad linear response range of 0–200 μM with a low detection limit of 1.23 μM, and excellent selectivity toward UO2 2+ in the presence of various interfering ions. The ratiometric fluorescence response was attributed to the synergistic effects of photoinduced electron transfer (PET) and molecular interactions between NH2-PCN-134 and UO2 2+. Moreover, the color features extracted from fluorescent images were integrated with multiple machine learning models for quantitative prediction, which exhibited strong agreement between the predicted and experimental values even in the presence of interfering ions, demonstrating their effectiveness for quantitative analysis. This study provides a machine learning-assisted ratiometric fluorescence sensing strategy for intelligent detection of UO2 2+, highlighting its potential for environmental monitoring.

title: Long-term exposure to fine particulate matter constituents and lung cancer risk in Chinese never-smokers
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Zhili Xia, Yuting Han, Yuanlin Mou, Jiayu Le, Qiufen Sun, Chen Ji, Xia Zhu, Canqing Yu, Dianjianyi Sun, Ling Yang, Yiping Chen, Huaidong Du, Juncheng Dai, Zhengming Chen, Zhibin Hu, Jun Lv, Guangfu Jin, Hongxia Ma, Meng Zhu, Jing Wei
abstract: Although long-term exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) has been linked to lung cancer incidence in never-smokers (LCINS), evidence for PM2.5 constituents remains limited. This study included 262,785 never-smokers from the China Kadoorie Biobank, among whom 2646 LCINS cases were identified. Annual average concentrations of PM2.5 and its major constituents during 2004–2018 were obtained from the ChinaHighAirPollutants database. Time-dependent Cox proportional hazards models estimated constituent associations with LCINS incidence, and Quantile-based g-computation assessed the importance of each constituent. The polygenic risk score (PRS) was constructed to explore the multiplicative and additive interactions between genetic risk and pollutant constituents. Per interquartile range increase, exposure to nitrate (NO3 −), ammonium (NH4 +), and chloride (Cl−) was associated with higher LCINS risk, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.35 (95% confidence interval (CI), 1.23–1.48), 1.22 (95% CI, 1.13–1.31), and 1.20 (95% CI, 1.12–1.28), respectively. Mixture analyses consistently identified NO3 − and NH4 + as the largest positive contributors to the overall PM2.5-related risk, with an overall mixture HR of 1.13 (95% CI, 1.07–1.19). Significant additive and multiplicative interactions between NO3 − exposure and PRS were observed. These findings suggest that long-term exposure to specific PM2.5 constituents, particularly NO3 −, was associated with higher LCINS risk, especially among genetically susceptible individuals.

title: Interactions between pharmaceutically active compounds and organic foulants in ultrafiltration processes
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Bongyeon Jung, Seungyeon Han, Choe Earn Choong, Min Jang, Chanhyuk Park, Chang Min Park, Byung-Moon Jun, Shane A. Snyder, Yi Huang, Yeomin Yoon
abstract: In this study, we systematically investigated the fundamental interactions between pharmaceutically active compounds (PhACs) and organic fouling layers during ultrafiltration (UF) processes. Two representative PhACs, propranolol (PRP) and naproxen (NPX), were filtered through polyethersulfone membranes fouled with natural organic matter surrogates, including humic acid, bovine serum albumin, and sodium alginate. The results suggested that electrostatic interactions contributed substantially to the association of ionic PhACs with organic fouling layers under the investigated UF conditions. Electrostatic attraction likely promoted the association of cationic PRP with negatively charged fouling layers, whereas electrostatic repulsion likely limited the association of anionic NPX with these layers under neutral and alkaline conditions. Experiments conducted at high ionic strength (1 M NaCl) further supported these mechanisms by suppressing electrostatic interactions, resulting in decreased PRP and improved NPX association with fouling layers. When electrostatic contributions were reduced, the observed PhAC retention was consistent with hydrophobic interaction, with possible additional contributions from π − π interactions and hydrogen bonding. These findings highlight the influence of foulant chemistry on pharmaceutical association.

title: Salinity–regulated interfacial interactions of asphaltene subfractions: Mechanistic insights into petroleum emulsion stability and destabilization
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Hongtao Ma, Xiaohui Mao, Yuanyuan Wang, Chenyu Qiao, Yongxiang Sun, Ying Hu, Hao Zhang, Hongbo Zeng
abstract: Asphaltenes are problematic petroleum components that contribute to persistent oil–water emulsions and complicate produced water treatment. However, how asphaltene subfractions with distinct interfacial activities respond to brine salinity and regulate emulsion stability remains insufficiently understood. Here, the salinity-dependent adsorption, interfacial film formation, and intermolecular interactions of interfacially active asphaltenes (IAA) and interfacially non-active asphaltenes (INAA) were investigated at different NaCl concentrations using dynamic interfacial tension measurements, interfacial film characterization, surface force measurements, and emulsion stability tests. With increasing NaCl concentration, the extrapolated equilibrium interfacial tension of INAA-containing systems increased monotonically, whereas that of IAA-containing systems initially decreased and then increased. Apparent diffusion coefficients and crumpling ratios increased with NaCl concentration up to 1 M and decreased at 3 M, whereas compression energies remained elevated or increased further at 3 M. Droplet adhesion increased at 1–100 mM NaCl but declined sharply at 1–3 M. Bottle tests using a steam-assisted gravity drainage emulsion showed greater stability at low salinity and pronounced oil–water separation at high salinity. These results reveal a salinity-dependent transition from interfacial film strengthening to emulsion destabilization, providing mechanistic insights into the salinity-regulated interfacial interactions of asphaltene subfractions in stabilizing petroleum emulsions.

title: Cell architecture regulates species-specific micro-nanoplastic toxicity through targeted organelle disruption and energetic pathway rewiring in freshwater algae: Insights from deuterium isotope tracing, ultrastructural profiling, and multi-omics
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Xiaofeng Jiang, Wenbo Guo, Hao Qiu, Liyue Zeng, Lian Wang, Shiyun He, Qin Qin, Jun Wang, Lijuan Sun, Yafei Sun, Shiyan Yang, Ping Lu, Xing Li, Hongbo Liu, Yong Xue
abstract: Micro-nanoplastics (MNPs) are prevalent in aquatic environments, yet the species-specific toxicological mechanisms associated with inherent cellular architecture remain poorly understood. Here we utilized synthesized deuterium (2H) stable isotope-labeled polystyrene MNPs (2H-PSMNPs; 0.1 μm and 2 μm) to quantify cellular uptake in two microalgae with contrasting cell architectures: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (rigid cell wall) and Euglena gracilis (cell-wall deficient). Exposure at 1 mg/L (environmentally relevant) and 5 mg/L (a mechanistic dose) showed that 2H-PSMNPs inhibited growth in both algal species. Under the most inhibitory treatment, growth inhibition reached approximately 35% in C. reinhardtii and 25% in E. gracilis. Isotope-based quantification revealed that E. gracilis accumulated 32 μg/g dry weight of 0.1 μm 2H-PSNPs, about twice that in C. reinhardtii. Ultrastructural confirmed distinct organelle targeting, revealing mitochondrial damage in C. reinhardtii, whereas E. gracilis suffered pronounced chloroplast disruption. Multi-omic analyses revealed species-specific metabolic reprogramming: C. reinhardtii adapts by reshaping propanoate metabolism and amino acid turnover, whereas E. gracilis suffers disrupted photosynthetic electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation. Structural equation modeling confirmed that species-specific cell traits contribute 67.3% to the overall transcriptomic and metabolic response. These findings link cell architecture to MNP internalization and toxicity, supporting preliminary screening of vulnerable species by cell-wall traits.

title: The nexus among biosolids land application, PFAS soil accumulation, and plant uptake from a comprehensive soil health perspective
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Xucheng Hu, Cassidy M. Buchanan, Steve W. Blecker, Aihua Wang, Kang Xia, Shilai Hao, James A. Ippolito
abstract: Biosolids land application is a widespread practice for the beneficial recycling of plant nutrients, yet its full implications at the soil-plant-contaminant nexus remain a challenge. This research aimed to connect soil health conditions using the Soil Management Assessment Framework (SMAF) within biosolids application sites that contained per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in a shortgrass steppe ecosystem. Evaluation of biosolids rates (0, 5, 10, and 15 Mg ha−1) revealed that increasing biosolids application rates drive the soil accumulation of long-chain PFAS. A distinct distribution difference was observed between soil and plant matrices; while soil profiles were dominated by long-chain PFAS, above-ground plant tissues preferentially accumulated short-chain PFAS (bioaccumulation factor [BAF] ranged from 1.17 to 139.8). Specifically, short-chain perfluorosulfonic acids (PFSAs) accumulated in the plant tissues, despite being nearly undetectable in the soil matrix, demonstrating the high mobility of short-chain PFAS. Multivariate analysis revealed that increasing biosolids-applied soil PFAS concentrations were negatively correlated with soil health conditions and were correlated with suppressed soil biological properties (beta-glucosidase activity, Pearson r = -0.51, and microbial biomass carbon, Pearson r = -0.48). These findings underscore integrating biological soil health monitoring into PFAS assessments of biosolids-amended (agro)ecosystems and further investigating specific PFAS and soil microbial interactions.

title: Au-loaded ZnO immobilized cellulose-derived carbon beads for enhanced photocatalytic degradation of tetracycline
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Yaoyao Wang, Pujuan Zhao, Gao Huan, Xiaogang Luo
abstract: The elimination of tetracycline antibiotics from aqueous environments remains a significant challenge. In this work, Au-loaded ZnO immobilized cellulose-derived carbon beads (Au/ZnO@C) composite materials, with varying Au molar ratios, were synthesized through a one-pot approach. The Au/ZnO@C composite featured a metal–semiconductor architecture built from Au nanoparticles deposited on ZnO. The introduction of Au nanoparticles can modify the interfacial electronic structure of ZnO and promote charge transfer between Au and ZnO. Meanwhile, using cellulose-derived carbon beads as a carrier effectively suppressed the aggregation of Au/ZnO particles, addressing a key limitation in ZnO-based photocatalysts. Compared to bare carbon beads and ZnO@C, Au/ZnO@C exhibited better photocatalytic degradation performance. Among all samples, Au(1%)/ZnO@C showed the best catalytic performance, achieving a degradation efficiency of 87.62% for tetracycline. The degradation kinetics were well described by the Langmuir–Hinshelwood model, exhibiting a first-order behavior and an optimal apparent rate of 0.00729 min−1. Mass spectrometry analysis revealed that tetracycline was progressively transformed into small-molecule intermediates during the degradation process.

title: Neurotoxicity and neurodegenerative disorders caused by pyrethroids: Adverse events, mechanisms of action and therapeutic approaches
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Yanan Liu, Shiyu Xie, Fangjing He, Irma Ares, Marta Martínez, Bernardo Lopez-Torres, Jorge-Enrique Maximiliano, María-Rosa Martínez-Larrañaga, Arturo Anadón, Xu Wang, María-Aránzazu Martínez
abstract: Pyrethroid insecticides are extensively used worldwide and were initially considered to have low toxicity to non-target organisms. However, with the widespread application of Type I (non-cyano) and Type II (α-cyano) pyrethroids, evidence increasingly indicates that chronic exposure can induce neurological damage and risk of neurotoxicity and neurodegenerative disorders. This effect is primarily mediated through the disruption of voltage-gated sodium channels. Their lipophilic nature facilitates passage across the blood-brain barrier (BBB), where they can impair tight junctions increasing barrier permeability and creating a dual insult scenario that exacerbates neurotoxic effects. This review article synthesizes current knowledge on the roles and interrelationships of oxidative stress coupled with mitochondrial damage, autophagy dysregulation, neuroinflammation, and disturbances in voltage-gated ion channels within the context of pyrethroid-induced neurotoxicity. It examines the dual role of the BBB, which functions as both protector and target, and discusses the application of plant-derived natural extract for intervention. The analysis extends to the synergistic interactions among these pathophysiological mechanisms, highlights exposure risks for susceptible populations, and outlines current research challenges alongside future directions. This literature review manuscript offers novel insights and a valuable reference for the prevention and treatment of pyrethroid-induced neurotoxicity and related neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Smart pH-regulated foams with tunable wettability and photothermal enhancement for controllable recovery of oil-contaminated water
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Yeqiang Lu, Mengyao Wei, Yuexiu Li, Xinyue Liang, Lei Qin, Zhishan Chen, Lixin Xue
abstract: Oil contamination in water poses persistent environmental risks, making the efficient removal and recovery of oil pollutants a pressing challenge. Materials capable of adapting their interfacial properties in response to environmental stimuli are highly desirable for oil pollution control. Herein, we develop a pH-responsive smart composite foam (SCF) that integrates reversible wettability switching, controllable oil absorption-desorption, and photothermal-assisted oil recovery within a single porous architecture. The SCF exhibits pronounced pH-dependent wettability switching (0°∼155°), enabling controllable separation of various immiscible oil-water mixtures. In acidic media, the SCF surface displays superhydrophilicity and underwater superoleophobicity, while it transitioned to hydrophobic/oleophilic state under neutral or alkaline conditions, with oil-water separation efficiency exceeding 99%. The SCF demonstrates reversible pH-regulated oil uptake and release, with high uptake capacity under alkaline conditions and desorption efficiency above 80% upon acidification. Integrated with a dissolved oxygen probe, the SCF enables real-time oil spill monitoring, and its photothermal conversion effectively reduce oil viscosity and accelerate absorption.
