Unlike traditional responsive materials relying mainly on wettability transitions, this study establishes a strategy for efficient oil recovery by exploiting pH-dependent interfacial energy changes to regulate the capillary driving force, thereby providing new mechanistic understanding of controllable oil transport and recovery in porous materials.

title: Deep transport potential of microplastics in estuarine riparian soils: coupled controls of pore structure, hydrodynamics, and interfacial adhesion
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Xuan Zhu, Ao Li, Jia Wang, Tao Zhou, Jinhao Bai, Qi Wei, Danhui Yang, Wenjie Lv
abstract: Estuarine riparian soils are critical interfaces connecting surface water, soils, and shallow aquifers, yet the pore-scale mechanisms governing microplastic (MP) transport and retention remain poorly understood. Here, undisturbed soil cores from the Huangpu River and Yangtze River riparian zones were investigated using stratified MP analysis, Py-GC/MS, micro-CT, and CFD-DEM simulations coupled with XDLVO calculations. MP abundance increased from 415.6 ± 20.8–960.1 ± 48.0 n/kg in Huangpu River soil and from 58.7 ± 2.9–187.1 ± 9.4 n/kg in Yangtze River soil from the 0–4–8–12 cm layers, while median particle size decreased from 118.82 to 19.89 μm and from 42.79 to 17.51 μm, respectively. These patterns were consistent with depth-dependent enrichment and size-selective redistribution. Micro-CT analysis showed that Huangpu River soil had finer pore throats and more tortuous pore networks, favoring shallow retention, whereas the Yangtze River soil contained larger, more directionally continuous pathways that facilitated deeper migration, particularly under water-scour conditions. XDLVO analysis further revealed contrasting interfacial adhesion behaviors between the two soils. Overall, MP migration and retention were jointly controlled by pore-network accessibility, hydrodynamics, and interfacial interactions, providing a mechanistic basis for assessing potential MP transfer toward deeper soils and shallow groundwater.

title: Rapid assessment of the intrinsic hazard potential of different types of plastic additives using machine learning (RF-MLP)
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Qiang Liu, Ye Zhang, Zhen Hua Liu, Hong hui Teng
abstract: As plastic pollution becomes increasingly severe, the additives released during its degradation have attracted widespread attention. How to effectively assess the potential hazards of plastic additives and identify candidates with relatively lower predicted intrinsic hazard potential for further evaluation has become an urgent issue. Experimental hazard assessment is costly and time-consuming, and the limited availability of baseline data prevents comprehensive screening of the large number of plastic additives in use. Currently, most additives lack sufficient baseline data, making it difficult for existing risk assessment methods to provide effective predictions under conditions of data scarcity. This paper proposes an intrinsic hazard potential assessment method based on the random forest-multilayer perceptron (RF-MLP) model to address this challenge. By combining the powerful nonlinear modeling capabilities of RF with the deep feature learning capabilities of Multi-Layer Perceptrons, this method can effectively capture the complex relationships between plastic additives and intrinsic hazard potential, thereby improving the accuracy of intrinsic hazard potential predictions. To further enhance the model’s robustness and predictive capability, an Out-of-Fold (OOF) combination strategy was incorporated into the model. Linear regression analysis was performed on the outputs of the RF and MLP, thereby improving the accuracy of intrinsic hazard potential predictions. This model was used to conduct intrinsic hazard potential assessments on 7267 plastic additives. The RF-MLP model achieved an R2 of 0.68 on the independent test set, reflecting the degree of agreement between the predicted and observed Hazard_score_sum values. Additionally, the performance of the RF-MLP model was compared with that of commonly used machine learning models (such as RF, MLP, SVR, and XGBoost) and other hybrid models. Validation was conducted on 60 plastic additives across different predicted intrinsic hazard potential intervals, incorporating toxicity or intrinsic hazard potential results reported in the literature and data from the T.E.S.T. software developed by the U.S. EPA. The results indicate that the RF-MLP model outperforms the comparison models in predictive performance. Comparisons with literature reports and T.E.S.T. outputs provided complementary evidence for interpreting the predicted hazard patterns. The constructed RF-MLP model partially mitigates the practical limitations caused by the prediction challenges caused by insufficient baseline data and can be applied not only to the intrinsic hazard potential assessment of plastic additives but also serve as a reference for chemical intrinsic hazard potential prediction in other data-scarce scenarios.

title: Polyaniline-modified sea sand suppresses phase-change-driven microplastic transport via regenerable interfacial retention for long-term solar desalination
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Lin Gong, Xushen Liu, Jingzhe Li, Shengde Yu, Wei Zhang
abstract: Solar interfacial evaporation (SIE) provides a low-carbon route for seawater desalination, but its nonequilibrium phase-change interface may facilitate microplastic transfer from seawater to condensate. To mitigate this water-quality risk, a low-cost, regenerable photothermal interface was constructed by modifying natural sea sand with polyaniline (PANI@SS). The PANI coating enhanced broadband solar absorption and promoted interfacial water activation, achieving an evaporation rate of 2.20 kg·m−2·h−1. Adsorption, spectroscopy, thermodynamic analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations showed that PANI converted the weak physical retention of pristine sea sand into stable interfacial anchoring, counteracting phase-change-driven microplastic transport. Reversible protonation/deprotonation enabled pH-regulated interfacial affinity, supporting facile regeneration and sustained antifouling performance. PANI@SS effectively retained seven representative microplastics with different structures and polarities, indicating broad applicability. In a 30-day outdoor test using natural seawater from the Yellow, Yangtze, and Pearl River estuaries, cumulative freshwater production exceeded 220 kg·m−2, while major ion concentrations met drinking-water guideline limits. Evaporation performance, microplastic retention, and material structure remained stable after repeated evaporation–regeneration cycles. This study reveals the competition between phase-change transport and interfacial retention as a key mechanism governing microplastic migration and product-water safety in SIE, providing a practical strategy for efficient, durable, and regenerable solar desalination.

title: Sublethal clothianidin disrupts PI3K–AKT–mTOR homeostasis and induces autophagic-apoptotic imbalance in Bombyx mori
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Danyang Sun, Yuhan Luo, Huanyan Ma, Qingyu Lu, Yiping Yang, Meiliang Pan, Enting Zhang, Huabing Wang
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have improved the operational efficiency of pesticide application. However, off-target droplet drift poses a potential threat to nontarget organisms. Clothianidin is widely applied, yet its sublethal toxicological impacts on nontarget organisms remain poorly characterized beyond neurotoxicity. Here, Bombyx mori larvae were exposed to clothianidin, followed by comprehensive analyses of fat body ultrastructure, biochemical responses, and transcriptomic profiles. Clothianidin exposure impaired larval growth and induced ultrastructural damage in the fat body. Transcriptomic analysis revealed pronounced responses in the fat body, with GO and KEGG analyses indicating disrupted ATP binding along with downregulation of immune and metabolic pathways. Mechanistically, clothianidin exposure perturbed the PI3K–AKT–mTOR signaling pathway, as evidenced by decreased p-AKT and p-4EBP levels. Furthermore, clothianidin induced an autophagic-apoptotic imbalance, as indicated by accumulation of ATG8-PE and ATG6 alongside elevated BmICE expression. Beyond the classical neurotoxicity observed at the synapse, these findings showed that the fat body was preferentially responsive to sublethal clothianidin, with cellular injury linked to PI3K–AKT–mTOR signaling perturbation and autophagy-related stress. This study provided novel mechanistic insights into sublethal neonicotinoid toxicity in silkworms and established a valuable foundation for ecological risk assessment of UAV-based pesticide application.

title: The GmEIN3.1-GmERF3-GmABCI17 module coordinately regulates soybean root development and cadmium tolerance through the ethylene signaling
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Chen Liu, Zhenghao Wang, Zhuorui Zhang, Songjie Qi, Min Wang, Xinchen Wang, Yubo Jia, Xinxia Li, Hengxi Zhao, Yaqing Wei, Huiru Sun, Hanqiu Zhang, Qiumin Chen, Zhimin Dong
abstract: Soybean (Glycine max) is a critical oil crop and a key source of fat and protein for both humans and animals. Cadmium (Cd) stress is a severe heavy metal stresses limiting root growth and yield. Significant variations exist in Cd tolerance among different soybean varieties. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying Cd-induced root growth inhibition and Cd accumulation remain elusive. Here, we identified that the GmEIN3.1-GmERF3-GmABCI17 module in the ethylene signal transduction pathway coordinately regulates soybean root growth and Cd accumulation. We found Cd stress positively regulates the expression of GmEIN3.1 (Glyma.13G076700), which inhibits root development but reduces Cd accumulation and enhances Cd tolerance. Multiple lines of experimental evidence demonstrate that GmEIN3.1 represses the expression of GmERF3 (Glyma.14G050100), a transcription factor that promotes root development. In turn, GmERF3 binds to and suppresses the expression of the ABC transporter GmABCI17 (Glyma.08G055000), a Golgi-localized protein with Cd efflux transporter activity. Overexpression of GmABCI17 promotes Cd efflux, thereby reducing intracellular Cd accumulation and enhancing Cd tolerance. Collectively, the GmEIN3.1-GmERF3-GmABCI17 transcriptional cascade coordinates Cd-induced root growth inhibition, restricts Cd accumulation, and Cd tolerance in soybean. It provides exploitable targets for breeding low-Cd soybean cultivars and addresses critical food safety concerns.

title: Lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide particles may impair cognitive function via CTCF-associated suppression of NMDAR-dependent synaptogenesis
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Xinchao Guan, Lijie Xie, Guoliang Li, Yujie He, Shilin Chen, Han Wang, Wenke Yuan, Huan Gao, Ming Chen, Xiaoge Yang, Yingxia Luo, Xiaojian Shao, Wen Chen, Lili Liu, Qing Wang
abstract: Lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide (NCM) is the predominant cathode material for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs); however, its occupational health risks remain insufficiently understood. In this study, we found that in occupationally NCM‑exposed workers, urinary levels of Li, Ni, Co, and Mn were negatively associated with Mini‑Cog test scores and positively associated with serum neurofilament light chain (NfL, as neuronal injury marker). In an intratracheal instillation rat model, NCM-exposed rats exhibited learning and memory deficits, neuronal injury, and reduced synaptic complexity. RNA‑seq analysis revealed suppression of N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors (NMDAR)‑dependent synaptogenesis pathways in rat hippocampus, along with downregulation of NMDAR subunits (GluN2A and GluN2B) and postsynaptic proteins such as CaMKII‑α, MAP2, PSD‑95, and Synapsin‑1. In SH-SY5Y cells, treatment with NCM-derived metals recapitulated these gene expression changes. Bioinformatics analysis identified CCCTC-binding factor (CTCF) as a potential regulator of NMDAR. Cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA) identified the binding of NCM-derived metals to CTCF. Based on in vivo data, human equivalent concentrations (HECs) derived from BMDL10 of Ni and Mn were below the current OELs of China and America. Collectively, these findings indicate that NCM may induce neurotoxicity and impair learning and memory by disrupting synaptogenesis, and CTCF is implicated in this process.

title: Zinc differentially modulates resistome responses to ciprofloxacin and sulfamethazine in activated sludge
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Yongchao Li, Yu Ang Li, Shijie Dong, Jiangxiao Luo, Shixuan Yu, Wenhui Xie, Bin Shi, Renxin Zhao
abstract: Antibiotics and metals frequently coexist in wastewater, but whether metals uniformly intensify antibiotic-driven resistome selection remains unclear. Here, activated sludge reactors were exposed to zinc (Zn), ciprofloxacin (CIP), sulfamethazine (SMZ), and their combinations across four stepwise exposure stages. Read-based, assembly-based, and genome-resolved metagenomics were integrated to characterize antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) abundance, composition, mobility-associated genetic contexts, and putative hosts. Antibiotics primarily drove resistome restructuring, whereas Zn alone had limited effects. CIP strongly enriched ARGs, while Zn co-exposure attenuated this response and caused late-stage declines in total ARG abundance and the relative abundance of ARG-hosting metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). In contrast, ARG abundance remained comparatively stable under SMZ but increased progressively under Zn+SMZ. Because antibiotic concentrations increased sequentially over time, these patterns represent stage-dependent responses rather than independent concentration effects. Antibiotic-related treatments showed higher contributions of ARGs on predicted plasmid-like contigs and more frequent ARG–mobile genetic element co-localization. Pseudomonadota dominated putative ARG hosts, and CIP showed broader ARG–host profiles. Approximately 67% of ARG-hosting MAGs carried virulence factor genes, indicating co-occurring resistance and virulence-associated genomic potential. These findings demonstrate that Zn altered activated sludge resistome in an antibiotic-dependent manner, highlighting that mixture effects cannot be inferred from single-contaminant responses alone.

title: Battery-type-associated pollutant fingerprints and cytotoxicity of firefighting wastewater from full-scale electric vehicle fires
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Qiang Dong, Zhan Wang, Qi Zhang, Yuheng Cheng, Huifeng Li, Yijia He, Xin Zheng, Yudie Jianyao, Jiale Zhang, Yang Yu, Guofeng Su, Hongyong Yuan, Xiaole Zhang
abstract: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has increased concern over fires, whose suppression generates chemically complex wastewater. However, the temporal evolution and toxicity of EV fire wastewater remain poorly understood. In this study, we conducted full-scale fire and suppression tests on EVs powered by nickel–manganese–cobalt (NMC) and lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries, using time-resolved sampling to characterize firefighting runoff and residual wastewater retained after suppression. By integrating chemical profiling and in vitro cytotoxicity assays, we resolved battery-type-associated wastewater hazards. Runoff wastewater exhibited distinct metal-release fingerprints: NMC-runoff carried substantially higher battery-derived ionic loads, with early-stage Li+ reaching 4.26–4.59 mg·L−1, approximately one order of magnitude higher than that in LFP-runoff (averaging 0.36 mg·L−1). Residual pallet wastewater acted as a concentrated pollution reservoir, with NMC samples becoming strongly alkaline (pH>11). Li+ and fluoride in residual wastewater reached about 7.21 × 102 mg·L−1 and 3.85×102 mg·L−1, respectively, generally more than two orders of magnitude higher than in runoff wastewater. Cytotoxicity tests revealed that residual wastewater induced concentration-dependent cytotoxicity, with human neuroblastoma cells being the most sensitive and viability decreasing to 5.7%. These findings identify residual or immersion-type suppression water as a secondary EV fire hazard and support battery-type-specific strategies for emergency management. Synopsis Full-scale NMC and LFP battery EV fire tests reveal distinct wastewater pollutant fingerprints, sludge properties, and cytotoxic profiles, underscoring the need for chemistry-specific environmental standards and emergency protocols.

title: Physical bioturbation coupled with gut-substrate cross-inoculation: A dual-pathway mechanism for enhanced acetochlor degradation in vermifilters
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Xinyi Li, Yang Ou, Xinhong Wang, Huiping Liu, Yupeng Jin
abstract: To mitigate acetochlor (ACT) diffuse pollution in the black soil region of Northeast China, a black soil-gravel biofilter was constructed to investigate how earthworm (Eisenia fetida) bioturbation enhances ACT degradation through coupled physical remodeling and micro-ecological regulation. At an HRT of 72 h, the vermifilter achieved 85.3% aqueous ACT removal and 66.4% solid-phase ACT removal rate, significantly outperforming planted and blank biofilters. In situ Micro-CT showed that earthworm burrowing increased matrix pore connectivity to 20 times that of the blank biofilter, reducing mass transfer resistance and maintaining pollutant bioavailability. High-throughput sequencing revealed that the earthworm gut functioned as a mobile incubator for key degrading bacteria, selectively enriching dechlorinating and dealkylating taxa such as Pseudomonas and Chryseobacterium and reinoculating them into the substrate. Under micro-acidic and nitrogen-rich conditions, the abundance of key transformation genes were higher, enabling complete ACT degradation to the molecular weight product N-(2-ethylphenyl) formamide.

title: Low-dose ionizing radiation exposure and tumor risk: An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Hyeyun Lee, Gwisang Park, Chaeseong Lim, Dokyoung Kim, Su-Yeon Cho, Yujin Kwon, Eun-Soo Lee, Won Kyu Kim, Yun Hak Kim, Kihun Kim
abstract: Low-dose ionizing radiation (LDIR) arises from medical, occupational, and environmental sources, but cancer risks at low doses remain debated. We conducted an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses on low-dose-relevant ionizing radiation exposure and observed tumor occurrence. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, and Epistemonikos for publications through July 2026. Findings were synthesized descriptively by exposure context and cancer type. We assessed methodological quality using AMSTAR 2, classified temporal exposure patterns and dose applicability, evaluated primary-study overlap, and rated certainty using an overview-level GRADE approach. Forty reviews were included: 15 systematic reviews without meta-analysis, 15 systematic reviews with meta-analysis, and 10 meta-analyses. Leukemia-incidence findings following pediatric computed tomography and protracted low-dose-relevant radiation exposure were rated as moderate certainty. Evidence for residential proximity to nuclear facilities, aviation exposure, occupational thyroid cancer, adult central nervous system tumors, dental X-ray-related meningioma, and skin cancer was less certain. No additional pooling was performed because reviews addressed heterogeneous questions and shared primary studies. These findings support exposure-specific, certainty-informed interpretation rather than a uniform conclusion across radiation exposure settings.

title: Lateral flow strip biosensor for visual detection of heavy metal ions based on feedback circuit with trigger DNA regeneration strategy and its logic gate applications
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Junhua Chen, Yile Deng, Jiafeng Pan
abstract: The on-site and visual detection of trace levels of heavy metal ions in resource-limited settings is still a big challenge. Herein, using chromium ions (Cr3 +) as a model target, we developed a lateral flow strip biosensor for visual detection of Cr3+ on the basis of a feedback circuit with trigger DNA regeneration strategy. Cr3+-specific DNAzyme was used to recognize Cr3+. The free trigger DNA (T) after the cleavage reaction can initiate the assembly of hairpin probes H1, H2, and H3. The resulting H1-H2-H3 products contain a freshly regenerated T fragment, which can continuously drive the operation of feedback DNA circuit, thereby yielding abundant H1-H2-H3 assemblies. Compared with the no T regeneration strategy, the feedback circuit with T regeneration method exhibits superior signal amplification capability. The strip biosensor achieves a visual detection limit of 10 pM. Moreover, the sensing platform exhibits favorable robustness and performs reliably when applied to practical water samples. Using Cr3+ and cadmium ion (Cd2+) as two inputs, we further constructed INHIBIT and XOR strip logic gates that open new avenues for intelligent detection of different heavy metal ions in resource-poor environments.

title: The construction of UiO-66(Ce)/Cu oxidase for multivariate identification of acetylcholinesterase, organophosphorus pesticides and tannic acid supported by machine learning
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Yuhan Zhao, Xinyu Han, Shuang Li, Miaomiao Tian, Xu Han, Fang Chai
abstract: The widespread abuse of organophosphorus pesticides (OPs) threatens human health and ecological sustainability. The development of a portable, intelligent, and prompt detection strategy poses a key priority in both environment and human health, but remains a significant challenge. Here, visual detection of OPs was achieved based on its inhibition of acetylcholinesterase (AChE), using the constructed metal-organic framework (MOF) composite UiO-66(Ce)/Cu as a catalyst in the 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) oxidation process. The coexistence of Cu2 +/Cu+ and Ce4+/Ce3+ redox pairs synergistically promoted electron transfer and oxidase-mimicking (OXD-mimicking) catalysis. Based on the oxidation capability of UiO-66(Ce)/Cu and reversible colorimetric response, the AChE, OPs, and tannic acid (TA) can be detected assisted by the smartphone integrating with the machine learning algorithm. The limits of detection for TA, AChE, and OPs were determined to be 0.344 μM, 0.102 mU mL⁻¹ , and 0.0891 μg mL⁻¹ , respectively. In addition, satisfactory recoveries of 91.95–106.04% were obtained from real water and food samples, further corroborating the applicability of the intelligent and visual readout system for the portable analysis of OPs and TA. This work presented a practical strategy for constructing MOF-based OXD-mimicking nanozyme toward cascade biosensing and food safety applications.

title: Dynamics of tire-related chemicals in roadside aerosol over one year in Leipzig, Germany-influencing factors, potential source materials and comparison with rural aerosol
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Volkwin Kuntz, Daniel Zahn, Ankush Kaushik, Hartmut Herrmann, Thorsten Reemtsma
abstract: With tire and road wear particles (TRWP) generated by automotive traffic on roads also tire-related chemicals (TRCs) become airborne. A long-term monitoring of TRCs in roadside aerosol (PM10) was performed for 14 months (119 samples). In total, 40 TRCs were determined by LC-MS/MS in the samples, belonging to phenylendiamines, guanidines, benzothiazoles, ureas and amines. Median volume concentrations were 0.61 pg/m3 for 6-PPD and 2.9 pg/m3 for 6-PPDQ, with 19 of the studied chemicals showing higher concentrations (benzothiazolesulfonic acid 41 pg/m3, diphenylguanidine 90 pg/m3). TRC volume concentrations varied by about four orders of magnitude over time, with precipitation being the single most influential factor, further modulated by temperature, sunshine, wind, and reactive trace gases. Traffic-normalized roadside aerosol concentrations of TRCs were calculated and allow extrapolation to other urban sites. TRC mass concentrations in tire tread particles were one to two orders of magnitude higher than in roadside aerosol and dominated by parent chemicals rather than their transformation products. In rural aerosol TRC concentrations were up to one order of magnitude lower. This study shows that a broad range of TRCs is present in roadside aerosol, with their concentration being highly variable in time and governed by a complex interplay of emission, transport and transformation.

title: Spatial distribution tracing of MOFs in cucumber seedlings by fluorescence imaging and LA-ICP-MS
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Yu Wang, Qi Liu, Xue-Sheng Wang, Ya-Fei Chen, Ming-Yu Zhang, Ming-Li Chen, Jian-Hua Wang
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) show great potential in agricultural applications, and clarifying their in-plant distribution is essential for assessing their ecological effects and biosafety. Single imaging method suffers from limited spatial resolution and inaccurate localization, restricting reliable analysis of plant-MOF interactions. Herein, we established a synergistic imaging approach combining fluorescence and LA-ICP-MS to characterize the translocation of Eu-BDC-NH2 and UiO-66-NH2 in cucumber seedlings. The imaging results demonstrate the preferential accumulation of two MOF in cucumber root tissues, which is further verified by quantitative ICP‑MS analysis. Especially in the high-exposure group (200 mg/L), compared with the corresponding Eu and Zr levels in stems and leaves, substantially higher concentrations of both elements were detected in cucumber roots. Furthermore, MOF aggregates are not limited to root peripheral zones. Eu-BDC-NH2 and UiO-66-NH2 displays efficient translocation from roots to stems and leaves, alongside favorable biocompatibility. By combining the intuitive visualization of fluorescence and the high sensitivity elemental tracing of LA-ICP-MS, this strategy overcomes the limitations of single detection. This study provides a robust analytical tool for evaluating the bio-safety of agricultural nano-materials, advances the understanding of MOF and plant interactions, and benefits the development of sustainable agriculture.

title: An integrated approach to assess the molecular mechanisms and cellular effects of environmentally realistic mixtures of microplastics in Mytilus galloprovincialis
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Alessandro Nardi, Lucia Pittura, Veronica Vivani, Ilaria Bernardini, Matteo Baini, Giuseppe d’Errico, Marica Mezzelani, Andrea Maccantelli, Luca Peruzza, Giovanna Monticelli, Chiara Mascitelli, Massimiliano Babbucci, Maura Benedetti, Stefania Gorbi, Maria Cristina Fossi, Massimo Milan, Francesco Regoli
abstract: Microplastics pose great biological concern due to their ubiquity and ability to enter food webs. Despite their environmental heterogeneity, most laboratory studies still rely on pristine, single-polymer microplastics that inadequately reflect complex field conditions. We provide an integrated multilevel toxicological assessment in mussels Mytilus galloprovincialis exposed for 14 days to three 20–50 µm microplastics typologies: EPM, Environmental Plastics Mixture, obtained by micronizing field-collected objects of polyethylene, polyethylene terephthalate, polypropylene, polystyrene, and polyvinyl chloride; VPM, Virgin Plastics Mixture, pristine particles matching EPM polymer composition; RTR, Rapido Trawling Rubber, derived from fisheries-related litter (ethylene-propylene-diene monomer). Additive bioaccumulation, transcriptomic profiles, cellular biomarkers, and microbiota composition were assessed. EPM increased total phthalate concentrations 4.6-fold relative to controls, with DEHP accounting > 90% of the total, and induced immune, oxidative, metabolic, and microbiota alterations. RTR mainly affected redox balance and energy metabolism, whereas VPM produced more limited responses. The integration of results through a Weight of Evidence framework provided synthetic hazard classification, indicating greater integrated toxicological concern for the environmentally derived materials under the tested conditions (EPM and RTR: “MODERATE”; VPM: “SLIGHT”). Overall findings highlight the importance of incorporating environmentally-derived microplastics into toxicological studies to better reflect realistic exposure scenarios and capture their heterogeneous physico-chemical properties.

title: Bimetallic synergy-driven generation of high-valent metal-oxo species in a nanoconfined catalytic ceramic membrane for efficient antibiotic-containing water treatment
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Wei Zhang, Kaiming Fan, Mu Li, Weihua Xu, Ziyi Yuan, Yanling Liu, Shengji Xia
abstract: Efficient purification in complex waters requires catalytic membranes with high selectivity and interference resistance, a need addressed by nanoconfinement through steering reactive species toward nonradical oxidation. Herein, a cobalt-nickel layered double hydroxide (CoNi-LDH) catalyst was synthesized via hydrothermal conversion of a CoNi metal-organic framework self-sacrificing template and deposited onto a ceramic substrate. In a continuous flow-through system with peroxymonosulfate (PMS), the membrane achieved 97.6% sulfadiazine degradation. The nanoconfined effect increased the pseudo-first-order reaction rate constant of sulfadiazine degradation to 4.916 s−1, three orders of magnitude higher than that of conventional batch system (2.433 × 10−3 s−1). Mechanistic investigation showed that the O-O bond heterolysis of PMS generated high-valent cobalt-oxygen species as the dominant reactive species, endowing high resistance and oxidation selectivity. The degradation efficiencies exceeding 95% for various organic micropollutants and performed stably in actual surface water and secondary effluent. It also exhibited permeate flux recovery efficiency exceeding 80% after multiple cycles of cleaning and fouling caused by humic acid, indicating excellent antifouling properties. This work provides a theoretical foundation and instructive demonstration for nonradical catalytic membrane reactors toward practical water treatment.

title: Context-dependent removal of emerging pollutants in constructed wetlands: a dependence-aware meta-analysis and explainable machine-learning framework for performance envelopes
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Diantong Li, Mengze Gao, Dawei Yu, Jie Mao, Yaohui Bai
abstract: Constructed wetlands (CWs) are widely used as low-energy polishing systems, yet their performance for emerging pollutants (EPs) varies across pollutant classes, wetland configurations, wastewater matrices, and experimental scales. We synthesized 67 peer-reviewed studies and 849 paired influent-effluent comparisons using multilevel random-effects models with study-level cluster-robust inference. Heterogeneity was extreme (I2≈99%), and pollutant class, flow configuration, wastewater matrix, and scale defined distinct attenuation regimes. Microplastics showed the strongest short-term outlet attenuation, primarily reflecting physical retention within wetland compartments under the available monitoring durations. None of the 14 continuous moderators remained significant after Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction, indicating that performance is shaped by combinations of conditions rather than a single universal control variable. In the study-grouped held-out evaluation, CatBoost outperformed the linear and other baseline models (R2 = 0.619; RMSE = 1.251). Leave-one-study-out validation retained a positive but lower predictive signal (R2 = 0.238; RMSE = 3.125; MAE = 2.055). We translate these findings into quantitative, context-specific performance envelopes that report expected lnRR together with confidence and prediction intervals. The resulting framework supports scenario-based system selection, conservative scale-up, and targeted monitoring of hydraulic conditions, wastewater chemistry, and particulate retention.

title: A ZIF-8-based ternary heterostructure gas sensor for monitoring benzene micro-leakage and autonomous robotic inspection
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Xuyang Duan, Hao Zhang, Chengyu Zhang, Liang Zhu, Guangbin Li, Zhaogang Zhang, Peng Zhou, Dongzhi Zhang
abstract: Benzene (C6H6) is a volatile organic compound with strong carcinogenicity, and achieving its rapid and sensitive detection is of great significance for environmental protection and the prevention and control of public health risks. In this study, a ternary heterostructure gas-sensing material composed of Pd-modified ZnO@ZIF-8 was proposed. The pre-concentration effect of ZIF-8, the catalytic sensitization of Pd nanoparticles, and the construction of the Schottky barrier at the Pd/ZIF-8 interface collectively endow the sensor with excellent detection performance. This sensor exhibits extremely high sensitivity at 375℃, with a rapid detection speed (response/recovery time of 2 s/2 s) and an extremely low detection limit (capable of reaching the ppb level). Meanwhile, based on this sensor, a pipeline condition monitoring platform was developed. On the mobile end, online monitoring of benzene leakage and graded early warning were realized. Furthermore, this detection system is integrated with robots. Through a combined olfactory and visual detection method, it enables intelligent inspection of the risks of gaseous and liquid benzene leakage. Therefore, the proposed Pd-ZnO@ZIF-8 sensor and its integrated monitoring platform offer a reliable and efficient solution for real-time benzene leakage detection, holding great promise for enhancing industrial safety and public health protection.

title: OH and 1 O 2 mediated oxidative reduction of antibiotic-resistant bacteria cultivability and tet A abundance in a 3D electro-Fenton system
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Haijun Chen, Shiyi Zhao, Zhuowen Wang, Chunli Kang, Jiao Qu, Deming Dong, Haiyang Liu, Guangqing Ma, Xiuyi Hua
abstract: The proliferation of antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARB) in aquatic environments necessitates efficient remediation strategies. This study developed a three-dimensional electro-Fenton (3DEF) system employing a novel MnO2/Pd(Ⅱ)@CA particle electrode to simultaneously inactivate tetracycline-resistant Escherichia coli (TR E. coli) and mitigate antibiotic resistance dissemination. Under optimal conditions (1.5 V, 12 mM Fe2+, 1.5 g L−1 particle electrode, pH 5), complete inactivation of TR E. coli (> 7-log reduction) was achieved within 4 min. The particle electrode promoted in-situ H2O2 generation, subsequently activated to produce •OH and 1O2 as dominant reactive species, with reactive chlorine species also contributing. Scanning electron microscopy confirmed extensive membrane disruption, accompanied by substantial leakage of intracellular K+ and proteins. Both intracellular and extracellular tetracycline resistance genes (tetA) were detected, while residual extracellular DNA lost transformation capability, indicating reduced dissemination potential. Proteomic analysis revealed suppression of the AcrAB-TolC efflux pump, disrupted DNA repair pathways, and impaired energy metabolism, ultimately leading to complete loss of viability and regrowth capacity. This work highlights the 3DEF system as a promising technology for mitigating environmental risks posed by ARB.

title: Rapid disinfection byproduct formation from microplastics-derived dissolved organic matter during short-term chlorination: Polymer-dependent pathways
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Tengfei Li, Jingqi Xu, Rui Li, Menglei Zhao, Jianchao Zhang, Xingli Zhang, Wei Zou, Tiecheng Wang
abstract: Microplastics-derived dissolved organic matter (MPs-DOM) has emerged as a potential precursor of disinfection byproducts (DBPs), yet its behavior under realistic short-term chlorination remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the formation patterns of both conventional and unknown DBPs from polystyrene (PS) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) leachates under short contact times, combining bulk DBP analysis with Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS). Abundant traditional DBPs were formed rapidly, with trihalomethanes (THMs) as the dominant species. In comparison, PS-DOM showed higher chlorine consumption but PET-DOM produced higher DBP yields and a broader spectrum of species, accounting for 14.63 µg/mg DOC of total 15 DBPs subtypes versus 8.56 µg/mg DOC of total 12 DBPs subtypes for 60 min. For unknown DBPs, molecular-level analysis revealed that PET-DOM generated a more diverse pool of DBPs enriched in oxidized compounds, whereas DBPs derived from PS-DOM were relatively more unsaturated and aromatic-like. Further analysis reflect distinct transformation for two DOM during chlorination. PS-DOM underwent decarbonization, and mono-halogenation dominated its DBP formation. In contrast, PET-DOM exhibited oxidation transformation, with mono- and multi-halogenation contributing comparably to DBP formation. These findings demonstrate that DBP formation from MPs-DOM is highly dependent on polymer structure and can occur rapidly under short-term chlorination. And the elevated DBP formation potential of PET-DOM highlights a greater risk of PET MPs in aquatic environments.

title: Zero liquid discharge and salt recovery from heavy metal wastewater via hollow-umbrella hydrogel solar evaporation
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Hang Su, Limei Li, Chen Yuan, Shanbin Zhang, Guohao Lei, Chen Song, Qing Xu, Jitian Song
abstract: The sustainable treatment of heavy metal-laden industrial wastewater toward zero liquid discharge (ZLD) requires simultaneous water purification, heavy metal immobilization, and salt recovery. Here, we demonstrate a hollow-umbrella hydrogel evaporator addressing all these needs within a single platform. Fabricated from a chitosan/PEI/phytic acid matrix with MXene as the photothermal material, it features a hierarchically porous structure with a central hollow channel and radially aligned pores achieved by sequential vertical and radial directional freezing. This design enables three synergistic functions: hollow-geometry-enhanced natural convection accelerates vapor diffusion; unidirectional water transport directs ions to the hydrophobic umbrella edge for directional crystallization while heavy metals are selectively adsorbed by abundant amino and hydroxyl groups during migration; and hydrophobic edge modification spatially separates evaporation and crystallization zones, preventing salt accumulation. Consequently, the CPPMO-3 evaporator achieves an evaporation rate of 4.97 kg m⁻² h⁻¹ with 97.9% energy efficiency under 1 kW·m⁻² solar irradiation, and adsorption capacities of 234.6 mg g⁻¹ for Cr(VI) and 155.6 mg g⁻¹ for Pb(II). By harvesting the edge-crystallized salt before adsorption saturation, clean salt can be recovered without heavy metal contamination. This work provides a viable pathway toward ZLD treatment and salt resource recovery from high-salinity heavy metal wastewater.

title: Revealing coastal atmospheric mercury redox processes with a photochemical box model MECCA-Hgv1.0
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Junkai Cui, Tao Li, Guojing Wang, Xinyi Gong, Rolf Sander, Lin Du, Yan Wang
abstract: Atmospheric reactions and source-sink pathways of atmospheric mercury (Hg) in coastal regions remain complex. Here we conducted field observations of atmospheric Hg in coast Qingdao in northern China, and developed a photochemical box model (MECCA-Hgv1.0) to investigate its redox processes. Our model successfully reproduced observed concentrations and diurnal variations of gaseous oxidized mercury (GOM), revealing its main species as HgCl2 (∼80%) and brominated speciation. Bromine radicals initiate 85% of Hg(0) oxidation fluxes, but the brominated products are readily photolyzed, ultimately making HgCl2 as the stable GOM species through the hydroxyl-initiated oxidation followed by HCl substitution. The GOM removal process is highly determined by BrHgOH photolysis and gas-liquid partitioning. Sensitivity analysis reveals that either higher humidity or increased temperatures can significantly reduce GOM concentrations via enhanced aqueous uptake and thermal decomposition of Hg(I) intermediates, respectively. Unexpectedly, GOM production reversely responds to anthropogenic volatile organic compounds (VOCs) that consume reactive halogen species in coastal atmosphere. Future emission control of anthropogenic VOCs likely leaves more available reactive halogens, thereby enhancing the potential for coastal Hg oxidation. This study provides critical mechanistic insights into the coastal atmospheric mercury cycle driven by interactions between anthropogenic pollution and marine halogen chemistry.

title: Integrated physiological, transcriptomic, and metabolomic analyses provide insights into zinc-doped carbon quantum dot-mediated alleviation of cadmium toxicity in lettuce
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Songyue Chai, Maohang Bai, Bingxue Chen, Tao Shen, Lujie Wang, Qiuguo Zhang, Mengmeng Sun, Songqing Liu
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) accumulation in crops seriously threatens agricultural productivity and food safety, highlighting the need for effective strategies to mitigate Cd toxicity. Uniformly dispersed zinc-doped carbon quantum dots (Zn-CQDs; 2.67 ± 0.36 nm) were synthesized in this study. The synthesized dots demonstrated enzyme-mimetic activities in vitro and potent radical-scavenging capacity. Foliar application of Zn-CQDs markedly alleviated Cd-induced growth inhibition in lettuce (Lactuca sativa L.), increasing shoot fresh and dry biomass by 30.8% and 23.9%, respectively. Moreover, Zn-CQDs treatment reduced the Cd concentration in lettuce shoots by 44.7% while elevating the Zn concentration by 167.9%. Photosynthetic performance was also substantially restored, as evidenced by a 61.0% increase in total chlorophyll content. Concurrently, Zn-CQDs mitigated Cd-triggered oxidative damage, reducing H2O2 and MDA levels by 31.4% and 38.9%, respectively, and lowering the activities of the antioxidant enzymes POD, SOD, and CAT by 23.3%, 71.5%, and 44.3%, respectively. Transcriptomic profiling revealed that Zn-CQDs modulate stress-responsive signaling networks involving MAPK cascades, Ca2 +, and phytohormone signaling, as well as their associated transcription factors, thereby regulating downstream genes involved in ROS detoxification and metal transport. Metabolomic analysis further demonstrated that Zn-CQDs extensively reprogram Cd-responsive metabolic pathways, particularly those related to phenylpropanoid, lipid, amino acid, and phytohormone metabolism, accompanied by increased accumulation of jasmonic acid, flavonoids, and organic acid derivatives. The above-mentioned findings offer mechanistic insights into Zn-CQD-mediated alleviation of Cd stress and lay a theoretical basis for functional carbon nanomaterials’ application to reduce heavy metal risks in agricultural systems.

title: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, seminal plasma metabolome, and sperm telomere length and mitochondrial DNA copy number: a cohort study
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Guangming Li, Keyi Si, Jie Zhang, Xixi Chen, Xiaotao Shen, Vicente Mustieles, Audrey J. Gaskins, Miao Li, Fengjiang Sun, Tian-Qing Meng, An Pan, Chong Liu, Da Chen, Lili Huang, Xiaocui Li, Yi-Xin Wang
abstract: This study investigated the associations between exposure to 16 per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), seminal plasma metabolome, and sperm telomere length (STL) and mitochondrial DNA copy number (mtDNAcn) among more than 1000 healthy Chinese men screened as potential sperm donors. No associations were observed between PFAS concentrations in blood or seminal plasma and sperm mtDNAcn. However, PFAS concentrations in seminal plasma, but not blood plasma, were associated with longer STL in both single-chemical and mixture models (all FDR-adjusted P < 0.05). Metabolome-wide association analyses identified 79 metabolites associated with seminal PFAS concentrations and 62 metabolites associated with STL. Among these, 18 overlapping metabolites were enriched in pathways related to steroid metabolism and unsaturated fatty acid metabolism, suggesting potential metabolic processes linking seminal PFAS exposure with STL. Exploratory indirect-effect analyses further identified 12 metabolites with indirect-effect proportions ranging from 5.6% to 15.2%. Our findings provide novel insights into potential metabolic pathways linking PFAS exposure with sperm telomere biology and highlight the utility of untargeted metabolomics for generating hypotheses about potential biological mechanisms.

title: Enzymatic biotransformation of polystyrene: Interfacial oxidative modification by a serine hydrolase from Pseudomonas aeruginosa
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Indra Nyamjav, EunKyo Lee, Hong Rae Kim, Bong Hyun Sung, Dong-Eun Suh, Sukkyoo Lee
abstract: Polystyrene (PS) is highly resistant to biodegradation, and the enzymatic processes capable of initiating its environmental transformation remain poorly defined. This study investigates the previously underexplored association between a purified serine hydrolase (SH) from Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a bacterium isolated from the gut microbiome of PS-fed Zophobas atratus, and the early-stage oxidative modification of PS at the polymer–water interface. Under aqueous conditions, SH-treated high-molecular-weight PS films exhibited pronounced nanoscale surface alterations and progressive oxygen functionalization, as demonstrated by field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). These surface chemical changes were accompanied by a modest reduction in number-average molecular weight (M n) from 36.7 ± 0.5 kDa to 33.8 ± 0.2 kDa, while the weight-average molecular weight (M w) remained largely unchanged, indicating limited molecular weight reduction without extensive polymer depolymerization. AEBSF inhibition further supported the involvement of SH activity in the observed PS surface modification. Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) detected signals tentatively assigned to low-molecular-weight aromatic compounds, including oxygenated species, consistent with chemical transformation associated with SH treatment. Structural modeling and molecular docking suggested that SH adopts a conserved α/β-hydrolase fold with a surface-accessible aromatic binding cavity, potentially facilitating interactions with styrenic motifs at the polymer–water interface. Collectively, these findings reveal a novel association between SH activity and interfacial PS modification, highlighting enzyme-associated surface oxygenation as a potential early-stage process in plastic aging with implications for the environmental fate and potential chemical risks of persistent plastic pollutants.

title: Interfacial mechanisms governing the transport of bacteria in Yellow River sediments: Impact of antibiotic exposure and resistance phenotypes
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Shaojie Ren, Jia Yao, Yuanfang Wang, Mingyu Gao, Mengyao Li, Lin Gong, Ying Cao, Wei Zhang, Fengchang Wu
abstract: The environmental dissemination of antibiotic resistance is inextricably linked to microbial transport within natural porous media; however, the driving factors governing these processes remain elusive. Here, we systematically explored the transport behaviors of antibiotic resistant bacteria (ARB) and antibiotic susceptible bacteria (ASB) in Yellow River sediments (SS) under antibiotic stress. The rough surface and Fe/Al-rich composition of SS constitute robust physicochemical barriers that facilitate bacterial retention. By integrating breakthrough experiments with physiological assays, we demonstrated that bacterial transport in sediment is governed by a dynamic interplay between extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) mediated transport resistance and metabolically driven bacterial motility. Under ampicillin stress (corresponding resistance of ARB), ASB exhibited a higher intracellular ATP levels (reaching ∼3.0 RLU) that fuelled motility and transport. Whereas, ARB maintained transport stability through the coordinated regulation of EPS secretion (with relative EPS content rising to ∼2.52 RLU). Moreover, elevated levofloxacin (no corresponding resistance of ARB) stress induces the hypersecretion of EPS, thereby enhancing adhesion and effectively constraining transport. Our findings demonstrate that bacterial transport in complex sediments is dictated by the interplay between metabolically driven motility and interfacial retention, underscoring the critical need to integrate microbial metabolic states into predictive models of antimicrobial resistance dissemination.

title: Sequential reduction-oxidation degradation of alkaline nitrophenol wastewater by a novel Al 0 /O 2 system
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Haowen Xue, Ximiao Ma, Shiying Yang
abstract: Alkaline nitrophenol (NP) wastewater is highly toxic and resistant to direct oxidation. Although reductive treatment can enhance NP degradability, the alkaline environment complicates remediation, especially for zero-valent iron (Fe0) that readily undergoes passivation. To address these challenges, this study developed a sequential reduction-oxidation system employing carbon nanotube-modified micron-sized zero-valent aluminum (CNTs@mAl0) to activate O2 for p-nitrophenol (PNP) degradation under alkaline conditions. In the reduction stage, CNTs@mAl0 achieved complete conversion of PNP to p-aminophenol (PAP). Upon subsequent O2 sparging, the generated PAP underwent further oxidation and mineralization by •OH and 1O2 derived from O2 activation, achieving > 99.9% overall PNP removal and 66.1% TOC removal. Electrochemical analyses and material characterizations (SEM-EDS and XPS) revealed that CNTs not only act as conductive bridges to facilitate electron transfer in mAl0, but also facilitate O2 diffusion and activation through their high specific surface area, hydrophobic porous structure, and π*-electron-rich carbon framework, boosting reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and enhancing PAP mineralization. Notably, this method effectively removed 98.3% of diazodinitrophenol (DDNP) from real alkaline NP explosive wastewater, while also removing 49.5% TOC, confirming its practical efficacy. Overall, this study offers a promising strategy for the treatment of alkaline wastewater contaminated with refractory nitroaromatic pollutants.

title: Ti/RuO 2 -Ir-Ti 4 O 7 composite electrocatalytic membrane for PFOA removal and transformation: Cross-flow vs. dead-end operation, transformation pathways, and toxicogenomic response evolution
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Yi-fan Wang, Xiaoliang Li, Hao Xu, Heyun Yang, Qiansi Li, Yangtao Wang, Xiaolin Li, Hengtao Dong, Xin Jiang, Xing Zheng, Yu Zhu
abstract: Selecting anode materials is critical for electrocatalytic membrane treatment of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), affecting activity, stability, and mass transfer. Three Ti-based electrodes were screened to construct a composite electrocatalytic membrane (CEM) comprising a Ti substrate, RuO2-Ir interlayer, and Ti4O7 surface layer. The composite exhibited an oxygen evolution potential of 2.67 V, a charge-transfer resistance of 11.8 Ω, and 722 h accelerated lifetime. After optimization, C/C0 reached 0.34 and 0.03 after 3 h under dead-end and cross-flow modes, corresponding to approximately 66% and 97% parent-PFOA removal, respectively. Polarity reversal every 15 min improved removal by up to 19.34 percentage points over the control, suggesting partial alleviation of surface passivation. Differential radical-quenching experiments suggested the involvement of radical-associated oxidation, while substantial residual parent-PFOA removal after alcohol quenching suggested contributions from additional interfacial oxidation pathways. HRMS-detected transformation products were consistent with possible decarboxylation followed by progressive carbon-chain shortening, although multiple pathways may coexist in the CEM system. Because fluoride release and CO2 evolution were not quantified, defluorination and overall mineralization could not be determined. Toxicogenomic assessment showed that transcriptional stress decreased after 1 h and then increased, indicating that parent-PFOA removal did not correspond to a monotonic decrease in toxicogenomic response.

title: Gestational prednisone exposure causes subfertility in male offspring mice: Role of testicular E2f1 N6-methyladenosine modification
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Kai-Wen Wang, Wei Chang, Yong-Wei Xiong, Xin-Yue Wu, Hao Li, Zun-Yu Du, Lan-Lan Wu, Jin Zhang, Hua-Long Zhu, De-Xiang Xu, Hua Wang
abstract: Previous studies showed that abnormally high glucocorticoid exposure during pregnancy impaired fetal development and health. However, its impacts on fertility in adult male offspring and the underlying mechanisms remain unknown. Here, pregnant mice were treated intragastrically with prednisone (PDN), a widely used synthetic glucocorticoid and emerging environmental pollutant, from gestational day 0–17. Testicular development was traced in offspring. Sperm quality and male fertility were evaluated at adulthood. Results showed that gestational PDN exposure caused sperm count decline and subfertility in adult male offspring. Microarrays profile and subsequent experiments revealed that gestational PDN exposure inhibited spermatogonial proliferation in offspring. We identified the transcription factor E2f1, known to regulate cell proliferation, as being downregulated in the testes of PDN-exposed offspring. Additionally, testicular E2f1 N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification levels were also elevated in these offspring. Notably, these molecular changes persisted from the fetal period into adulthood. Moreover, both Mettl3 (the key m6A methyltransferase) knockdown and E2f1 overexpression alleviated the inhibited spermatogonial proliferation induced by prednisolone (the metabolite of PDN) in GC-1 cells. Finally, gestational supplementation with S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH, a m6A inhibitor) attenuated the PDN-evoked elevation of testicular E2f1 m6A in offspring. Expectedly, PDN-induced subfertility and spermatogonial proliferation suppression in male offspring were also ameliorated by gestational SAH supplementation. These results suggest that gestational PDN exposure causes spermatogonial proliferation inhibition and subfertility via elevating testicular E2f1 m6A in male offspring. Our research provides a warning and basis for further attention regarding the potential environmental health risks associated with gestational PDN exposure in the future.

title: Iron oxide-mediated hydrolysis of phthalate and organophosphate esters under indoor-relevant temperature and humidity: Kinetics, molecular structure effects, and acidic product accumulation
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Xiaopeng Ren, Lijie Wang, Weijian Zhang, Luying Nian, Ying Xu
abstract: Ester-containing semi-volatile organic compounds (SVOCs), including phthalates and organophosphate esters, are ubiquitous indoor pollutants, yet their transformation on reactive indoor surfaces remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the hydrolysis of representative phthalate and organophosphate esters on hematite, used as a model iron oxide surface, under indoor-relevant temperature and relative humidity (RH) conditions. Controlled hydrolysis experiments showed that these compounds underwent hematite-mediated hydrolysis, with apparent kinetics governed by RH, temperature, and molecular structure. Increasing RH markedly suppressed apparent hydrolysis of alkyl-substituted esters, whereas phenyl-containing esters exhibited faster hydrolysis and weaker RH dependence. Molecular dynamics simulations of interfacial partitioning supported a water-film accessibility mechanism, whereby thicker water films restricted ester–surface contact and inhibited hydrolysis. For phenyl-containing esters, the weaker RH dependence was associated with structure-dependent chemical and interfacial effects, including the greater leaving-group ability of phenoxy groups and compound-specific surface accessibility. Accelerated gas-phase exposure experiments further showed that dimethyl phthalate supplied through gas-phase adsorption could undergo hydrolysis on hematite and chemically complex iron-rich surfaces, including aged corrosion materials. These findings identify hematite and iron oxide-rich surfaces as reactive indoor interfaces that may transform phthalate and organophosphate ester SVOCs, promote acidic product accumulation, and potentially alter their surface retention and indoor fate. Because the apparent kinetics were determined under a nominal surface loading selected for reliable quantification, they are best interpreted as RH-, temperature-, and structure-dependent trends under the present experimental conditions, warranting future quantification under realistic indoor surface loadings and broader surface conditions.

title: Kinetics and mechanism of DBT degradation during chlorination and natural solar photochlorination
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Junji Chen, Rundong Chen, Hong Gao, Zhigang Wang, Cheng Zeng, Jia Yuan, Jianjun Liu, Rong Chen
abstract: Diethylhexyl butamido triazone (DBT), an emerging triazine-based ultraviolet filter widely employed in personal care products, is inevitably exposed to both solar irradiation and free chlorine in water. However, studies on its chlorination behavior remain limited. This first systematic investigation demonstrates that DBT exhibits high stability under chlorination in swimming pool water, yet undergoes rapid degradation under photochlorination. Moreover, the experimental batches were conducted over a period of seven-month under natural ambient weather conditions, providing robust evidence that photochlorination serves as a persistent and effective attenuation mechanism for DBT across a range of natural UV regimes, including those encountered in swimming pool water and real seawater. The water matrix exerts a dual and complex influence, simultaneously promoting and inhibiting DBT transformation, depending on the specific constituents present. Reactive chlorine species (RCS) and hydroxyl radicals (•OH) were identified as the dominant reactive species during photochlorination. The chlorination of DBT proceeds predominantly via electrophilic aromatic substitution, yielding mono-, di-, and tri-chlorinated derivatives. In contrast, photochlorination triggers a broader spectrum of reaction pathways, including chlorination, hydroxylation, carbon-nitrogen bond cleavage, and formation of chlorinated cleavage products. Acute toxicity assessment indicates that photochlorination transformation products are generally less toxic than those generated by chlorination.

title: Trophic transfer characteristics of mercury affected by food source in coral reef fish from the South China Sea
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Zhenwei Sun, Min Pang, Chang Sun, Jilin Liang, Yuanchao Li, Penggong Wang, Qing Guo, Yating Sun, Xuli Ma, Zongling Wang, Xuelei Zhang, Pei Qu
abstract: Mercury (Hg), particularly neurotoxic methylmercury (MeHg), persists globally and bioaccumulates in marine food webs. Hg biomagnification and ecological risks remain poorly characterized for the offshore oligotrophic Nansha Islands coral reef system with low background Hg. We measured total Hg (THg) and MeHg concentrations, plus carbon and nitrogen stable isotopes, in 144 coral reef fish from 41 species. Using proportional contributions of four basal food sources, namely organic matter from predominantly autotrophic corals (PACs), predominantly heterotrophic corals (PHCs), algae and plankton, we evaluated Hg trophic transfer in this system. Trophic magnification factors were 5.88 for THg and 6.76 for MeHg, much higher than those reported for nearshore ecosystems in China. Higher Hg biomagnification was associated with larger dietary fractions of coral-derived organic matter (OMC, including PACs and PHCs), indicating basal food-source heterogeneity modulates Hg trophic transfer. MeHg target hazard quotient (THQ) in some high-trophic-level fish exceeded safety thresholds, and 47.2% of samples presented THQ > 1, with particular risks for children. Even in minimally disturbed offshore waters with low background Hg levels, intense Hg biomagnification may lead to substantial health risks. Basal food-source composition is associated with Hg biomagnification, providing a reference for sustainable fishery governance and seafood consumption recommendations.

title: Impacts of microplastics on the nitrogen transformation in hyporheic zones with different grain sizes
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Zhenhua Yan, Xi Chen, Tao Zhang, Shiqi Liu, Yufang Chen, Chengying Zhang, Ping Lu, Saiyu Yuan, Jue Ding, Guanghua Lu
abstract: Hyporheic zones (HZs) play a pivotal role in nitrogen transformation and serve as reservoirs for microplastics (MPs) in rivers. While the effects of MPs on nitrogen transformation have gained wide attention, their general patterns and mechanisms remain poorly understood in natural environments. Here, we compared the effects of non-biodegradable polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and biodegradable polylactic acid (PLA) MPs on inorganic nitrogen transformation in simulated HZs with sediments of different grain sizes under water exchange. The results showed that exposure to PVC MPs had little effect on inorganic nitrogen in the HZs with mixed sediments, whereas PLA markedly decreased nitrate. Within the PLA treatment, fine-grained sediment decreased nitrate by 84.6% and increased nitrite by 90.7% compared with the mixed-grain condition, accompanied by oxygen-deficient conditions. Microbial community composition and nitrogen-related functional responses also differed across sediment grain size conditions. In the PVC treatment, fine-grained sediment enhanced AMO, NAR, and NIR activities and showed higher abundances of nitrification- and denitrification-related functional genes. A similar grain size response was observed in the PLA treatment. Hence, PVC and PLA produced distinct nitrogen transformation responses across sediment grain size conditions, accompanied by differences in oxygen dynamics, microbial community composition, enzymatic activities, and functional gene abundances.

title: Native-state monitoring of nanoplastic corona dynamics and their mitigating role in ecotoxicity using an integrated hollow fiber flow field-flow fractionation platform
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Xinyi Wu, Hongwei Liu, Zhengchang Xing, Yan Li, Xuan Zhao, Xiaodong Wen, Bin Liang, Yongguang Yin, Gang Li, Shixiang Gao, Maoyong Song, Zhiqiang Tan, Yan Ma, Baoshan Xing
abstract: Upon entering environmental systems, nanoplastics (NPs) adsorb natural organic matter, forming eco-coronas that dictate their ecotoxicological fate. However, conventional isolation alters fragile corona structures, and unseparated free biomolecules confound toxicity assessments, making native-state characterization challenging. To overcome this, we developed an integrated platform coupling hollow fiber flow field-flow fractionation with UV-Vis and point-discharge optical emission spectrometry (HF5-UV/PD-OES). This gentle separation isolated intact corona-coated polystyrene NPs (PSNPs) while eliminating free-molecule interference. Tracking native-state temporal dynamics of bovine serum albumin (BSA) and fulvic acid (FA) coronas revealed a three-stage evolution: rapid adsorption, structural reorganization, and dynamic equilibrium. Governed by surface curvature, 100 nm PSNPs accommodated significantly thicker coronas than highly curved 50 nm counterparts. A hybrid CNN-BiLSTM deep-learning model decoded PD-OES spectral fingerprints, accurately discriminating pristine, BSA-coated, and FA-coated PSNPs (98.67% accuracy). Using these highly purified fractions, ecotoxicological assays on Tetrahymena thermophila provided unconfounded evidence that the corona acts as a protective interfacial shield. While effectively mitigating acute oxidative stress and lethality, internalized particles continue to impose a persistent sub-lethal physical burden on cells. This study offers a robust tool for probing NP surface transformations and proves the corona decisively modulates toxicity in ecological risk assessments.

title: Nitrate transformation enables selective Fe–As decoupling from iron tailings through pyrrolic-N-associated electron transfer
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Zhuoye Lu, Haojie Liang, Jingyi Liu, Liulong Cheng, Chuanhao Li, Runliang Zhu, Qingze Chen, Yunfei Xi, Jun Yao, Zhuobiao Ni, Yue Wang, Yongjun Guo, Yanping Zhu, Rongliang Qiu
abstract: Strong iron–arsenic (Fe–As) coupling in iron tailings hinders selective As separation during Fe recovery, posing risks of secondary contamination and limiting tailings valorization. This study developed a nitrate–biomass hydrothermal treatment that enables selective Fe–As decoupling from iron tailings through pH evolution and As(V) reduction. The proposed strategy achieved ∼90% Fe recovery in the solid phase for valorization and ∼90% As separation to the liquid phase for safe management. During hydrothermal treatment, nitrate reduction induced pH rebound, which promoted Fe recovery. Notably, nitrate addition markedly enhanced the electron-donating capacity of the hydrothermal system, resulting in a six-fold increase in As(V) reduction efficiency. The reduction of As(V) weakened the association between As and Fe-bearing phases, thereby promoting Fe–As separation. Nitrogen transformation analysis indicated that nitrate participated in the formation of pyrrolic-N structures within hydrochar through interactions with biomass-derived intermediates. Combined experimental evidence and density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggested that pyrrolic-N contributed to As(V) reduction by enhancing electron transfer from carbon matrices to As(V) and lowering the energy requirement for reduction. Overall, this study establishes a nitrate-driven electron transfer system for selective Fe–As decoupling, providing mechanistic insights into nitrogen-mediated reductive transformation and a sustainable strategy for resource recovery from complex solid wastes.

title: Dry-wet cycling accelerates environmental transformation of emerging tungsten dust: Predictions from an atomistically based oxidation-dissolution kinetic model
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Yuxuan Wang, Haoyang Wu, Baojie Nie, Jia Song, Wentao Zhou, Dezhong Wang
abstract: Tungsten dust from mining, military, industrial, and fusion-related sources combines a high specific surface area with repeated environmental wetting. Yet the kinetic link between oxidation, dissolution, and soluble tungstate release remains poorly constrained. Here, we develop a cross-scale coupled oxidation-dissolution model by integrating density functional theory, reactive molecular dynamics, and particle-scale rate coupling. Calculations and sensitivity analysis show that oxide growth is predominantly controlled by oxygen transport through the WO3 layer, leading to self-limiting oxidation. The oxidation model reproduces experimental from 25 to 800 °C with R log 2 = 0.9789 and NRMSE = 3.97%. At the WO3-water interface, W release proceeds through hydration-assisted W-O bond weakening, water backfilling, and stabilization of solvated W species, with an effective barrier of 1.262 eV. The dissolution model captures non-calibration experimental data across pH, temperature, initial dust diameter, and exposure time with R log 2 = 0.8939 and NRMSE = 11.38%. Climate simulations show that precipitation pattern rather than temperature alone controls source release, with humid subtropical dry-wet cycling producing the highest normalized tungstate release. These results show that repeated oxide growth and removal can shift deposited tungsten dust from a particulate reservoir to a source of aqueous tungstate release.

title: From single- to binary-sorbate systems: Zeolite selectivity for Cs + and Sr 2+ in Na + - and Ca 2+ -rich waters
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Yoojin Cheon, Sookyung Kim, Hoon Young Jeong
abstract: This study investigated Cs+ and Sr2+ sorption—individually and in binary mixtures—by aluminous (4A and 13X) and siliceous (SSZ-13 and MOR) zeolites across Na+ and Ca2+ backgrounds, using kinetic modeling, extended Langmuir isotherms, multivariable regression, and SEM-EDS/XRD analyses. In single-sorbate systems, siliceous zeolites achieved superior Cs+ removal via accessible 8-membered-ring (8MR) sites accommodating partially dehydrated Cs+, while aluminous zeolites preferentially removed Sr2+ through high-charge-density sites, though Ca2+ competition sharply suppressed Sr2+ uptake. Unexpectedly, Ca2+ conditioning enhanced Sr2+ uptake by H+-form siliceous zeolites, requiring a modified Langmuir model incorporating a synergistic conditioning term. Regression identified accessible 8MR density and Si/Al ratio as principal descriptors governing Cs+ and Sr2+ distribution coefficients, respectively. In binary systems, co-sorbate effects were condition-dependent: Sr2+ strongly inhibited Cs+ uptake by aluminous zeolites in Na+ media but not in siliceous zeolites, whereas Cs+ produced framework-dependent inhibition or synergistic enhancement of Sr2+ uptake by 13X, SSZ-13, and MOR, likely reflecting steric relief from displacement of bulkier hydrated cations. A 4A–SSZ-13 composite achieved simultaneous Cs+/Sr2+ removal in sodic waters, though pure 4 A was preferable in Ca2+-rich waters. These results establish a mechanistic and practical framework for selecting zeolite sorbents according to contaminant mixtures and water chemistry in nuclear waste remediation.

title: Microplastic degradation and organic acids recovery via homogeneous catalytic wet air oxidation: Role of redox and Lewis acidity of metal ions
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Xing Luo, Chenchen Zhao, Yanchanjuan Yang, Yuanyuan Liu, Shuaiqi Zhao, Huangzhao Wei, Aihua Xu, Xiaoxia Li, Xiuying Liu
abstract: The pervasive accumulation of microplastics (MPs) in aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems poses a growing threat to environmental and human health, yet current advanced oxidation technologies are constrained by inefficiency or reliance on excess oxidants. Here, a homogeneous catalytic wet air oxidation (CWAO) system using Cu2 + ions was developed to degrade polyethylene (PE) MPs and simultaneously recover value-added carboxylic acids. The system enables 98.7% weight loss of PE (1.0 g/L) and a liquid-phase total organic carbon of 489 mg/L at 170 °C, substantially outperforming non-catalytic WAO. About 57.1% of the PE carbon is transformed into carboxylic acid species, with a total dicarboxylic acid concentration reaching 186.9 mg/L. The catalyst functions through a synergistic dual-mechanism pathway, consisting of a Cu2+/Cu+ redox cycle that activates O2 to generate •OH radicals for C-C bond scission, and Lewis acidity that polarizes C-H and C-C bonds to lower the activation energy for oxidative cleavage, which enables controlled polymer chain scission and stepwise oxidation, including hydroxylation, carbonylation, and carboxylation. The system also exhibits applicability to other MPs or real-world PE-rich plastic waste, with more than 97.7% weight loss. This work establishes CWAO as a promising route that integrates environmental remediation with resource recovery for MPs treatment.

title: Hydrodynamic regulation drives azo dye transformation and hydrolysis acidification by reshaping microbial metabolism in the micro-aerobic hydrolysis acidification reactor
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Jiayao Hui, Jiehui Ren, Xiaoxin Yang, Ziyi Jia, Yong Zhang, Tian Wan, Min Wang, Wen Cheng
abstract: Acid Red GR is a representative sulfonated azo dye frequently detected in dyeing wastewater, yet the role of hydrodynamic conditions in regulating its biodegradation in micro-aerobic hydrolysis acidification (MAHA) systems remains unclear. This study investigated how hydrodynamic conditions drive Acid Red GR transformation, hydrolysis acidification, and microbial metabolic responses in the MAHA reactor. The results showed that a moderate stirring speed of 120 rad/min (R2) balanced turbulence intensity and flow uniformity, with relatively high oxygen transfer, a favorable micro-aerobic niche, and the highest biodegradability (0.50) and volatile fatty acid (VFA) production (140.38 mg/L). This hydrodynamic condition enriched hydrolytic, facultative, and fermentative genera, including Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Bacteroides, Propionivibrio, and Bacillus, and was associated with higher abundances of genes encoding enzymes involved in azo reduction, aromatic intermediate transformation, pyruvate generation, and acidogenic metabolism. Integrated metagenomic, metabolomic, and functional group evidence further indicated that Acid Red GR degradation proceeded through azo reduction, deamination, desulfonation, aromatic ring cleavage, and subsequent acidogenesis. These findings demonstrate that hydrodynamic optimization regulates MAHA performance by coordinating oxygen transfer, microbial niche formation, and metabolic functional potential, providing a mechanistic basis for enhancing the biodegradability and treatment efficiency of dyeing wastewater.

title: Au@Pt NCs nanozyme-based multichannel sensor array coupled with smartphone for selective identification and on-site detection of imidacloprid
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Xuran Fu, Yongmei Ji, Zexun Zhang, Wanmei Chen, Jijuan Cao, Jian Ji, Jiadi Sun
abstract: As a widely applied neonicotinoid insecticide, imidacloprid (IMI) necessitates portable residue monitoring to ensure food safety. Herein, a multichannel colorimetric sensor array was developed for selective IMI identification and quantification, employing Au@Pt nanoclusters (Au@Pt NCs) as the sole nanozyme sensing receptor. Rather than introducing multiple sensing materials, the proposed strategy extracts three characteristic absorption responses at 370, 450, and 652 nm from a single Au@Pt NCs-catalyzed TMB-H₂O₂ reaction to generate multidimensional cross-reactive fingerprints. The Au@Pt NCs provided sufficient peroxidase-like catalytic activity for signal generation, enabling five representative pesticides, including IMI and its structural analogues, to be successfully discriminated. Linear discriminant analysis achieved 100% classification accuracy as confirmed by cross-validation, while hierarchical cluster analysis further demonstrated clear clustering among the different pesticide groups. Moreover, capitalizing on the pronounced inhibitory effect of IMI on the nanozyme catalytic activity, a dual-mode detection platform integrating colorimetry with smartphone-based readout was established for IMI quantification. Under optimized experimental parameters, the limits of detection were 0.112 µg/L for the colorimetric mode and 1.236 µg/L for the smartphone-assisted approach. By converting the Au@Pt NCs mediated catalytic reaction into multidimensional analytical information, this work provides an affordable, portable, and practical strategy for pesticide discrimination and on-site IMI monitoring.

title: Determination of perfluorobutane sulfonyl fluoride in environmental water and soil using a novel quaternary ammonium derivatization LC-MS/MS method
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 517 Author(s): Junchen Zhu, Ruochen Zhang, Xinyi Shao, Siwei Rao, Ning Han, Yuanjiang Pan, Cuirong Sun
abstract: Although current derivatization methods have enabled the detection of perfluorooctane sulfonyl fluoride (PFOSF) and perfluorohexane sulfonyl fluoride (PFHxSF), the analysis of their short-chain substitute, perfluorobutane sulfonyl fluoride (PFBSF), remains challenging despite its increasing production. This study developed a novel quaternary ammonium derivatization reagent and established a highly sensitive liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) method for the trace quantification of PFBSF in water and soil, while enabling the simultaneous determination of PFHxSF and PFOSF. Method validation demonstrated exceptional sensitivity, with method detection limits (MDLs) for PFBSF reaching 0.84 ng L−1 in water and 0.022 ng g−1 in soil. For PFHxSF and PFOSF, the MDLs ranged from 0.93 to 0.98 ng L−1 in water and 0.027–0.030 ng g−1 in soil. The method exhibited excellent linearity (R2 > 0.99 over 5–100 ng L−1), stable recoveries (71%–116%), and satisfactory specificity and stability.
